# Chio: The Spend Control Plane for Autonomous Agents
### The runaway-agent kill switch you can audit

## 1. Thesis

Fork Orca (the MIT cockpit for running fleets of parallel CLI coding agents) and fuse it with the Chio protocol to ship the one thing no agent runner and no payment rail has: out-of-agent, fail-closed spend enforcement plus a cryptographically replayable receipt for every dollar an agent was authorized to move and every dollar it actually did. We sell the brake and the audit trail, not a wallet. Concretely: a hard per-worktree and per-fan-out budget mandate that the kernel refuses to exceed before any money moves, terminating in a signed, offline-verifiable receipt a developer hands their client and a CISO hands their auditor. Chio never custodies or transmits funds (the code is custody-neutral and simulation-first by construction, which is both the legal shield and the honest scope), so a licensed rail moves money later if ever. The wedge lands with AI-native dev shops burning client API budgets today; it expands into the regulated enterprise that needs provable agent governance; and it earns the right, only after that installed base exists, to become the neutral cross-rail verifier and federated trust mesh the whole agent economy will route through.

## 2. Why now

The timing is asymmetric, and being honest about which half is real is the whole game.

- **The half that is NOT ready: agents transacting as an economy.** Agent-to-agent settlement over x402/ACP/AP2 is nascent. A "take-rate on the agent economy" business is basis points of a near-zero base in 2026, and a two-sided tool marketplace is a 2027+ cold-start with no supply and no demand on day one. Any plan underwritten on that volume is a narrative.
- **The half that IS acute right now: runaway spend and prove-what-we-billed.** Teams already run many CLI agents in parallel (Orca's actual product-market signal) and already bill compute and API spend to clients or controlled budgets. The cited "$47k runaway LangChain agent with dashboards but no kill-switch" is their lived nightmare. The entire market, across every grounding source, openly admits the same unfilled white space: **enforcement must live OUTSIDE agent code**, and **there is no accepted audit-trail standard for AI-generated logs** (code-based authorization trails are untested before courts and regulators). AP2, ACP, and x402 each define authorization and payment artifacts but explicitly do NOT revoke or refuse at execution time.
- **Why Chio specifically, why now.** That white space maps almost one-to-one onto what is already built and tested in this repo: a fail-closed kernel mediating every tool call, capability tokens, a Merkle receipt log, hierarchical budget enforcement, signed IOUs per receipt, an offline buyer-side verify path, and an axum control-plane sidecar. Orca is MIT, forkable, and ships the exact parallel-fan-out UX the budget primitive was built for. The fragmentation of the payment standards is itself a closing window: nobody yet owns the neutral verifier above all three, and the architectural position is incentive-incompatible for the rails to occupy themselves.

The move is to sell the brake and the audit trail into a market that is buying control THIS year, and treat settlement and marketplace as a later option we are positioned for but do not bet the company on.

## 3. What we fork and what we add

**We fork:** Orca (github.com/stablyai/orca, Lovecast Inc., MIT). An Electron 42 + React 19 + TypeScript cockpit (~5,120 files) that runs any CLI coding agent in its own git worktree, with parallel fan-out, Ghostty-class terminals, an embedded-Chromium Design Mode, and an Expo mobile companion. Four clean process seams make it an ideal host: the main/renderer IPC hub (`src/main/ipc/register-core-handlers.ts`), the token-authed Unix-socket terminal daemon (the precedent for a Rust sidecar), the public `orca` CLI JSON-RPC transport, and the agent-hooks bus (`src/main/agent-hooks/`) that fires on every agent tool call.

**We add (all verified in-tree), and we route through ONE new `commerce:*` IPC namespace plus `orca commerce ...` CLI verbs:**

- **The enforcement spine:** `chio-metering` (`BudgetEnforcer`, `BudgetTree` for org -> dept -> team -> agent caps), `chio-credit` (`CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy` kill switch; `CreditEvaluatorHook` minting signed IOUs), `chio-workflow-preflight` (`WorkflowBudgetPool` for fan-out), `chio-core-types` (`ChioReceipt`, `FinancialReceiptMetadata`).
- **The transport:** `chio-api-protect` (the finished axum control plane: `/chio/evaluate`, `/v1/capabilities/mint` and `/release`, `/approvals/*`) spawned as a bundled, token-authed sidecar exactly like Orca's terminal daemon. `chio-bindings-ffi` (pinned ABI v1, JSON in/out) via koffi for offline signature and hash checks on the read path only.
- **The proof surface:** the existing `chio-cli/dashboard` React/Vite components (`ReceiptTable`, `BudgetSparkline`, `DelegationChain`) ported into the renderer; `chio-cli` `cert.rs` (session compliance certificate); `chio-enterprise-export` and `chio-siem` for audit export and OCSF streaming.
- **The custody posture we keep as a product stance:** `chio-credit/capital_and_execution.rs` defaults (`external_execution_authoritative=false`, `custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true`, `simulation_first_only=true`). `chio-settle` (the EVM/web3 broadcast path) stays feature-gated and OFF.

**We add it correctly with a product-crate boundary:** a versioned `chio-orca` + `chio-orca-core` crate pair (mirroring the shipped `chio-mercury`/`chio-wall` template) holds 100% of Orca-specific Rust and the `commerce:*` schemas behind the public-entrypoint allowlist, so the Electron fork carries only brand strings, one `src/main/ipc/commerce.ts`, and the ported dashboard. This is what makes the daily-shipping upstream rebaseable instead of a treadmill.

## 4. The wedge

**First customer (land):** the 10-75 person **AI-native dev shop or product team running parallel CLI-agent fleets on client money.** The economic buyer is a head of engineering or a fractional controller. They feel two pains at once: an agent can torch the month's API budget in an afternoon, and they cannot prove to a client what was spent on what. The deal is a per-seat-plus-usage SaaS line approved this quarter, and the ICP is narrow enough to win by word of mouth in the Orca/Claude Code community.

**First use case:** a developer fans one prompt across N agents against a fixed budget pool, the agents run, and the fleet provably cannot exceed the pool; every run exports as a signed receipt for the client invoice.

**What we sell first:** the smallest valuable unit is **the per-prompt budget pool field on fan-out** plus a **hard per-worktree spend mandate**, with the **signed receipt per run** as the deliverable proof. That is the entire v1 pitch: *"Set a budget pool, fan a prompt across N agents, your agents physically cannot exceed it, and here is the signed receipt you give the client."*

**Expansion (land-and-expand into the real margin):** the CISO/CFO at a regulated enterprise (financial services, healthcare, regulated SaaS) moving agents from PoC to production, who buys the **compliance and audit-export license** because EU AI Act, ISO 42001, SOC 2, and PCI-DSS timelines are live and there is no audit-trail standard for AI logs.

## 6. The killer demo

**"The $47K Runaway, Stopped Mid-Keystroke, With a Receipt."** Ninety seconds, one screen, no money rail, nothing that depends on broadcasting a transaction. Provably true against shipped code.

1. The operator fans one prompt across five worktree-agents and sets "Budget pool: $50" in the launch dialog. The grid shows five cards, each with a remaining-slice chip. An attempt to spawn a sixth, over-allocated agent is **rejected at preflight** with the typed `workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded` error, before any agent runs.
2. The agents run. The repurposed usage panel is now a live spend bar climbing per metered tool call.
3. One agent, told to be aggressive, races toward its slice. At the ceiling, the kernel **denies the next paid call**. The agent's terminal split shows a typed `CreditBondedExecutionDecision::Deny` finding code; the spend bar stops. The money never moved, because enforcement is outside the agent, not in its prompt. The denial is a signed, replayable artifact, not a log line.
4. The operator opens the Attested Receipts tab. Every call is a line with `cost_charged`, an IOU id, and the stamped `policy_hash`. They click "Verify offline" on one; it re-verifies the signature with no running Chio node.
5. They merge the winning worktree. A "Session Certified" badge appears, and "Export Audit Package" downloads a signed bundle ready to hand an auditor.

The line: **every other cockpit shows you the spend; Chio refuses it, and hands you the receipt.**

**The demo we deliberately do NOT lead with:** "click-to-buy-the-API, settled on-chain in 30 seconds." The code is unambiguous: `chio-settle` is `#![cfg(feature = "web3")]`, its EVM entrypoints are all `prepare_*` (the `eth_sendTransaction` call sits inside `prepare_*`), and the credit layer is `simulation_first_only=true`. Nothing in-tree broadcasts. Leading with a live-money demo invites a credibility-destroying "it does not actually settle" discovery and drags us across the money-transmitter line. We keep the on-chain escrow loop as a feature-flagged, internal, testnet-only proof of the rail-neutral story, never the headline and never a revenue dependency.

## 7. Business model

**We price as governance and security software, never as a payments take-rate.** The unit economics must not depend on agent-to-agent settlement volume existing.

- **Per-seat + usage SaaS (land):** priced per worktree-seat and per attested run, billed straight out of `chio-metering` `BillingExport`/`CostQuery`, which is value-neutral. The invoice is itself derived from signed receipts, so it is provable, a thing no other cockpit can claim.
- **Enterprise compliance and audit-export license (expand, the real margin):** a flat license for the offline-verifiable, clause-mapped evidence package, SIEM streaming, and continuous tamper-evidence monitoring. This is the SKU a regulated buyer actually has budget for in 2026, and it touches no money so it triggers no money-transmission analysis.
- **Bonded-autonomy and higher-tier features (future upsell):** higher unattended-autonomy tiers gated by a posted bond and an attested runtime tier (`CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy` + `chio-attest-verify`). A natural revenue ladder, but downstream of trust we have not yet earned.

**What we explicitly refuse to monetize:** a settlement take-rate. Skimming 30-50 bps while in the flow of funds is the single most license-triggering decision in the entire idea space (receiving compensation for directing the movement of value is the textbook definition of money transmission), and it contradicts the custody-neutral architecture that is our legal spine. If a percentage-of-value fee is ever commercially essential, it must be charged and remitted BY a licensed partner who pays Chio a flat technology or referral fee, with Chio never in control of, and never compensated as a function of, the movement of funds.

## 8. Competitive moat

Be honest about what is a wall versus a one-quarter bolt-on. The receipt format, the kill switch, the wallet, the dashboard, and a single-rail integration are each features an incumbent ships in a quarter, and several are shipping now. The durable moat is the **combination** of two things, neither of which any single-rail incumbent can occupy:

1. **Architectural neutrality plus out-of-agent enforcement.** Stripe (ACP), Coinbase (x402), Visa/Mastercard (Agentic Tokens), Google (AP2), and Skyfire (KYA) are each a single rail or SDK that runs INSIDE agent code. None can credibly verify a rival's rail without conceding it is not the universal rail, and none can put the kill switch OUTSIDE the agent because their SDK is the agent's library. An out-of-agent kernel that mediates every tool call with signed denials and verifies rivals' artifacts is an architecture they would have to rebuild from scratch and against their own incentive. Its value grows with every rail it does NOT own.
2. **A multi-operator federation mesh of signed registries with cross-operator trust gossip, plus accumulated kernel-signed reputation a fork cannot mint.** The MIT cockpit is copyable; the protocol crates are open. The only uncopyable asset is the live network and its history. `chio-federation` is verified to be the deepest part of the codebase (stake-gated open admission, pheromone and revocation gossip, bilateral co-signing, with extensive tests), and you cannot fork other operators' receipts. This is the actual wall, and it is a Year-3 asset that the wedge's installed base seeds.

The **custody-refusal stance** is the strongest moat that is true TODAY rather than contingent on a future network: it is verified in code (loopback-only settlement RPC, prepare-only EVM dispatch, `simulation_first_only=true`), and it is architectural and legal, not merely technical. Incumbents who took custody to win UX cannot un-take it without dismantling their product. The **offline-verifiable compliance export** is the most defensible enterprise moat because "hard to build" there genuinely equals "hard to compete against," and a payment rail is counter-incentivized to make its own logs independently re-verifiable by a third party.

The honest exposure: this moat is a standards-adoption and two-sided-network bet, and the rails own the distribution and the standards authorship needed to win it. We hedge by being the first and most complete cross-rail binder during the fragmentation window, and by leaning the near-term business on the compliance franchise, which is defensible even if the rails consolidate.

## 9. Top risks and how we design around them

**Risk 1 (disqualifying if unfixed): fan-out double-spend makes the headline claim false.** `BudgetEnforcer` is verified to be an in-memory, single-process, non-atomic `u64` (`total_spent`, `&mut self`, no `Arc`/`Mutex`). Across Orca's signature N-parallel-worktree fan-out, two worktrees checking the same pool concurrently both pass, so "physically cannot overspend" is untrue in exactly the topology the product runs in.
*Design-around:* the `chio-api-protect` sidecar is the SINGLE authoritative reservation service with atomic reserve-then-charge against a durable, concurrency-safe ledger. Every paid call must obtain a scoped capability via atomic mint before execution; per-worktree enforcers are advisory caches only. The `WorkflowBudgetPool` preflight validates allocation but must be backed by atomic mint at call time. This is the first hard engineering milestone, and we do not ship the kill-switch claim until no-double-spend is demonstrated under concurrent fan-out.

**Risk 2 (disqualifying if unfixed): approval is opt-in at the type level (mandate-bypass).** `ApprovalRequest.approval_token` is verified to be `Option<GovernedApprovalToken>`. With an untrusted LLM authoring tool-call requests and a prompt-injection adversary, any path that treats missing-approval as proceed-without-approval defeats the gate.
*Design-around:* invert to fail-closed-by-construction. Any governed or over-threshold intent with no valid `ApprovalToken` DENIES, never proceeds. Bind every approval to `execution_nonce` (already shipped) over the full economic envelope (amount, counterparty, currency, resource), so an approval for call A cannot authorize call B and an injected purchase cannot substitute a malicious payee after a benign approval.

**Risk 3: the fork treadmill and a mid-refactor substrate drown a small team.** Orca ships daily across ~5,120 files, and the commerce crates are mid-extraction out of `chio-control-plane` in the uncommitted working tree.
*Design-around:* land the extraction and build the `chio-orca` + `chio-orca-core` product crate FIRST so the Electron fork carries only brand strings, one IPC file, and ported dashboard components. Pin to an Orca tag, rebase weekly, and isolate all rename churn into a scripted, re-runnable brand codemod so a rebase is "re-apply patch," not "resolve 200 conflicts." Assert `CHIO_FFI_ABI_VERSION` and a sidecar `/version` handshake at startup so any drift fails closed. Retain the Lovecast Inc. MIT notice in every kept file, add Chio copyright only to net-new files, drop the `Orca`/`Stably` marks and the `com.stablyai.orca` appId, and run a "Chio" wordmark clearance search before public launch.

**Risk 4: the marketed differentiator is thinner than the marketed depth.** The cross-rail binding (`chio-commerce-order`) is verified to be three hashed mandate fields in a fixed state machine with few tests, and it verifies an already-assembled bundle rather than orchestrating a live order. A competent incumbent replicates "we hash your AP2 mandate and ACP token" in a quarter.
*Design-around:* do not sell the cross-rail verifier as the v1 wedge. Sell the brake and the receipt, where the depth (the kernel, the budget tree, the signed IOU, the federation layer) is real. Make deepening the verifier into a true cryptographic check of the underlying mandate documents the explicit Year-2 job, and anchor durable defensibility in the federation mesh and the compliance export, not the hash binding.

**Risk 5: no AML/sanctions/KYC primitive exists, and we deliberately do not build one.** A case-insensitive search across all crate sources returns zero hits; the "KYA credential" is a reputation tier, not legal-entity binding or sanctions screening.
*Design-around:* this is a non-issue precisely because v1 moves no money. We refuse custody, escrow, peer settlement, and any real-value rail in v1, which removes the entire AML surface. If a money rail is ever added, sanctions/Travel-Rule screening becomes a fail-closed kernel guard at mint AND settle, and KYC is carried by a licensed issuer who holds the BSA/CIP obligation; Chio is strictly the relying party that verifies and pins the issuer.

**Risk 6: demand is asserted from one anecdote.** One viral incident is a hook, not a market.
*Design-around:* sign 2-3 named design-partner agencies running fleets on real client budget who will pay for the budget pool plus receipts BEFORE scaling spend. If they will not pay, the "now" thesis is unproven regardless of how good the Rust is.

## 10. Phased roadmap

**Phase 0 - First 90 days: ship the brake and the receipt to paying design partners.**
- *Weeks 1-3:* land the `chio-control-plane` commerce-crate extraction; create `chio-orca` + `chio-orca-core` behind the public-entrypoint allowlist (defining `commerce:*` schemas and the worktree-to-`WorkflowBudgetPool` mapping). Build the minimum `chio commerce` CLI (`budget set`, `run-with-cap`, `receipt export`, `cert generate`), which does not exist today.
- *Weeks 3-6 (the gating milestone):* stand up the sidecar as the single authoritative, atomic, durable reserve-then-charge ledger (Risk 1) and invert approval to fail-closed (Risk 2). Demonstrate no double-spend under concurrent fan-out before any UI polish.
- *Weeks 6-9:* fork Orca at a pinned tag with the scripted brand codemod; spawn the sidecar behind one `src/main/ipc/commerce.ts`; wire the agent-hooks bus to the allow/deny gate; ship features 1, 2, 4; port the dashboard (feature 6).
- *Weeks 9-12:* ship features 3 and 5; build and code-sign/notarize the slim sidecar and FFI binary per platform (plan CI around the `lto=fat` workspace); cut the 90-second demo; convert 2-3 design partners to paid seats.
- *Finish line:* a forked, rebranded cockpit where an agency sets a budget pool, fans a prompt across N agents, the kernel provably refuses overspend, and every run exports as a signed, offline-verifiable receipt, with at least one paying design partner.

**Phase 1 - V1 (months 4-9): become the enterprise audit-and-enforcement plane.**
- Ship the compliance franchise: one-click regulator evidence package (feature 7), OCSF SIEM streaming (feature 8), policy-as-code spend governor with `policy_hash` stamped into receipts, and continuous Merkle-checkpoint tamper-evidence monitoring that alerts the SOC and freezes export on a broken root.
- Add the mobile Secure-Enclave phone-tap mandate (feature 9) as the human circuit-breaker for high-value spend.
- Land the CISO/CFO ICP on the audit-export license. Expand the budget primitives to the hierarchical `BudgetTree` for org-wide governance.

**Phase 2 - Platform (year 2-3): become the neutral verifier, then the mesh.**
- *Year 2 (the neutrality land-grab):* deepen the Rail-Neutral Receipt (feature 10) into a true cross-rail cryptographic verifier of ACP + AP2 + x402, joining the `chio-agent-web-interop` adapters to the order replay. Be the audit-and-enforcement plane every rail integration flows through while the standards are still fragmented.
- *Year 3 (the mesh and, only now, the marketplace):* seed independent operators into a federation of signed registries with cross-operator trust gossip and portable reputation (`chio-federation`, `chio-proof-room`). The bonded, slashable agent-to-agent marketplace ships here and ONLY here, because by now the installed base of governed agents needs somewhere to transact, so the two-sided cold-start is solved by demand the brake created. If a money rail is ever turned on, it is a regulated-operator add-on routed entirely through a licensed partner, with sanctions screening as a fail-closed kernel guard.

## 11. Naming and narrative

- **Product name:** Chio. **Category:** the spend control plane for autonomous agents.
- **Primary tagline:** *No receipt, no spend.* (The receipt, not the payment, is the hero object.)
- **The wedge line:** *Every other cockpit shows you the spend. Chio refuses it.*
- **The contrarian framing that is also the safest:** *We sell the NO.* The whole market builds rails that let agents spend faster; the defensible product is the signed, court-admissible proof that an agent was structurally prevented from overspending, over-disclosing, or over-reaching, and was provably more conservative than a human would have been. Where the catalog wants flourish, brand the artifact a "Restraint Receipt."
- **The enterprise line:** *Provably bounded. Mandate-gated. Exportable for your auditor.*
- **The custody stance as a feature, not a footnote:** *Chio never holds your money.* (Architectural and legal, verified in code.)
- **Dual-audience glossary, one true word:** to a developer Chio means "capability-gated agent cockpit"; to a CFO it means "every agent spend is mandated and attested." Same binary, two landing pages, both true because the same key the kernel meters is the key that would pay, and the kill switch is a real `CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy` field.
- **The autonomy dial named from the real enum:** Shadow -> Advisory -> Active (from `chio-autonomy`), backed by signed advisory-versus-active decision artifacts, not UI sugar.

## 12. Open questions for the human

# Chio: The Settlement and Trust Layer for the Autonomous Agent Economy
## A category-defining platform brief (2-3 year arc)

## 1. One-line thesis

**Every payment rail is racing to let agents spend; nobody owns the neutral layer that proves an agent was allowed to, bounded the spend, and recorded what happened. Chio is that layer - the out-of-agent kernel plus the federated trust mesh that sits ABOVE ACP, AP2, and x402, and over three years becomes the clearinghouse the entire agent economy routes through.**

We are not building a wallet. We are building the place where agent commerce is verified, governed, and settled - and the network of operators whose signed receipts no single rail can fork.

## 2. Why this is a platform and not a feature

The category insight, drawn straight from the market: the payment standards (ACP/AP2/x402) are fragmenting into complementary layers and explicitly punt on three things - runtime enforcement, tamper-evident audit, and cross-rail neutrality. Those three gaps are not a feature gap; they are an entire missing layer of the stack. Whoever fills it becomes infrastructure, because:

- **It is incentive-incompatible for the rails.** Coinbase (x402), Google (AP2), and OpenAI/Stripe (ACP) each want attestation to live on THEIR rail. None can credibly verify a rival's rail without conceding it is not the universal one. A neutral verifier's value *grows with every rail it does not own*. That is the textbook structural position of a platform, not a product.
- **The moat compounds off-app, not in-app.** The forked cockpit is MIT and copyable. The durable asset is the multi-operator federation mesh (chio-federation: 147 tests, stake-gated open admission, pheromone and revocation gossip) plus the accumulated kernel-signed reputation history. You cannot fork other operators' receipts. Network effects accrue to the mesh.
- **The substrate already exists.** This is the rare platform bet where the hard Rust (107 crates, a fail-closed kernel, capability tokens, Merkle receipt log, a tested federation layer, custody-neutral capital instructions) is largely built. The platform risk is go-to-market and network seeding, not core invention.

The 2-3 year arc, stated plainly:

- **Year 1 - The Brake (wedge + proof).** Own "agent spend you can prove is bounded." Single-operator. Sell control and audit to dev shops and CISOs. Ship the receipt as the hero artifact.
- **Year 2 - The Verifier (neutrality land-grab).** Become the rail-neutral receipt that binds ACP + AP2 + x402 into one signed chain. Be the audit-and-enforcement plane every rail integration flows through while the standards are still fragmented. This window is open and closing.
- **Year 3 - The Mesh (clearinghouse + marketplace).** Turn verifier adoption into a federation of operators with portable reputation, bonded marketplaces, and revenue-split settlement. Now the marketplace has both sides because the installed base of governed agents needs somewhere to transact. The standard is set because everyone already routes through Chio to verify.

You do not get to Year 3 by building the marketplace in Year 1. You get there by owning the brake, then the verifier, then letting the mesh become inevitable.

## 3. The wedge and first customer

**Wedge: "The runaway-agent kill switch you can audit."** The single sellable unit is the kernel-enforced per-worktree spend cap plus a per-prompt fan-out budget pool, with a signed receipt per run as the deliverable proof.

Decisiveness here is the difference between a platform and a 60-feature death march.

No settlement take-rate.** The take-rate-on-every-settlement business model is the single most license-triggering decision in the entire idea space - receiving a cut while directing the flow of funds is money transmission. We adopt the code's existing posture as a hard product stance: `external_execution_authoritative=false`, `custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true`. Chio emits signed instructions and proofs; a licensed partner moves money. - **No "live order engine."** chio-commerce-order *verifies* an assembled bundle; it does not orchestrate an order forward, reserve budget, call a PSP, and advance states in real time. - **No spend decision on the FFI hot path.** chio-bindings-ffi exports only stateless verify/sign/hash. Budget enforcement, minting, and the kill switch are stateful and live behind the sidecar. We use FFI for fast local signature/expiry/canonicalization checks on the read path only, and we drop the "sub-millisecond zero-IPC kill switch" claim entirely. # Chio: The Attested Spend Control Plane for Autonomous Agents

## One-line thesis

Chio is the cockpit where every dollar an AI agent spends is policy-gated before it moves and cryptographically provable after it does, so a CFO can set hard spend mandates and a CISO can hand an auditor an offline-verifiable receipt for everything the fleet bought. We sell the brake and the audit trail, not a wallet.

## The wedge and first customer

**Wedge:** Out-of-agent, fail-closed spend enforcement plus tamper-evident receipts for teams running fleets of parallel CLI coding agents. Every other cockpit (including Orca itself) only reads provider token quota; none can refuse the next paid tool call, and none emits a signed, replayable record of what an agent was authorized to do versus what it did.

**First customer (land):** The 10-75 person AI-native dev shop or product team that runs many CLI agents in parallel and bills compute and API spend back to clients or to a controlled internal budget. They feel two pains at once: an agent can burn the month's API budget in an afternoon, and they cannot prove to a client or finance what was spent on what. The economic buyer is a head of engineering or a fractional CFO/controller; the deal is a per-seat plus usage SaaS line approved this quarter.

**Expansion (land-and-expand into the real ICP):** The CISO/CFO at a regulated enterprise (financial services, healthcare, regulated SaaS) moving agents from PoC to production who needs EU AI Act / ISO 42001 / SOC 2 / PCI-DSS-grade evidence that autonomous agents stayed inside an authorized boundary. They buy the enterprise compliance and audit-export license.

We deliberately do not target a payments TAM. Chio is governance, control, and audit software for agent spend. It is priced like security tooling, not like a payment rail.

## Top features

Each is tied to a verified Chio crate and a concrete Orca surface. All of these ride the non-custodial, simulation-first posture (`external_execution_authoritative=false`, `custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true`): Chio governs and proves, a licensed rail (later, optional) moves money.

### 1. Hard per-worktree spend mandate that fails the next call closed
The control that no agent runner has. A signed spend cap per worktree and per agent; when a metered tool call would breach it, the kernel denies the call instead of a dashboard merely warning.
- **Crates:** `chio-metering` (`BudgetEnforcer`/`BudgetPolicy`, `budget_hierarchy::BudgetTree` for org -> dept -> team -> agent caps), `chio-credit` (`CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy` kill switch).
- **Orca surface:** A "Spend mandate" control grafted onto the existing rate-limits/usage panel (`src/main/rate-limits`); the agent-hooks bus (`src/main/agent-hooks`) calls the bundled sidecar for an allow/deny before each tool call; an exceeded cap surfaces a typed `BudgetViolation` and pauses the worktree.
- **Critical correctness note:** enforcement must route through a single authoritative reservation service (the sidecar), not per-process in-memory enforcers, or parallel worktrees double-spend. This is a must-fix, not a nice-to-have.

### 2. Per-prompt fan-out budget pool (the smallest sellable unit)
When a user fans one prompt across N agents, all N draw capped slices of one signed pool and over-allocation is rejected before any agent runs. This maps one-to-one onto Orca's signature fan-out UX.
- **Crates:** `chio-workflow-preflight` (`WorkflowBudgetPool`, `WorkflowPreflightPlan`, `workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded` validation), `chio-core-types` (`budget_share_bps` on `CapabilityToken`).
- **Orca surface:** A "Budget pool" field in the fan-out launch dialog (`src/cli/handlers/orchestration` and the parallel-worktrees UI), with a shared-pool gauge above the worktree grid and a per-worktree remaining-slice chip.

### 3. Signed receipt and IOU per paid call, replayable in the review pane
Every metered call mints a signed IOU bound to the receipt and its policy and content hashes, rendered as an attestable line item a human or auditor can verify offline. This is the proof artifact that makes the wedge a compliance product.
- **Crates:** `chio-credit` (`CreditEvaluatorHook` minting `chio.credit.iou-envelope.v1`, binding amount and currency to `receipt_id` + content/policy hashes; zero-price skips), `chio-core-types` (`ChioReceipt`, `FinancialReceiptMetadata`: `cost_charged`, `root_budget_holder`, `SettlementStatus`), `chio-attest-buyer` (offline replay).
- **Orca surface:** An "Attested Receipts" tab beside Orca's annotate-AI-diffs review (`src/renderer` review surfaces; mobile `review/[worktreeId].tsx`), each call showing `cost_charged`, the IOU id, and a "Verify offline" button.

### 4. Policy-as-code spend governor with diff-on-change and a stamped policy hash
A YAML policy in the repo defines per-agent spend velocity and approval thresholds; the cockpit shows a policy diff and the `policy_hash` that gets stamped into every receipt. This closes the loop from control to evidence: you can prove what the rule was at decision time.
- **Crates:** `chio-policy` (`HushSpec` `VelocityRule` with `max_spend_per_window` / `approve_above`, `BudgetExhausted` trigger, compiler/merge/version; `policy_hash` per receipt).
- **Orca surface:** A "Spend Policy" editor panel with before/after diff and live `policy_hash`, wired to a new `commerce:*` IPC namespace (`src/main/ipc/commerce.ts`) and an `orca commerce policy lint/apply` CLI verb.

### 5. Per-worktree Session Compliance Certificate on merge
Every time an agent's worktree is merged, Chio emits a signed, auditor-verifiable certificate proving the session stayed in scope, in budget, and never bypassed a guard. The merge gate the CFO/CISO actually wants.
- **Crates:** `chio-cli` `cert.rs` + `chio-acp-proxy` (`generate_compliance_certificate` / `verify_compliance_certificate`, `spec/COMPLIANCE-CERTIFICATE.md`; FullBundle mode re-verifies every receipt signature with no running node).
- **Orca surface:** A "Session Certified" badge gating the merge button in the annotate-AI-diffs review pane, plus an `orca commerce cert generate/verify/inspect` CLI verb.

### 6. One-click regulator evidence package (EU AI Act Art. 19 / PCI Req. 10 / ISO 42001)
Select a date range or a worktree and export a signed bundle of receipts, control-to-clause mappings, and Merkle inclusion proofs that an auditor verifies with no running Chio node. This defeats the "your logs could have been edited" objection that every payment protocol punts on.
- **Crates:** `chio-enterprise-export` (`EnterpriseExportBundle`, `verify_enterprise_export`, `ControlEvidenceMap`, `DataGovernanceReport` with forced PII redaction, `ApprovalCase` quorum), `chio-transaction-passport` (evidence graph), the compliance mappings already in `docs/compliance/*`.
- **Orca surface:** An "Export Audit Package" action in the review/source-control surface and an `orca commerce export --since <ts> --scope <worktree>` CLI verb.

### 7. Stream every agent decision to the company SIEM as OCSF events
Pipe every Chio receipt (allow and deny) into Splunk/Sentinel/Elastic/Datadog as OCSF 1.3.0 Authorization events, live, with cryptographic trust grading (an untrusted-signer Allow downgraded to Unverified). The integration that gets a CISO to yes.
- **Crates:** `chio-siem` (`ocsf::receipt_to_ocsf`, `SplunkHecExporter`/`ElasticsearchExporter`/`DatadogExporter`, OCSF Security Lake sink, DLQ, rate-limit, redaction).
- **Orca surface:** A "Compliance Sinks" settings tab beside the usage panels and a `commerce:siemConfig` IPC namespace; per-receipt fan-out fires from the agent-hooks bus.

## The killer demo: "The $47K Runaway, Stopped Mid-Keystroke, With a Receipt"

90 seconds, no crypto rail, nothing that depends on broadcasting a transaction. This is the honest, defensible demo.

1. Fan one prompt across five worktree-agents. A "Budget pool: $50" field is set in the launch dialog. The sixth agent is rejected at preflight with `workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded` (feature 2).
2. One agent, told to be aggressive, races toward the cap. The repurposed usage panel shows the live spend bar climbing per metered tool call (feature 1).
3. At the mandate ceiling, the kernel denies the next paid call. The agent's terminal split shows the typed deny finding code; the spend bar stops. It is a signed, replayable denial, not a log line (feature 1, `CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy`).
4. Open the Attested Receipts tab. Every call so far is a line with `cost_charged`, an IOU id, and the stamped `policy_hash`. Click "Verify offline" on one; it re-verifies the signature with no running node (features 3, 4).
5. Merge the winning worktree. A "Session Certified" badge appears; click "Export Audit Package" and the signed bundle downloads, ready to hand an auditor (features 5, 6).

The line: every other cockpit shows you the spend; Chio refuses it, and hands you the receipt.

A second, quieter enterprise demo: flip a `commerce:siemConfig` toggle and watch the same allow/deny decisions land in Splunk as OCSF Authorization events in real time (feature 7).

## What we deliberately do NOT build

- **No custody, no wallet, no fund movement in the default product.** Chio prepares and proves; a licensed rail moves money. The web3/`chio-settle` broadcast path stays feature-gated, off by default, and is at most a later regulated-operator add-on SKU. We never bundle an operator signing key in the distribution.
- **No settlement take-rate.** Charging basis points on the flow of funds is the single most license-triggering decision available and contradicts the custody-neutral architecture. We price as SaaS (seat + usage) and an enterprise compliance license.
- **No two-sided marketplace in v1.** No Bazaar, no list-to-sell wizard, no federated registries, no bonded-seller slashing, no agent-to-agent hiring. These are cold-start traps that need buyer and seller liquidity that does not exist; they are a year-two option the wedge must earn first.
- **No live on-chain "buy the API" demo as the headline.** It is prepare-only in-tree and needs a broadcaster and testnet ops nobody has budgeted. We keep it as an internal proof of the rail-neutral story, not a sales demo.
- **No KYC/AML/sanctions product we cannot back.** We are strictly a relying party. If counterparty screening is ever needed, the licensed issuer carries the BSA/CIP obligation and liability; Chio verifies, it does not warrant identity. (And because v1 moves no money, this surface stays out of scope entirely.)
- **No autonomous, unattended buying.** v1 is enforcement and audit of agent spend under human-set mandates, not agents transacting unattended on the open market.
- **No FFI-based spend gate.** The FFI surface (`chio-bindings-ffi`) is stateless verify/sign/hash only. Budget enforcement is stateful and lives behind the sidecar. We use FFI only for offline signature/canonicalization checks on the read path, never to authorize a call.

## Top risks and mitigations

### Risk 1: The headline enforcement claim is false in Orca's signature topology (fan-out double-spend)
`BudgetEnforcer` is an in-memory, single-process, non-atomic counter. Across N parallel worktrees, two agents checking the same pool concurrently both pass, so "physically cannot overspend" is not true in exactly the configuration the product runs in. This is the single most dangerous gap because it is a marketed feature that the code does not deliver as-pitched.
- **Mitigation:** Make the bundled `chio-api-protect` sidecar the one authoritative reservation service. Every paid call must obtain a scoped capability via an atomic reserve-then-charge against a durable, concurrency-safe ledger before execution; per-worktree enforcers are advisory caches only. The `WorkflowBudgetPool` preflight validates allocation but must be backed by atomic mint at call time. Do not ship the kill-switch claim until a single-ledger reservation path is demonstrated under concurrent fan-out. Treat this as the first hard engineering milestone.

### Risk 2: Demand for "agents transacting" is premature; we could build for a market that is not buying yet
If we drift toward marketplace, settlement, or autonomous-buying features, we are underwriting a 2027 thesis with a small team and will starve the one thing customers buy now.
- **Mitigation:** Lead with control and compliance, not commerce. The sellable unit this quarter is the budget pool plus the signed receipt; the expansion is the audit-export and SIEM license. Validate with 2-3 named design-partner agencies running fleets on real budget who will pay for the brake and the receipt before any spend on marketplace surfaces. Cut every feature whose unit economics depend on agent-to-agent transaction volume materializing. The contrarian "sell the NO" framing (prove the agent did less than authorized) is both the safest positioning and the one matching the prepare-only code.

### Risk 3: The fork is a maintenance treadmill and the moat lives in code that is MIT and copyable
Orca ships daily across ~5,000 files; a naive fork drowns a small team in rebase conflicts. Separately, both the cockpit (MIT) and the protocol crates are forkable, so a well-funded incumbent could copy the surface. The durable moat is not the receipt format or the kill switch (each a one-quarter bolt-on) but architectural neutrality plus an accumulated, signed audit history a fork cannot mint.
- **Mitigation (fork):** Build a versioned `chio-orca` + `chio-orca-core` product crate first (mirroring the existing `chio-mercury`/`chio-wall` template) so all Orca-specific Rust and the `commerce:*` IPC schemas live in this repo behind the public-entrypoint allowlist. The Electron fork carries only brand strings, one `src/main/ipc/commerce.ts`, and the ported `chio-cli` React dashboard (React 18 + Vite -> Orca's React 19 + Vite is a minor skew). Pin to an Orca tag, rebase on a fixed weekly cadence, and isolate all rename churn into a scripted, re-runnable brand codemod so a rebase is "re-apply patch," not "resolve 200 conflicts." Retain the Lovecast Inc. MIT notice in every kept file; only net-new Chio files carry fresh copyright; drop the `Orca`/`Stably` marks and the `com.stablyai.orca` appId and run a clearance search on "Chio."
- **Mitigation (moat):** Anchor the durable defensibility in the offline-verifiable, clause-mapped compliance export (years of compliance engineering an agent-IDE incumbent will not prioritize, and counter-incentivized for any single rail that does not want its logs independently re-verifiable) and in the federation substrate (`chio-federation`, the deepest part of the codebase) as the year-two network play. Keep the operator receipt-signing trust root a service Chio runs, not a binary anyone compiles.

## The first 90 days

**Weeks 1-3: Stabilize the substrate and surface the CLI contract.**
- Land the in-flight crate extraction (`chio-commerce-order`, `chio-transaction-passport`, `chio-agent-web-interop` out of `chio-control-plane`) and pin a `chio-orca-core` contract crate so nothing downstream is wiring against types that move.
- Build the minimum `chio` commerce CLI the cockpit will shell to: `budget set`, run-with-cap, `receipt export`, `cert generate/verify`. Today the crates are linked but no commerce verb is surfaced; without this the fork has nothing to call.

**Weeks 3-6: Prove the one hard thing.**
- Stand up `chio-api-protect` as a bundled sidecar and implement the single authoritative, atomic, durable reserve-then-charge spend ledger (Risk 1). Demonstrate no double-spend under concurrent fan-out. This is the milestone that makes the kill-switch claim true. Do not proceed to UI polish until this passes.

**Weeks 6-9: Fork, rebrand, wire the wedge.**
- Fork Orca at a pinned tag; apply the scripted brand codemod; create `chio-orca`/`chio-orca-core`; add the one `src/main/ipc/commerce.ts` and the `registerCommerceHandlers()` line.
- Port the existing `chio-cli` React dashboard in as the "Attested Receipts" and budget tabs (lowest-risk, highest-leverage build).
- Wire the agent-hooks bus to the sidecar allow/deny gate for the per-worktree mandate and the fan-out budget pool field in the launch dialog (features 1, 2, 3).

**Weeks 9-12: Make it sellable and land design partners.**
- Ship the Session Compliance Certificate on merge and the one-click signed audit export (features 5, 6), and the OCSF SIEM sink behind a settings toggle (feature 7).
- Cut the 90-second "$47K Runaway, Stopped, With a Receipt" demo end to end.
- Sign 2-3 design-partner agencies running fleets on real client budget; charge them. The deliverable at day 90 is a forked, rebranded cockpit that enforces a hard per-worktree and per-pool spend mandate, refuses the call that breaches it, and exports an offline-verifiable receipt and compliance certificate, with at least one paying design partner validating the wedge.

Out-of-scope-but-noted, deferred to after day 90: policy-as-code editor UI (feature 4) can ship as a fast-follow once the `chio-policy` `policy_hash` is stamped into receipts; the mobile phone-tap approval flow; and any federation or marketplace surface.
