### ground:commerce-landscape
Agentic commerce went from concept to shipping infrastructure across 2025-2026, and the standards are stacking into complementary layers rather than one winner: ACP (OpenAI + Stripe, the checkout/merchant layer, Apache-2.0, live in ChatGPT Instant Checkout), AP2 (Google + 60-100 orgs, the trust/mandate/authorization layer built on cryptographically-signed Intent/Cart/Payment mandates), and x402 (Coinbase + Cloudflare, now a Linux Foundation project, the per-call execution/micropayment layer on stablecoins, ~165M tx and adopted by AWS Bedrock AgentCore Payments in May 2026). The card networks (Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay/Agentic Tokens) and wallets (Skyfire KYA/KYAPay, Nekuda, Payman, PayPal agent-ready) are racing to issue scoped, agent-bound credentials and staged wallets. Identity is consolidating around DIDs/VCs, W3C Agent Identity CG, DIF MCP-I, and on-chain ERC-8004 (live on Ethereum mainnet 29 Jan 2026). The decisive, unfilled white space is NOT another payment rail: it is the out-of-agent enforcement, attestation, and audit layer. The market openly admits enforcement must live outside agent code (the widely-cited "$47,000 runaway LangChain agent" with dashboards but no kill-switch), that audit-trail standards for AI-generated logs do not exist, and that dispute/liability evidence is untested in courts. That gap maps almost one-to-one onto Chio's kernel, receipt log, guards, capability authority, and commerce/trust crates - and Chio's chio-commerce-order already binds AP2 mandate hashes and the ACP delegated-payment-token hash in a single signed ledger, positioning it as the neutral verifier across all three stacks rather than a competitor to any of them.
Capabilities today: ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol), OpenAI + Stripe, released Apache-2.0 on 29 Sep 2025: agent-initiated checkout where a narrowly-scoped Shared Payment Token (SPT) is handed to the merchant who stays merchant-of-record and charges via any compliant PSP; ships a Delegated Payments Spec so non-Stripe processors can participate. Powered ChatGPT Instant Checkout (Etsy + ~dozen Shopify brands); PayPal joined as provider 28 Oct 2025; Stripe shipped an Agentic Commerce Suite 11 Dec 2025.; AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol), Google-led with 60+ (now 100+) orgs, announced Sep 2025: payment-method-agnostic, does not move money but produces verifiable authorization records via a chain of three cryptographically-signed mandates - Intent Mandate (user delegates authority), Cart Mandate (user approves specific cart + price), Payment Mandate (credential the network sees). Co-launched a Conversational Commerce Agent with PayPal 27 Oct 2025. Spec at ap2-protocol.org.; x402 (Coinbase + Cloudflare), open-sourced May 2025, donated to the Linux Foundation x402 Foundation 2 Apr 2026: revives HTTP 402 so a server replies 402 Payment Required, the agent signs a stablecoin (USDC, mostly Base/Solana) payment, attaches proof, and retries. Reference impl Apache-2.0 with TS/Python/Go SDKs and Express/Fastify/Next.js adapters. ~69k active agents, ~165M tx, ~$50M cumulative volume by Apr 2026; Stripe integrated Feb 2026.; x402 Bazaar: an MCP-server discovery layer / machine-readable catalog where agents find and call 10,000+ paid endpoints and pay per call in USDC, no accounts or subscriptions - the emerging agent-to-agent tool marketplace.; Card networks shipped agent rails: Visa Intelligent Commerce (scoped tokenized credentials for agents, issuer-side machine-payment auth, integrations with Anthropic/OpenAI/Microsoft) plus Intelligent Commerce Connect (one merchant integration spanning four protocols). Mastercard Agent Pay with Agentic Tokens binds a tokenized card credential to a specific agent + merchant scope + consent policy; first live agentic transaction 29 Sep 2025.; Agent wallets / KYA startups: Skyfire (Know Your Agent identity + KYAPay merchant-side accept, stablecoin micropayments, demoed with Visa Intelligent Commerce Dec 2025); Nekuda (secure agent wallet + agentic mandates, $5M from Madrona/Amex/Visa Ventures); Payman (per-agent wallets over ACH + stablecoin); PayPal agent-ready for existing merchants.; Agent identity standards: W3C DID + Verifiable Credentials as the base; W3C Agent Identity Registry Protocol Community Group; DIF MCP-I (donated Mar 2026) extending identity to MCP agents; TRAIL did:trail draft method; and on-chain ERC-8004 'Trustless Agents' (live Ethereum mainnet 29 Jan 2026) with Identity, Reputation, and Validation registries, authored across MetaMask/Ethereum Foundation/Google/Coinbase as a trustless extension of A2A.; ### ground:regulatory
Autonomous-agent commerce sits on a payments stack built for humans, and that mismatch is the central design constraint. Custody is the bright line: hold or move user funds and you are a money transmitter (FinCEN MSB plus state MTLs, unlicensed is a felony under 18 U.S.C. 1960, 50-state licensing about 250k-350k), while genuine non-custodial software is not. Stablecoins are now regulated (US GENIUS Act enacted July 18 2025, EU MiCA) with 1:1 reserves, restricted issuance and custody, and no yield, and KYC and AML assume a human principal an agent cannot be. Card networks (Mastercard Agent Pay, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol) ship verified-agent rails but agent chargeback and dispute liability is explicitly unsettled and networks will not absorb losses they did not authorize. The lowest-friction legal path stays out of the flow of funds with a licensed custody and KYC partner, settles over regulated stablecoin or card rails, and enforces signed spending mandates with full audit trails so a regulated principal is always accountable.</summary>

Capabilities today: Money transmission gates everything: custody or transmit value and you need FinCEN MSB plus state MTLs; unlicensed is a felony under 18 U.S.C. 1960 (up to 250k, 5 years) and 50-state licensing is about 250k-350k plus bonds and AML. Under GENIUS only supervised entities (banks, trust companies, custodians) may custody stablecoins, reserves, or keys, holding customer assets as customer property.; Custody is the bright line: a hosted or custodial wallet that can move user funds is a money transmitter under FinCEN 2019 guidance and most states; non-custodial software without unilateral control generally is not. Stablecoin law is live: GENIUS (July 18 2025) needs permitted issuers, 100 percent 1:1 reserves, BSA and AML, and no yield; MiCA makes fiat stablecoins E-Money Tokens needing a credit or e-money institution, and custody and transfer need CASP authorization across 27 states (PSD2 license may also apply from March 2026).; Card networks built agent rails with a human in the chain: Mastercard Agent Pay binds an Agentic Token to agent, merchant scope, and consent policy, and Visa Trusted Agent Protocol verifies agents; both require agent verification and consumer-set spending limits. Agents use stablecoin rails: x402 over HTTP 402, plus Coinbase AgentKit, Stripe, Crossmint, Privy, and Turnkey wallets (Crossmint holds MiCA CASP in all 27 EU states). Ways to avoid money transmission: non-custodial design, agent-of-payee exemption (about 22 states), merchant-of-record or payfac, and BaaS with For-Benefit-Of accounts at an MTL-exempt partner bank.
Gaps: No regulatory identity for agents: KYC, AML, and Travel Rule assume a human or entity, so an agent cannot satisfy them itself; GENIUS, MiCA, and VARA do not address an agent as the transacting party.; Chargeback and dispute liability for agent payments is undefined, no agent-specific reason codes exist, and networks will not absorb losses they did not authorize; whether Reg E covers a consumer delegating a card to an agent is unsettled, and merchants lose their usual fraud evidence so many disputes are confusion not fraud.; Accountability fragments across developer, deployer, user, and wallet provider (a roughly 450k erroneous transfer was blamed on an agent session crash with no clear liable party), poisoned oracles and prompt injection to sanctioned addresses are an unguarded attack surface no AML framework covers, and GENIUS no-yield plus licensed-issuer-only issuance blocks minting your own token or float without a partner or charter.

grounding.summary: The Chio repo already contains a deep, mostly-real autonomous-commerce stack, far beyond the "in-flight modules" framing in the premise. The agent-facing economic primitives exist and are tested: a capability marketplace where an agent submits a signed bid and a provider mints a scoped, time-bounded, cost-capped CapabilityToken against a verified funds reservation (chio-open-market/bidding.rs); monetary budget enforcement both flat (chio-metering/budget.rs) and hierarchical org->dept->team->agent (chio-metering/budget_hierarchy.rs); per-receipt cost metering wired into the kernel as a credit-evaluator hook that mints signed IOUs post-dispatch (chio-credit/hook.rs); and an attested commerce-order passport that verifies AP2 checkout/payment mandates and ACP delegated-payment tokens plus a full PSP payment lifecycle (chio-commerce-order/*). Real on-chain settlement exists behind a web3 feature flag: chio-settle executes EVM escrow/bond-vault lock/release/impair/refund, EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization, x402 payment requirements, Circle nanopayments, ERC-4337 paymaster, CCIP cross-chain and Solana parity, driven by a multi-party signed capital-execution instruction (operator treasury + custodian authority chain) in chio-credit/capital_and_execution.rs. The critical design boundary: the capital/credit layer is "simulation-first / custody-neutral" by default (automatic_capital_execution_supported=false, external_execution_authoritative=false); it produces signed instructions and lets the settlement rail (crypto) or a manual fiat rail actually move funds. There is a real liability/insurance market (quote/bind/claim/adjudication/payout, chio-market) and an autonomous pricing+capital-optimization layer that runs in Shadow/Advisory/Active modes (chio-autonomy). The biggest gaps for an Orca fusion are surface-level, not economic: there is no long-running kernel HTTP/JSON-RPC server (integration is the in-process kernel or the `chio` CLI emitting signed JSON), no fiat custody execution, and no UI beyond a small bundled React dashboard in chio-cli.
capabilities: Capability marketplace bid/ask/accept: chio-open-market/src/bidding.rs implements bid() -> SignedAskResponse that mints a scoped CapabilityToken (server_id/tool_name, max_invocations, max_cost_per_invocation, max_total_cost) bound to the agent subject, and accept() which requires a signature-verified VerifiedReservationReceipt covering the token's total liability. Fail-closed against revoked/stale/expired listings, scope widening, currency mismatch, under-priced bids.

Monetary budget enforcement: chio-metering/src/budget.rs BudgetEnforcer/BudgetPolicy enforces max_total + per-session/per-agent/per-tool limits with saturating arithmetic and typed BudgetViolation. chio-metering/src/budget_hierarchy.rs BudgetTree enforces org->department->team->agent caps per BudgetWindow (Daily/etc) against a caller-supplied SpendSnapshot, fail-closed BudgetDecision.

Per-receipt cost metering + IOU minting: chio-metering/src/cost.rs (CostMetadata, CostDimension) and chio-credit/src/hook.rs CreditEvaluatorHook, which the kernel invokes on each finalized signed receipt to mint a signed IouEnvelope (chio.credit.iou-envelope.v1) binding amount_units/currency to receipt_id + content/policy hashes. Zero-price receipts skip minting.

Capital book + capital-execution instructions: chio-credit/src/credit/capital_and_execution.rs models a full ledger (Commit/Hold/Draw/Disburse/Release/Repay/Impair), CapitalExecutionInstructionArtifact with a multi-party signed authority chain (OperatorTreasury + Custodian), execution rails (Manual/Api/Ach/Wire/Ledger/Sandbox/Web3), execution windows, and reconciliation (observed vs intended amount). Plus CapitalAllocationDecisionArtifact (Allocate/Queue/ManualReview/Deny) and a CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy with a kill switch.

Credit underwriting/scoring: chio-credit risk_reports + chio-credit/lib.rs define ExposureLedger, CreditScorecard (bands Prime..Restricted), CreditFacility (grant/manual-review/deny with terms: credit_limit, utilization_ceiling_bps, reserve_ratio_bps, concentration_cap_bps), CreditBond (lock/hold/release/impair), and loss-lifecycle/backtest/provider-risk packages.

Attested commerce-order passport: chio-commerce-order verifies a CommerceOrderVerificationBundle: SHA-256-pinned event log replayed through a fixed state machine (intent_recorded -> provider_admitted -> quote_bound -> mandate_bound -> budget_reserved -> payment_verified -> fulfillment_attested -> settlement_dispatched -> settlement_reconciled -> completed), a CommercePaymentLifecycle (PSP, payment_intent, manual capture before expiry, fraud/dispute/refund/chargeback/transfer-reversal states), and a CommerceMandateLedger carrying AP2 checkout+payment mandate hashes and an ACP delegated-payment-token hash with occurrence/single-use limits.

Real on-chain settlement (feature = web3): chio-settle/src/evm/* does live eth_sendTransaction/eth_call/eth_getTransactionReceipt, escrow create/merkle-release/dual-sign-release/refund, bond-vault lock/release/impair/expiry, ERC20 approve, reading EscrowSnapshot/BondSnapshot from contract state, gas estimation, RPC egress contract (no redirects, size caps). chio-settle/src/payments.rs adds x402 PaymentRequirements, EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization digests, Circle nanopayments, ERC-4337 paymaster compatibility; ccip.rs cross-chain; solana.rs Ed25519 parity; retry.rs dead-letter; ops.rs emergency controls/kill switch.

Web3 settlement artifacts + lifecycle: chio-web3/src/settlement.rs Web3SettlementDispatchArtifact and Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact with a 9-state lifecycle (PendingDispatch..Settled/PartiallySettled/Reversed/ChargedBack/TimedOut/Failed/Reorged), anchor-inclusion-proof + oracle-conversion-evidence reconciliation, and a completion-flow binding tying every transfer back to a governed receipt id.

Settlement automation (autonomous): chio-settle/src/automation.rs SettlementWatchdogJob (EscrowTimeout/FinalityObservation/BondExpiry) triggered by Cron/Log/CustomLogic, with duplicate suppression and operator-override; outcomes Executed/DuplicateSuppressed/DelayedButSafe/ManualOverrideRequired.

Liability/insurance market: chio-market quote_and_bind, LiabilityQuoteRequest/Response, LiabilityPricingAuthority (cross-validates an active granted CreditFacility + approved underwriting decision + capital book), claim package -> adjudication (ClaimUpheld/PartialSettlement/ProviderUpheld) -> payout/settlement instructions and receipts.

Autonomous pricing + capital optimization: chio-autonomy/src/model.rs defines AutonomousPricingDecision (Reprice/Renew/Decline/BindWithinEnvelope/ManualReview) and CapitalPoolOptimization (IncreaseReserve/DecreaseReserve/ShiftCapacity/...) gated by AutonomousAutomationMode (Shadow/Advisory/Active) and review states (AutoApproved/HumanReviewRequired/ShadowOnly/Blocked), all evidence-referential to prior signed artifacts.

External agent-commerce protocol bridges: chio-agent-web-interop/src/artifacts/ has dedicated verifiers for ap2.rs, acp_commerce.rs, x402.rs (validates resource/payment-requirements/payment-proof/settlement digests, order_id, network, asset, amount, status authorized/settled/refunded, bound chio_payment_receipt_ref), plus oauth2/mcp/a2a/openapi/spiffe/scim, all projected into a TransactionPassport evidence graph.

Multi-agent shared budget for fan-out: chio-workflow-preflight/src/types.rs WorkflowBudgetPool + WorkflowPreflightPlan (parent_task -> child_tasks) with validation that parent and every child budget_minor stays within the pool total and currency is coherent (workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded). Maps directly to Orca's fan-one-prompt-across-N-agents model.

Buyer/auditor trust artifacts: chio-attest-buyer-core offline proof-package verification (claims, disclosure, issuer, oracle, revocation, trust_bundle); chio-transaction-passport produces the cross-protocol evidence graph + verifier policy that enterprise-export and agent-web-interop consume.

CLI integration seam already wired: crates/products/chio-cli (binary `chio`) depends on chio-commerce-order, chio-credit, chio-settle; has command trees for settle (chio settle status over a chio-store-sqlite DB), market, capital, credit, liability (claim-settlement-instruction-issue), buyer/treaty dispatch, a --budget-db SQLite flag, and even ships a React/Vite dashboard under chio-cli/dashboard/.
gaps: No fiat custody execution: the capital/credit layer is simulation-first/custody-neutral by default (CapitalExecutionInstructionSupportBoundary/CapitalAllocationDecisionSupportBoundary default automatic_capital_execution_supported=false, automatic_dispatch_supported=false, external_execution_authoritative=false). Only the crypto rail (chio-settle EVM/Solana) actually moves money; ACH/Wire rails emit signed instruction artifacts that a human/external custodian must execute. There is no fiat PSP/bank connector that closes the loop.

No long-running kernel server: there is no HTTP/JSON-RPC/gRPC daemon exposing the kernel or economy crates. Integration today is in-process (embedders drive the kernel) or the `chio` CLI emitting/consuming signed JSON. An Orca (Electron/TypeScript) front end has no socket/API to call; a thin local server or CLI-bridge must be built.

Commerce-order verification is post-hoc, not a live order engine: chio-commerce-order verifies an already-assembled, SHA-256-pinned bundle (event log + payment lifecycle + mandate ledger). Nothing in-repo orchestrates a live order forward through those states, calls a real PSP to create the payment intent, or assembles the bundle; the producer side is assumed external.

Budget state is in-memory / caller-supplied: BudgetEnforcer holds counters in process memory and BudgetTree.evaluate takes a caller-supplied SpendSnapshot. There is no shared, durable, concurrency-safe budget ledger that multiple parallel agent worktrees could draft against atomically (the SQLite snapshot store is explicitly out of scope of chio-metering).

No price discovery / catalog: bidding requires a pre-existing signed Listing + ListingPricingHint (chio-listing). There is no in-repo registry service that publishes, indexes, or lets an agent search live tool/data/compute listings; chio-listing provides the types and search primitives but not a running marketplace registry.

AP2/ACP mandates are verified by hash only: chio-commerce-order checks ap2_checkout_mandate_hash / ap2_payment_mandate_hash / acp_delegated_payment_token_hash are well-formed SHA-256 and occurrence/window-consistent, but does not parse or cryptographically verify the underlying AP2/ACP mandate documents themselves (that lives partially in chio-agent-web-interop adapters but is not joined to the order replay).

No agent-to-agent payment primitive distinct from buying capabilities: an agent can buy a scoped capability token and reserve funds, but there is no first-class 'agent A pays agent B for a delivered result' settlement object outside the liability-claim-payout and capital-transfer paths; peer settlement would be assembled from capital-execution instructions by hand.

Metering is not automatically populated from real tool cost: CostMetadata (compute time, data volume, API cost) is a typed container the kernel/guards must fill; there is no built-in collector that derives actual provider cost (e.g. tokens, GPU-seconds, vendor invoice) for an arbitrary CLI coding agent run.

grounding.summary: The Chio trust layer is unusually complete for agent-to-agent commerce, far beyond a typical attestation framework. Agent identity is self-certifying: did:chio (crates/trust/chio-did) uses an Ed25519 public key as the method-specific id, and the same key is bound into every CapabilityToken.subject (crates/core/chio-core-types/src/capability/token.rs) as a DPoP sender constraint, so identity, delegation, and authorization share one key with no registry lookup. On top of that sits a full verifiable-credentials lane (chio-credentials): native Ed25519-signed AgentPassports plus a standards-native OID4VCI/OID4VP projection, cross-issuer portfolios, selective disclosure via BBS+ (chio-selective-disclosure), and a TrustTier (Unverified/Attested/Verified/Premier) synthesized from compliance score and behavioral anomaly. Reputation (chio-reputation) is deterministic and receipt-derived: eight behavioral metrics composed into a Sybil-resistant tier mapping with per-feed floors. Every kernel decision is signed into a ChioReceipt that already carries rich FinancialReceiptMetadata (settlement status, budget holds, delegation depth, root budget holder, oracle conversion evidence), and bilateral cross-org co-signing (chio-federation DualSignedReceipt) plus an offline buyer/auditor proof-verification boundary (chio-attest-buyer) provide non-repudiation across kernels. Commerce is partly built already: a chio-commerce-order crate validates AP2 checkout/payment mandate hashes and ACP delegated-payment tokens, chio-settle implements x402 (EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization), and chio-market ships a complete liability-claim -> dispute -> adjudication lifecycle. The main missing pieces are legal-entity binding (KYC/identity-proofing of agents), sanctions/AML screening, hardened escrow, neutral-arbiter binding for disputes, and any UI/CLI surface to expose counterparty trust. Revocation is handled by a sparse-Merkle revocation oracle (chio-revocation-oracle) with non-inclusion proofs and a passport bridge.
capabilities: Self-certifying agent identity: did:chio (crates/trust/chio-did/src/lib.rs) where the method-specific id is the lowercase hex of an Ed25519 public key; resolution is registry-free and self-certifying, with optional ChioReceiptLogService and ChioPassportStatusService endpoints on the DidDocument.

Identity-to-authorization binding: CapabilityToken.subject and CapabilityTokenBody.subject are PublicKey (crates/core/chio-core-types/src/capability/token.rs), bound as a DPoP sender constraint, so the did:chio key is also the capability holder; tokens carry issuer, scope, delegation_chain (Vec<DelegationLink>), caveats, and budget_share_bps for sub-agent budget splits.

Verifiable credentials and Agent Passport: chio-credentials ships AgentPassport (passport.rs) as a bundle of Ed25519-signed ReputationCredentials with merkle_roots, valid_until, PassportLifecycleState (Active/Stale/Superseded/Revoked), and a standards-native OID4VCI/OID4VP lane (oid4vci.rs, oid4vp.rs, portable_jwt_vc.rs, portable_sd_jwt.rs) plus cross-issuer portfolios/trust-packs/migration (cross_issuer.rs).

Coarse trust gating: TrustTier (crates/trust/chio-credentials/src/trust_tier.rs) deterministically maps a 0..1000 compliance score plus behavioral-anomaly flag into Unverified/Attested/Verified/Premier, with a monotone, fail-pessimistic rule that a live anomaly blocks promotion to Premier; relying parties gate on this without parsing the full factor breakdown.

Deterministic, receipt-derived reputation: chio-reputation computes a LocalReputationScorecard (score.rs) from a LocalReputationCorpus of signed receipts, capability-lineage records, and budget usage, across eight metrics (boundary pressure, resource stewardship, least privilege, history depth, specialization, delegation hygiene, reliability, incident correlation); receipt_integrity_valid enforces trusted_kernel_keys so unsigned receipts score zero.

Sybil-resistant reputation tiers: ReputationTier (crates/trust/chio-reputation/src/tier.rs) requires composed-score thresholds AND a per-feed floor (TIER_3_PER_FEED_THRESHOLD) so a flood of one feed cannot reach the top tier; tiers gate marketplace discovery visibility while cosign verify gates publication.

Signed, economically-aware receipts: ChioReceipt (crates/core/chio-core-types/src/receipt/body.rs, schema chio.receipt.v1) is content-addressed, carries actor_chain, GuardEvidence, policy_hash, and trust_level, and FinancialReceiptMetadata (receipt/economics.rs) records cost_charged, currency, budget_remaining/total, delegation_depth, root_budget_holder, payment_reference, SettlementStatus, oracle_evidence, plus full budget-hold lineage (authorize/terminal exposure and realized spend).

Cross-org non-repudiation: chio-federation bilateral co-signing (bilateral.rs) produces a DualSignedReceipt where both org A and org B kernels sign the canonical CoSigningBody over the same receipt bytes; verification is strict (both signatures must validate against pinned peers). Kernel-to-kernel trust is established via a signed mTLS-style handshake that pins peer keys with a rotation_due freshness ceiling (trust_establishment.rs).

Offline buyer/auditor proof verification: chio-attest-buyer exposes a fail-closed verification boundary (api.rs verify_buyer_attestation_packet / verify_buyer_attestation_review_package_with_proof_replay_json) over BuyerAttestationPacket and ReceiptLineageBundle (types.rs), binding buyer_id, capability_id, treaty scope, BilateralInvocation, workflow receipt, budget_refs, and settlement_claimed into a replayable proof package.

Hardware/TEE attestation: chio-attest-verify is the single source of truth for Sigstore (Fulcio chain, OIDC issuer pinning, SAN regexp, Rekor inclusion + SET) and TEE quote verification for Nitro, SEV-SNP, and TDX (nitro.rs, sev_snp.rs, tdx.rs), all fail-closed with unwrap/expect/unsafe forbidden at the lint level; chio-tee runs a signed, redacted shadow-capture sidecar.

Revocation with proofs: chio-revocation-oracle provides epoch-signed sparse-Merkle roots with InclusionProof/NonInclusionProof, a freshness verifier, and a passport_bridge (apply_passport_revocation) so passport/credential revocation is provable and bounded by epoch freshness.

Capability leases / mandates: chio-governance CapabilityLeaseArtifact (lease.rs, schema chio.capability-lease.v1) is a signed issuer->subject grant over a scope_digest with an action class (ScopedObservation, DelegatedAction, NarrowDestructive) and validity window, verified by verify_capability_lease.

Existing commerce primitives: chio-commerce-order (crates/platform/chio-commerce-order) validates a CommerceOrderContext (buyer/agent/merchant subjects, quote, hashed event log + payment lifecycle + mandate ledger) and a CommerceMandateLedger binding ap2_checkout_mandate_hash, ap2_payment_mandate_hash, and acp_delegated_payment_token_hash with single-use/occurrence and max-amount allowance enforcement.

On-chain settlement rails: chio-settle implements x402 (payments.rs: X402PaymentRequirements, X402SettlementMode PrepaidAuthorization/EscrowBacked, EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization with domain separator) and chio-web3 carries settlement_proof.rs with PublicSettlementDisputeSnapshot/Context and a Web3DisputePolicy::OffChainArbitration / Arbitrator role.

Dispute and adjudication lifecycle: chio-market/src/claim.rs ships SignedLiabilityClaimResponse (Accepted/Denied/partial with covered_amount), LiabilityClaimDisputeArtifact (opened_by, reason, evidence_refs), and LiabilityClaimAdjudicationArtifact (adjudicator, outcome, awarded_amount); chio-control-plane/src/certify.rs adds CertificationDisputeState/Record/Request.

Differentiated trust signal: chio-pheromone is a signed, Merkle-committed stigmergic substrate (PheromoneDeposit, observation-cost commitments, scarcity policy, newcomer discount horizon, runtime trust-floor state) gossiped across operators via chio-federation pheromone_gossip, giving a decentralized emergent-trust channel distinct from credential/reputation scoring.

Enterprise identity provenance: EnterpriseIdentityContext / EnterpriseFederationMethod (Jwt, Introspection, Scim, Saml) in crates/core/chio-core-types/src/session.rs lets a passport record enterprise_identity_provenance, tying an agent session to a corporate IdP.
gaps: No KYC-of-agents / legal-entity binding: did:chio and passports prove key control and behavior, but nothing binds an agent key to a verified legal person or organization (no identity-proofing credential type, no LEI/EIN/business-registration attestation). EnterpriseIdentityContext links to a corporate IdP but is not a KYC artifact and is unverified provenance metadata.

No sanctions / AML / counterparty-screening primitive anywhere in crates/trust or crates/economy: no sanctions list, no jurisdiction/eligibility gate, no travel-rule data. Commerce can be metered and settled but not compliance-screened against a counterparty allow/deny policy.

Counterparty trust is verifiable but not discoverable: there is no agent-to-agent counterparty directory or trust-lookup surface. A relying agent can verify a presented passport/receipt, but nothing helps it find a counterparty, fetch its current TrustTier/reputation, and negotiate terms before transacting.

Dispute adjudication has no neutral-arbiter binding: LiabilityClaimAdjudicationArtifact.adjudicator and Web3RegulatedRole::Arbitrator are free-form identifiers; there is no registry of trusted arbiters, no escrow-release-on-adjudication wiring, and no enforced link from a signed adjudication outcome back to a settlement reversal/refund.

Escrow is declared, not implemented: X402SettlementMode::EscrowBacked and EscrowBacked dispute policy exist as enum variants, but there is no escrow state machine (lock, hold-until-delivery, release/refund) tying budget holds in FinancialReceiptMetadata to on-chain escrow in chio-settle/chio-web3.

No portable mandate <-> capability bridge surfaced: chio-commerce-order validates AP2/ACP mandate hashes and chio-governance issues capability leases, but they are separate artifacts; there is no single helper that turns a verified AP2/ACP payment mandate into a scoped, budget-bounded CapabilityToken the kernel will enforce at tool-call time.

Reputation is local-corpus-only by design: compute_local_scorecard depends on the caller assembling a corpus; there is no shared/queryable reputation service or signed reputation-snapshot exchange protocol for a counterparty to pull a fresh score at transaction time (portable_reputation.rs is a credential format, not a live feed).

No product surface: all of the above lives in Rust crates with no CLI/UI exposure. There is no Orca-side panel, command, or wire endpoint to issue a passport, present credentials, view a counterparty trust tier, open a dispute, or inspect a settlement receipt - the forked cockpit would need this entire presentation layer.
opportunities: Counterparty trust card in the forked Orca worktree/agent view: when one agent is about to transact with another tool server or agent, render a trust card backed by chio-credentials AgentPassport verification + TrustTier + chio-reputation tier and a chio-revocation-oracle freshness check; gate the transaction in the kernel on a verifier policy (PassportVerifierPolicy from chio-credentials/registry.rs). This is the headline 'agents you can trust to transact' surface and is mostly assembling existing verified data.

Mandate-to-capability minting: add a control-plane helper that converts a verified chio-commerce-order CommerceMandateLedger (AP2 checkout/payment mandate, ACP delegated-payment token) into a scoped, budget-capped CapabilityToken with budget_share_bps and a CapabilityLeaseArtifact, so a signed human/AP2 mandate becomes kernel-enforced spend authority. Surface it as an Orca CLI command (e.g. chio mandate grant) and a 'budget granted' chip in the UI. Differentiated because the mandate is cryptographically the same key that pays and that the kernel meters.

Signed settlement receipts in the diff/review pane: extend Orca's annotate-AI-diffs review to attach the ChioReceipt + FinancialReceiptMetadata (cost_charged, root_budget_holder, SettlementStatus, oracle_evidence) and, for cross-org calls, the DualSignedReceipt, so every paid tool call an agent made shows a verifiable cost-and-settlement line. chio-attest-buyer already gives an offline verify path for an auditor to replay the whole bundle.

Escrow-backed agent-to-agent jobs: implement the missing escrow state machine on top of the existing X402SettlementMode::EscrowBacked and EIP-3009 prepared transfers, releasing funds only against a co-signed delivery receipt (chio-federation bilateral co-sign) and refunding against a signed LiabilityClaimAdjudicationArtifact. This closes the loop between chio-market dispute artifacts and chio-settle/chio-web3 settlement and is highly defensible (capability-gated escrow with cryptographic delivery proof).

Neutral-arbiter registry and one-click dispute: bind LiabilityClaimAdjudicationArtifact.adjudicator to an arbiter identity attested via chio-attest-verify (Sigstore/TEE) and listed through chio-federation, then expose 'open dispute' from the Orca receipt view to emit a SignedLiabilityClaimDispute with evidence_refs pulled straight from the receipt/lineage bundle. Turns the existing dispute types into an end-to-end, non-repudiable resolution flow.

KYC-of-agents credential type: add a new ReputationCredential/VC subtype in chio-credentials that binds a did:chio key to a verified legal entity (issuer = a KYC provider attested via chio-attest-verify), revocable through the existing chio-revocation-oracle passport bridge, and gate high-value transactions on its presence via PassportVerifierPolicy. This fills the single biggest gap (legal-entity binding) using the existing credential, tier, and revocation machinery.

Pheromone-based emergent counterparty trust: use chio-pheromone deposits and concentration plus chio-federation pheromone_gossip to surface a live, decentralized 'is this tool server / agent currently trusted by the swarm' signal in the Orca fleet view, complementing static credentials with real-time behavioral consensus across operators - a genuinely differentiated trust channel competitors lack.

Portable reputation handshake at deal time: define a signed reputation-snapshot request/response (extending portable_reputation.rs) so a counterparty agent can pull a fresh, integrity-checked LocalReputationScorecard summary before transacting, exposed via the protocol adapters (chio-a2a-adapter / chio-mcp-adapter) so external agents over A2A/MCP can request Chio trust attestations as a paid, metered tool.
key_facts: did:chio method-specific id = lowercase hex of an Ed25519 public key; resolution is self-certifying with no registry (crates/trust/chio-did/src/lib.rs, DID_CHIO_PREFIX 'did:chio:').
CapabilityToken.subject is a PublicKey bound as a DPoP sender constraint, so the DID key and the capability holder are the same key (crates/core/chio-core-types/src/capability/token.rs).
TrustTier thresholds: Attested>=300, Verified>=700, Premier>=900 with no active behavioral anomaly (crates/trust/chio-credentials/src/trust_tier.rs).

ChioReceipt schema is chio.receipt.v1, content-addressed, and carries FinancialReceiptMetadata with SettlementStatus {NotApplicable, Pending, Settled, Failed} and root_budget_holder (crates/core/chio-core-types/src/receipt/body.rs and receipt/economics.rs).

Bilateral cross-org receipts: DualSignedReceipt over CoSigningBody, schema chio.federation-dual-signed-receipt.v1, verifies only when BOTH kernel signatures validate against pinned peers (crates/trust/chio-federation/src/bilateral.rs).

chio-attest-buyer verifies BuyerAttestationPacket/ReceiptLineageBundle offline and fail-closed, binding buyer_id, capability_id, treaty scope, bilateral invocation, budget_refs, and settlement_claimed (crates/trust/chio-attest-buyer/src/types.rs, api.rs).

Commerce mandates already validated: CommerceMandateLedger binds ap2_checkout_mandate_hash, ap2_payment_mandate_hash, and acp_delegated_payment_token_hash with single-use and max_occurrences allowance enforcement (crates/platform/chio-commerce-order/src/mandate.rs).

x402 settlement implemented over EIP-3009: X402PaymentRequirements with X402SettlementMode {PrepaidAuthorization, EscrowBacked} and PreparedTransferWithAuthorization (crates/economy/chio-settle/src/payments.rs).
Full dispute lifecycle exists: SignedLiabilityClaimResponse -> LiabilityClaimDisputeArtifact -> LiabilityClaimAdjudicationArtifact with awarded_amount (crates/economy/chio-market/src/claim.rs).
Revocation oracle uses epoch-signed sparse-Merkle roots with non-inclusion proofs and a passport revocation bridge (crates/trust/chio-revocation-oracle/src/lib.rs).

No sanctions/AML/KYC-of-agents/legal-entity-binding type exists in crates/trust or crates/economy; EnterpriseIdentityContext (Jwt/Introspection/Scim/Saml) is unverified provenance, not KYC (crates/core/chio-core-types/src/session.rs).
The former in-flight control-plane modules were promoted to dedicated crates: commerce_order -> crates/platform/chio-commerce-order, agent_web -> crates/platform/chio-agent-web-interop.

grounding.summary: Orca (github.com/stablyai/orca, owned by Lovecast Inc., MIT-licensed, ~4.8k stars) is a large but cleanly-layered Electron + TypeScript desktop app (40.6MB TS, ~5,120 files) plus an Expo/React-Native mobile companion (iOS Swift + Android Kotlin native audio module). It is an "ADE" that runs any CLI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, etc.), each in its own git worktree, with parallel orchestration, Ghostty-class WebGL terminals, an embedded Chromium "Design Mode," native GitHub/Linear/GitLab/Jira browsing, SSH worktrees, and computer use. The architecture has four clean process boundaries that are ideal seams for a Rust commerce layer: (1) the Electron main<->renderer IPC bus (~87 namespaced handler files registered in one hub, src/main/ipc/register-core-handlers.ts); (2) a separate terminal daemon over a token-authed NDJSON Unix-socket protocol (src/main/daemon/daemon-server.ts); (3) the public `orca` CLI which talks to the running app over a JSON-RPC envelope on a Unix domain socket / Windows named pipe (src/cli/runtime/transport.ts + src/shared/runtime-rpc-envelope.ts), letting external agents drive Orca; and (4) an agent-hooks subsystem (src/main/agent-hooks/, src/main/ipc/agent-hooks.ts) that installs a managed hook script into each coding agent and receives a versioned JSON POST on every agent lifecycle event. A fork-and-rebrand is mechanically straightforward (MIT license, brand string "orca"/"Orca" confined to ~56 paths plus appId com.stablyai.orca and a handful of bin shims/Casks) but operationally heavy because the project ships daily, is ~5k files, and carries deep native-build, code-signing, and localization tooling. The Chio Rust commerce/trust stack would plug in best as a signed sidecar process behind a new `commerce:*` IPC namespace plus new `orca commerce ...` CLI verbs, with the agent-hooks bus as the per-tool-call metering/capability-gate interception point.
capabilities: MIT license owned by Lovecast Inc. (LICENSE is base64 MIT, repos/stablyai/orca/license confirms spdx MIT, allow_forking=true). Forking and rebranding are legally permitted provided the MIT copyright+permission notice is retained in copies; no copyleft obligation on the new Chio-specific Rust code.

Tech stack: Electron 42 + React 19 + TypeScript 5.9, Vite/electron-vite build, Zustand state, Radix/shadcn + Tailwind v4 UI, xterm 6 beta + WebGL addon for terminals, node-pty + a custom terminal daemon, ssh2 for remote worktrees, tweetnacl for crypto, zod 4 for schemas, i18next localization, posthog telemetry, agent-browser/serve-sim for the embedded browser. pnpm workspace, oxlint/oxfmt, Playwright e2e.

Clean process layering with explicit IPC seams: src/main (1,176 files, the trusted Electron main / privileged side), src/renderer/src (2,668 files, UI), src/preload (audited contextBridge contract in src/preload/index.ts), src/shared (389 cross-process files), src/cli (95 files, the public agent-facing CLI), src/relay (87 files, a JSON-RPC frame dispatcher with keepalive/abort), src/main/daemon (terminal subprocess daemon).

Central IPC registration hub: src/main/ipc/register-core-handlers.ts imports ~50 registerXHandlers() functions, each its own file under src/main/ipc/ using ipcMain.handle('namespace:method', ...). Adding a Chio surface is a one-line registerCommerceHandlers() addition plus a new src/main/ipc/commerce.ts; the pattern is already proven by existing security-flavored channels like agent-trust.ts ('agentTrust:markTrusted') and ai-vault.ts ('aiVault:listSessions').

Public CLI -> app transport is a documented JSON-RPC envelope (RuntimeRpcEnvelopeSchema in src/shared/runtime-rpc-envelope.ts: {id, ok, result|error, _meta.runtimeId}) sent over a Unix domain socket or Windows named pipe (src/cli/runtime/transport.ts via findTransport(metadata,'unix','named-pipe')). CLI command surface is declared as specs (src/cli/specs/*) + handlers (src/cli/handlers/*: worktree, repo, terminal, orchestration, browser, computer, automations, linear). Adding `orca commerce ...` verbs is additive in the same spec/handler pattern.

Agent-hooks subsystem is the per-agent interception bus: src/main/agent-hooks/server.ts runs a hook server; per-agent services (claude/codex/gemini/cursor/copilot/grok/droid/amp/hermes/openclaude hook-service.ts) install a managed script into each coding agent that POSTs a versioned JSON body (ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION) on agent lifecycle/status events. AGENT_HOOK_TARGETS enumerates 12 supported agents. This is where a capability-gate / metering call could fire on every agent action.

Terminal daemon is a self-contained, already-isolated sidecar precedent: src/main/daemon/daemon-server.ts owns a net.createServer Unix-socket protocol with a randomUUID token written to a token file (chmod-restricted), NDJSON framing (src/main/daemon/ndjson.ts), session lifecycle, and stream fanout. A Chio Rust sidecar can mirror this exact pattern (token-authed local socket, length/NDJSON framing) for low-friction, auditable integration.

Secrets/identity primitives already present to bind to Chio trust crates: src/main/ai-vault (scans agent session transcripts), src/main/runtime/e2ee-keypair.ts + e2ee-channel.ts + e2ee-crypto.ts (end-to-end-encrypted device channel using tweetnacl, used for the mobile pairing flow), src/main/runtime/device-registry.ts. These map onto chio-did / chio-credentials / chio-tee for agent identity and attested channels.

Usage/rate-limit/accounting scaffolding already exists per provider: src/main/rate-limits/ (claude/codex usage fetchers), src/main/claude-usage, src/main/codex-usage, src/main/opencode-usage stores, src/main/ipc/rate-limits.ts, and mobile AccountUsage.tsx. This is a natural host for chio-metering and chio-credit budget/mandate display.

Mobile companion (mobile/, 266 files) is an Expo Router React-Native app with routes for sessions, review, source-control, files, tasks, accounts, and a QR-code device pairing flow (pair.tsx/pair-scan.tsx/pair-confirm.tsx) plus a custom native two-way-audio module (Swift ios/ + Kotlin android/). It already renders per-account usage and can monitor/steer agents, so it can surface budgets, mandates, and signed-receipt approvals from a phone.

Native build + agent-driving skills already shipped: native/computer-use-macos is a Swift Package (computer use), native/computer-use-linux/windows runtimes; skills/orca-cli/SKILL.md documents the agent-facing CLI contract (orca status/worktree/terminal/browser --json), proving the product already treats agents as first-class CLI operators that a commerce layer can extend.
gaps: No economic primitives anywhere in Orca: zero pricing, payments, settlement, budgets, mandates, ledgers, or receipts. 'usage'/'rate-limit' modules only read provider quota (Claude/Codex tokens), they do not meter, price, or charge for tool calls. There is no money concept in the codebase.

No capability-based security or signed-decision mediation. agent-trust.ts only writes per-agent 'trust this folder' artifacts to silence first-launch prompts; it is not a capability authority, has no time-bounding, scoping, revocation, or cryptographic tokens. Nothing equivalent to the Chio kernel mediating tool calls with verifiable capabilities.

No append-only / Merkle / attested audit log. Telemetry is PostHog analytics (posthog-node) and there is crash-reporting and a stats collector, but no tamper-evident receipt log, no signed decision records, no lineage. The chio-web3 settlement_proof / receipt-log model has no counterpart.

No Rust anywhere in the tree (languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, Swift, CSS, HTML, PowerShell, Python, Kotlin, Ruby, Batchfile - no Rust). There is no existing native-module build path for a Rust binary/N-API addon; the Chio sidecar would introduce the first Rust toolchain, electron-builder packaging entry, and code-signing/notarization step for a Rust artifact.

No external protocol mediation layer (no MCP/A2A/ACP/OpenAPI gateway). Orca launches agents and drives a browser; it does not sit between an agent and arbitrary tool servers as a policy/guard enforcement point, which is exactly what Chio protocol adapters + guards provide.

No agent-to-agent value transfer or shared-balance concept. Orca's 'parallel worktrees' fan a prompt across N agents and merge a winner, but agents are siloed processes with no notion of paying each other, holding budgets, or settling balances between worktrees/agents.

The agent-hooks bus is fire-and-forget status reporting (best-effort JSON POST, version-tolerant), not a synchronous allow/deny gate. To make it a fail-closed capability check, the hook contract would need to become blocking/decision-returning, which is a wire-protocol change (the codebase explicitly reserves the next ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump for a real wire change).

Operational cost of tracking the fork is high: ~5,120 files, version 1.4.70-rc.0 shipping daily (pushed_at within a day of inspection, 421 open issues, 334 forks), with heavy bespoke tooling (config/scripts/* for native runtime, localization catalogs for es/zh/ja/ko, macOS entitlements/notarization, electron-builder per-OS). A rebrand is easy; staying merged with upstream is a continuous maintenance burden.

No deep-link / custom-URL-protocol handler was found in src/main/index.ts or electron-builder config, so a hosted-payment redirect flow (return-from-bank / OAuth-style settlement callback) would need a new protocol-client registration (e.g. chio://) to be added.

License attribution detail: the repo description and homepage use 'Orca' but the LICENSE copyright holder is 'Lovecast Inc.' (not stablyai). A rebrand must preserve the Lovecast Inc. MIT notice in retained files; only net-new Chio files can carry a fresh copyright.
opportunities: Ship a Chio commerce sidecar as a signed Rust binary launched by Electron main, mirroring the existing terminal daemon pattern (token file + local Unix-socket/named-pipe, NDJSON/length-framed). Expose it to the UI through one new src/main/ipc/commerce.ts registered in register-core-handlers.ts (a 'commerce:*' namespace), and to agents through new `orca commerce ...` CLI verbs in src/cli/specs + src/cli/handlers. This reuses three already-audited transport patterns and adds zero new attack surface shape.

Turn the agent-hooks bus into a fail-closed capability gate: extend the managed hook script + hook-service contract (bump ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION) so each agent tool call calls the Chio kernel for an allow/deny decision before proceeding, backed by chio-capability tokens (Capability Authority) and native guards. This makes Orca the first ADE where every agent action is capability-mediated, evaluated by guards, and signed - a defensible moat over plain agent runners.

Add a per-worktree / per-agent budget and mandate panel in the renderer, fed by chio-credit (capital_and_execution) and chio-metering, reusing the existing rate-limit/usage UI surface (src/main/rate-limits, mobile AccountUsage.tsx). Each parallel agent runs under a signed spending mandate; when an agent buys a tool/data/compute call it is metered (chio-metering), priced (chio-market/chio-appraisal), and debited against its budget, with overspend failing closed.

Bind agent identity to chio-did + chio-credentials using Orca's existing tweetnacl e2ee keypair/device-registry (src/main/runtime/e2ee-keypair.ts, device-registry.ts). Each agent/worktree gets a DID and verifiable credentials; the mobile pairing QR flow (mobile/app/pair*.tsx) becomes the human-approval step that mints a time-bounded mandate credential, so a phone tap authorizes an agent's spend.

Make every Chio decision a Merkle-committed receipt (chio-web3 anchors/settlement/settlement_proof, Receipt Log) and add an 'Attested Receipts' tab next to the existing AI-diff review UI (src/renderer review surfaces, mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx). Users review not just code diffs but the signed economic+capability decisions an agent made, with cryptographic audit trail - directly leverages the compliance docs (PCI-DSS v4, EU AI Act, ISO 42001) Chio already has.

Use Chio protocol adapters (MCP/A2A/ACP/OpenAPI wrappers) to make Orca's embedded browser and external tool calls into mediated, metered Chio tool servers. The embedded Chromium 'Design Mode' and agent-browser become priced/guarded resources: an agent buying a paid API call or data pull goes through a Chio-wrapped adapter that enforces policy and emits a receipt.

Enable agent-to-agent settlement across parallel worktrees via chio-settle / chio-link / chio-anchor: when 'fan across N agents, merge the winner' runs, losing agents that produced reused intermediate artifacts can be credited, and a shared worktree-group balance is settled with signed proofs - turning Orca's existing parallel-orchestration UX into a marketplace of cooperating agents.

Add an enterprise-grade signed manifest + SIEM/lineage layer using chio-manifest (signed tool manifests), the guards/observability SIEM export, and chio-store-sqlite, surfaced through Orca's existing enterprise_export-style flows and src/main/observability. Sells to regulated buyers who need provable, exportable audit of what autonomous agents bought and did - a clear differentiator over MIT agent runners with no compliance story.

Expose a phone-side approval/notification loop for high-value spend: reuse the mobile companion's existing 'notify when agent finishes' + steer-from-phone capability to push a signed-mandate approval ('Agent X wants to spend $Y on compute') that the user approves with the two-way-audio/native module, gating settlement through chio-governance. This is autonomous commerce with a human circuit-breaker, defensible and demo-friendly.

Stand up a metered Chio tool/data marketplace inside the CLI (chio-market + chio-underwriting + chio-appraisal): `orca commerce buy <tool>` / `orca commerce price <resource>` lets agents discover, price, underwrite, and purchase capabilities at runtime, settled via chio-web3 - making the forked product not just where agents run, but where they transact, which no current fork target offers.

grounding.summary: Agentic commerce went from concept to shipping infrastructure across 2025-2026, and the standards are stacking into complementary layers rather than one winner: ACP (OpenAI + Stripe, the checkout/merchant layer, Apache-2.0, live in ChatGPT Instant Checkout), AP2 (Google + 60-100 orgs, the trust/mandate/authorization layer built on cryptographically-signed Intent/Cart/Payment mandates), and x402 (Coinbase + Cloudflare, now a Linux Foundation project, the per-call execution/micropayment layer on stablecoins, ~165M tx and adopted by AWS Bedrock AgentCore Payments in May 2026). The card networks (Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Agent Pay/Agentic Tokens) and wallets (Skyfire KYA/KYAPay, Nekuda, Payman, PayPal agent-ready) are racing to issue scoped, agent-bound credentials and staged wallets. Identity is consolidating around DIDs/VCs, W3C Agent Identity CG, DIF MCP-I, and on-chain ERC-8004 (live on Ethereum mainnet 29 Jan 2026). The decisive, unfilled white space is NOT another payment rail: it is the out-of-agent enforcement, attestation, and audit layer. The market openly admits enforcement must live outside agent code (the widely-cited "$47,000 runaway LangChain agent" with dashboards but no kill-switch), that audit-trail standards for AI-generated logs do not exist, and that dispute/liability evidence is untested in courts. That gap maps almost one-to-one onto Chio's kernel, receipt log, guards, capability authority, and commerce/trust crates - and Chio's chio-commerce-order already binds AP2 mandate hashes and the ACP delegated-payment-token hash in a single signed ledger, positioning it as the neutral verifier across all three stacks rather than a competitor to any of them.
capabilities: ACP (Agentic Commerce Protocol), OpenAI + Stripe, released Apache-2.0 on 29 Sep 2025: agent-initiated checkout where a narrowly-scoped Shared Payment Token (SPT) is handed to the merchant who stays merchant-of-record and charges via any compliant PSP; ships a Delegated Payments Spec so non-Stripe processors can participate. Powered ChatGPT Instant Checkout (Etsy + ~dozen Shopify brands); PayPal joined as provider 28 Oct 2025; Stripe shipped an Agentic Commerce Suite 11 Dec 2025.

AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol), Google-led with 60+ (now 100+) orgs, announced Sep 2025: payment-method-agnostic, does not move money but produces verifiable authorization records via a chain of three cryptographically-signed mandates - Intent Mandate (user delegates authority), Cart Mandate (user approves specific cart + price), Payment Mandate (credential the network sees). Co-launched a Conversational Commerce Agent with PayPal 27 Oct 2025. Spec at ap2-protocol.org.

x402 (Coinbase + Cloudflare), open-sourced May 2025, donated to the Linux Foundation x402 Foundation 2 Apr 2026: revives HTTP 402 so a server replies 402 Payment Required, the agent signs a stablecoin (USDC, mostly Base/Solana) payment, attaches proof, and retries. Reference impl Apache-2.0 with TS/Python/Go SDKs and Express/Fastify/Next.js adapters. ~69k active agents, ~165M tx, ~$50M cumulative volume by Apr 2026; Stripe integrated Feb 2026.

x402 Bazaar: an MCP-server discovery layer / machine-readable catalog where agents find and call 10,000+ paid endpoints and pay per call in USDC, no accounts or subscriptions - the emerging agent-to-agent tool marketplace.

Card networks shipped agent rails: Visa Intelligent Commerce (scoped tokenized credentials for agents, issuer-side machine-payment auth, integrations with Anthropic/OpenAI/Microsoft) plus Intelligent Commerce Connect (one merchant integration spanning four protocols). Mastercard Agent Pay with Agentic Tokens binds a tokenized card credential to a specific agent + merchant scope + consent policy; first live agentic transaction 29 Sep 2025.

Agent wallets / KYA startups: Skyfire (Know Your Agent identity + KYAPay merchant-side accept, stablecoin micropayments, demoed with Visa Intelligent Commerce Dec 2025); Nekuda (secure agent wallet + agentic mandates, $5M from Madrona/Amex/Visa Ventures); Payman (per-agent wallets over ACH + stablecoin); PayPal agent-ready for existing merchants.

Agent identity standards: W3C DID + Verifiable Credentials as the base; W3C Agent Identity Registry Protocol Community Group; DIF MCP-I (donated Mar 2026) extending identity to MCP agents; TRAIL did:trail draft method; and on-chain ERC-8004 'Trustless Agents' (live Ethereum mainnet 29 Jan 2026) with Identity, Reputation, and Validation registries, authored across MetaMask/Ethereum Foundation/Google/Coinbase as a trustless extension of A2A.

Hyperscaler enablement: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Payments (preview May 2026) gives agents their own wallets via Coinbase + Stripe to pay for APIs, MCP servers, web content, and other agents mid-execution using USDC over x402; AgentCore Identity + Microsoft Entra Agent ID provide OAuth/credential vaulting and agent-on-behalf-of authorization.

Chio already speaks these standards: crates/platform/chio-commerce-order/src/mandate.rs defines a signed CommerceMandateLedger carrying ap2_checkout_mandate_hash, ap2_payment_mandate_hash, and acp_delegated_payment_token_hash with occurrence/single-use limits and validity-window enforcement against payment capture time - i.e. Chio binds AP2 and ACP artifacts into one verifiable allowance ledger.

Chio has commerce/trust crates that go beyond payments: economy (chio-credit capital_and_execution, chio-open-market with bidding/bonds/penalties/fee-schedules, chio-market, chio-settle, chio-metering, chio-web3 settlement_proof, chio-autonomy, chio-listing), trust (chio-attest-buyer buyer-side proof packets + receipt-lineage bundles, chio-did, chio-credentials, chio-reputation, chio-pheromone trust signals, chio-tee, chio-revocation-oracle), platform (chio-transaction-passport with an evidence_graph + runtime-security report, chio-risk-comptroller, chio-manifest signed tool manifests), all under a fail-closed kernel + append-only Merkle receipt log.
gaps: No standard owns out-of-agent runtime ENFORCEMENT. The market consensus (Focused Labs, Oracle, Ravoid, the '$47k runaway LangChain agent' case) is that dashboards/alerts/provider caps are observability, not control, and the kill/narrow/reroute decision must live outside agent code as a trace-linked runtime loop. AP2/ACP/x402 define authorization and payment artifacts but explicitly do NOT enforce budgets or revoke capabilities at call time.

No accepted audit-trail standard for AI-generated logs, and code-based authorization trails are untested before courts and regulators; consumers may lack standard dispute rights for agentic purchases. Tamper-evident, replayable, cross-party receipts are an open problem the payment protocols punt on.

Identity, mandate, payment, reputation, and discovery are fragmented across different orgs and layers (ACP vs AP2 vs x402 vs ERC-8004 vs card tokens vs KYA). No neutral verifier ties an AP2 mandate, an ACP/SPT token, an x402 settlement proof, and an agent DID/VC into one signed, attested execution record.

Payment players assume a 'verified agent' and a 'pre-authorized mandate' exist but provide thin tooling to prove the agent's runtime was sandboxed, the tool manifest was signed, the guard policy actually ran, and the capability was unrevoked at execution time - the attestation/TEE/manifest layer.

x402 Bazaar-style agent-to-agent marketplaces handle discovery + pay-per-call but have no built-in quality bonds, slashing/penalties for bad service, or reputation slashing tied to receipts - i.e. economic accountability for sellers in an agent tool market.

Most surfaces are crypto-rail-first (x402/USDC) or closed consumer surfaces (ChatGPT Instant Checkout, which was retired Mar 2026 after ~a dozen merchants). There is no developer-first, open, rail-agnostic cockpit that treats attested commerce as a first-class workflow with local audit and review.
No tooling binds the human-in-the-loop approval moment (the AP2 'consent and intent ambiguity' dispute driver) to a cryptographic, reviewable artifact a developer can inspect and replay later.
opportunities: Position the forked Orca cockpit as the neutral, rail-agnostic VERIFIER and audit plane across ACP + AP2 + x402, not a competing wallet. chio-commerce-order already ingests ap2_checkout_mandate_hash, ap2_payment_mandate_hash, and acp_delegated_payment_token_hash; surface a per-worktree 'Commerce' panel that shows every agent purchase as a verified mandate->payment->receipt chain and lets the reviewer replay it.

Own the white space everyone admits is missing: out-of-agent ENFORCEMENT. Wire the kernel + capability authority + guards (chio-credit capital_and_execution, chio-risk-comptroller, chio-autonomy) as the trace-linked runtime loop that refuses the next paid tool call when a budget/mandate is exhausted. Sell this directly against the '$47k runaway agent' story: Orca-Chio agents cannot overspend because enforcement is in the kernel, not the prompt. Expose it in the Orca account/usage panel as hard per-worktree spend mandates, and via the Orca CLI (e.g. a `chio budget`/`mandate` verb agents and operators can set/inspect).

Make Chio's append-only Merkle receipt log + chio-transaction-passport (evidence_graph + runtime-security report) the tamper-evident audit trail the market lacks. Every agent transaction yields a signed passport binding the AP2 mandate, the settlement proof (chio-web3 settlement_proof), the sandbox/TEE attestation, the signed tool manifest (chio-manifest), and the unrevoked-capability proof - exportable for disputes (chio-enterprise-export, SIEM) and defensible in the untested legal/regulatory setting.

Differentiate on BUYER-side attestation, which the payment crowd ignores. chio-attest-buyer already produces buyer attestation packets and receipt-lineage bundles; let a Chio agent prove to a merchant/another agent that it is a genuine, mandate-backed, sandboxed paying customer (a credible open answer to Skyfire KYA / Mastercard Agentic Tokens) without locking into a single network's token.

Turn chio-open-market (bidding, bonds, penalties, fee_schedule, slashing) into an accountable agent-to-agent tool marketplace that is strictly better than x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray model: sellers post bonds, bad service is penalized via signed evidence, and reputation (chio-reputation + chio-pheromone trust signals) is slashed and re-priced from receipts. Make it interoperable by letting listings be priced/settled over x402/USDC (chio-web3) or card rails while Chio mediates and attests.

Bind the human consent moment to a cryptographic artifact, attacking AP2's 'consent and intent ambiguity' dispute driver. Reuse Orca's mobile companion + notifications so a high-value agent purchase pushes an approval to the user's phone that mints a signed Chio approval receipt (a verifiable Cart/Intent-Mandate-equivalent) before the kernel releases the capability.

Mediate any rail via the protocol adapters: wrap x402 endpoints, ACP merchant flows, and MCP paid tools (chio-mcp-adapter, chio-openapi-mcp-bridge, chio-a2a-adapter, chio-hosted-mcp) as Chio tool servers so the Design-Mode/quick-open surfaces let an agent discover and buy a tool while the kernel meters, prices (chio-metering, chio-appraisal), enforces, and signs it - one cockpit over all standards.

Bridge the 'Mullet Economy': front-of-app compliant AP2/ACP/card rails for human-facing buys, back-of-app x402/stablecoin for high-volume B2B agent-to-agent, with Chio as the single attested settlement+audit substrate (chio-settle, chio-anchor, chio-web3 anchors) spanning both - a developer-first, open, MIT-cockpit + Rust-protocol alternative to the closed hyperscaler stacks (AgentCore Payments, Visa/Mastercard).

Lean into enterprise/compliance as wedge: Chio's existing EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 / PCI-DSS v4 / OWASP-LLM mappings plus signed receipts directly answer the regulatory-uncertainty and 'move agents from PoC to production' blockers cited as the main brake on agentic commerce in 2026.
key_facts: ACP (OpenAI + Stripe) released Apache-2.0 on 29 Sep 2025; introduced the Shared Payment Token (SPT) so apps like ChatGPT initiate payment without exposing buyer credentials; ChatGPT Instant Checkout launched with Etsy then Shopify brands but was retired Mar 2026 after ~a dozen merchants shipped, while the protocol continued (PayPal provider 28 Oct 2025, Stripe Agentic Commerce Suite 11 Dec 2025).

Industry framing: ACP/AP2/x402 are complementary layers (checkout / trust+authorization / execution), not rivals; analysts predict a 'Mullet Economy' - compliant AP2/ACP/card rails for consumer front-end, x402/crypto for high-volume B2B back-end.

Visa Intelligent Commerce issues scoped tokenized agent credentials and added Intelligent Commerce Connect (one integration across four protocols); Mastercard Agent Pay binds Agentic Tokens to agent + merchant scope + consent policy, with its first live agentic transaction 29 Sep 2025.

grounding.summary:
Autonomous-agent commerce sits on a payments stack built for humans, and that mismatch is the central design constraint. Custody is the bright line: hold or move user funds and you are a money transmitter (FinCEN MSB plus state MTLs, unlicensed is a felony under 18 U.S.C. 1960, 50-state licensing about 250k-350k), while genuine non-custodial software is not. Stablecoins are now regulated (US GENIUS Act enacted July 18 2025, EU MiCA) with 1:1 reserves, restricted issuance and custody, and no yield, and KYC and AML assume a human principal an agent cannot be. Card networks (Mastercard Agent Pay, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol) ship verified-agent rails but agent chargeback and dispute liability is explicitly unsettled and networks will not absorb losses they did not authorize. The lowest-friction legal path stays out of the flow of funds with a licensed custody and KYC partner, settles over regulated stablecoin or card rails, and enforces signed spending mandates with full audit trails so a regulated principal is always accountable.</summary>
<key_facts>["sacrificial buffer entry that absorbs the parser boundary; the substantive facts are carried in capabilities, gaps, and opportunities"]
capabilities: Money transmission gates everything: custody or transmit value and you need FinCEN MSB plus state MTLs; unlicensed is a felony under 18 U.S.C. 1960 (up to 250k, 5 years) and 50-state licensing is about 250k-350k plus bonds and AML. Under GENIUS only supervised entities (banks, trust companies, custodians) may custody stablecoins, reserves, or keys, holding customer assets as customer property.

Custody is the bright line: a hosted or custodial wallet that can move user funds is a money transmitter under FinCEN 2019 guidance and most states; non-custodial software without unilateral control generally is not. Stablecoin law is live: GENIUS (July 18 2025) needs permitted issuers, 100 percent 1:1 reserves, BSA and AML, and no yield; MiCA makes fiat stablecoins E-Money Tokens needing a credit or e-money institution, and custody and transfer need CASP authorization across 27 states (PSD2 license may also apply from March 2026).

Card networks built agent rails with a human in the chain: Mastercard Agent Pay binds an Agentic Token to agent, merchant scope, and consent policy, and Visa Trusted Agent Protocol verifies agents; both require agent verification and consumer-set spending limits. Agents use stablecoin rails: x402 over HTTP 402, plus Coinbase AgentKit, Stripe, Crossmint, Privy, and Turnkey wallets (Crossmint holds MiCA CASP in all 27 EU states). Ways to avoid money transmission: non-custodial design, agent-of-payee exemption (about 22 states), merchant-of-record or payfac, and BaaS with For-Benefit-Of accounts at an MTL-exempt partner bank.
gaps: No regulatory identity for agents: KYC, AML, and Travel Rule assume a human or entity, so an agent cannot satisfy them itself; GENIUS, MiCA, and VARA do not address an agent as the transacting party.

Chargeback and dispute liability for agent payments is undefined, no agent-specific reason codes exist, and networks will not absorb losses they did not authorize; whether Reg E covers a consumer delegating a card to an agent is unsettled, and merchants lose their usual fraud evidence so many disputes are confusion not fraud.

Accountability fragments across developer, deployer, user, and wallet provider (a roughly 450k erroneous transfer was blamed on an agent session crash with no clear liable party), poisoned oracles and prompt injection to sanctioned addresses are an unguarded attack surface no AML framework covers, and GENIUS no-yield plus licensed-issuer-only issuance blocks minting your own token or float without a partner or charter.
opportunities: Chio identity crates (chio-did, chio-credentials, chio-attest-verify) bind each agent to a KYC-verified human or business principal via a DID plus verifiable credential, exactly what Mastercard Agentic Tokens, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, and Travel Rule require.

Capability tokens at the kernel enforce card-network consent and the standard control set (spending limits, approved addresses, auto-escalation) with an agent-merchant-amount-time binding checked by guards before money moves (chio-credit capital_and_execution); the Merkle receipt log plus chio-web3 settlement_proof and lineage give regulator-grade audit and chargeback evidence.

Stay non-custodial and delegate custody, KYC, and AML to a licensed partner (CASP like Crossmint, BaaS partner bank with FBO accounts, or chartered trust) to avoid 18 U.S.C. 1960 and the 250k-350k MTL build; settle over regulated rails (GENIUS stablecoins, x402, tokenized card credentials) wrapped as Chio tool servers, add guards plus data-input monitoring as a fail-closed perimeter, and productize revocable chio-credit budget mandates as a per-agent wallet in the Orca cockpit while chio-reputation, chio-metering, and chio-underwriting price agent-to-agent access on a licensed rail.

ideas.title: Per-worktree capability wallet derived from one budget tree
ideas.one_liner: Every Orca worktree boots with its own did:chio key and a scoped, cost-capped wallet that is a leaf in a single org-to-agent BudgetTree, so spend is hard-capped at four levels before any paid tool fires.
ideas.description: When Orca creates a git worktree it already mints an e2ee keypair (src/main/runtime/e2ee-keypair.ts); reuse it as a did:chio subject and register the worktree as a leaf BudgetNode under team/dept/org parents. The Chio sidecar evaluates BudgetTree::evaluate against a durable SpendSnapshot on every metered call and returns BudgetDecision::Deny with the closest-to-root offender, so an agent that exhausts its slice (or whose parent dept is capped) fails closed. The wallet itself is a ChioScope with max_invocations / max_cost_per_invocation / max_total_cost bound to that subject key, rendered as a wallet chip in the worktree sidebar showing remaining() over max_total. Because the cap is enforced in the kernel and not the prompt, this is the direct, demoable answer to the 47k runaway-agent story.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-metering BudgetTree / BudgetNode (budget_hierarchy.rs), chio-core-types ChioScope cost caps (scope.rs), chio-did
ideas.orca_surface: New src/main/ipc/commerce.ts (commerce:* namespace) feeding a per-worktree wallet chip in the renderer sidebar next to the existing rate-limit/usage panels; worktree-create path in src/main wires the leaf node.
ideas.user_value: A user can hand an autonomous agent a worktree knowing the absolute most it can ever spend is fixed at create time, with per-dept and per-org ceilings above it, and can watch the meter drain live.
ideas.moat: Orca has zero money concept and only reads provider quota; a four-level parent-capped, fail-closed monetary tree bound to a per-worktree DID key is not reproducible without the whole chio-metering + capability stack.
ideas.risk: Needs a durable, concurrency-safe SpendSnapshot store (the crate is explicitly storage-agnostic) so N parallel worktrees draft atomically; today BudgetTree::evaluate takes a caller-supplied snapshot.

ideas.title: Phone-tap mandate that mints a time-boxed, cost-capped capability lease
ideas.one_liner: A high-value agent purchase pushes an approval to the Orca mobile app; the user's tap signs a CapabilityLeaseArtifact that becomes the kernel-enforced spend authority for exactly that scope and window.
ideas.description: Reuse Orca's existing QR device-pairing and notification loop (mobile/app/pair*.tsx) as the human-consent surface. When an agent requests spend above a threshold, the sidecar emits a pending CapabilityLeaseArtifact (chio-governance) over a scope_digest with an action_class (DelegatedAction / NarrowDestructive) and an issued_at/expires_at window; the phone tap is the issuer signature. verify_capability_lease then gates the next capital draw, and the lease id flows into CapitalAllocationDecisionArtifact.approval_token_id so the approval is cryptographically joined to the funds movement. This binds the AP2 consent moment to a verifiable, replayable artifact, attacking AP2's documented consent-ambiguity dispute driver.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-governance CapabilityLeaseArtifact + verify_capability_lease (lease.rs), chio-credit CapitalAllocationDecisionArtifact.approval_token_id
ideas.orca_surface: Mobile companion approval card (mobile/app, reusing pair/notification flow); desktop shows a pending-mandate row in the worktree commerce panel.
ideas.user_value: Autonomous spend stays unattended until it crosses a line the user set, then a single phone tap authorizes precisely one scoped, time-bounded grant - a human circuit-breaker, not a blanket allowance.
ideas.moat: The same key that the user taps is the issuer the kernel verifies and that the capital decision references; that consent-to-enforcement chain is unique to Chio's signed-artifact model and impossible to fake from a dashboard toggle.
ideas.risk: Requires the agent-hooks bus to become a blocking allow/deny gate (a wire-protocol change, ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump) so the call actually waits for the lease; latency of the round-trip to a phone must be handled.

ideas.title: Per-agent autonomy dial gated by a bonded-execution control policy
ideas.one_liner: An autonomy slider on each agent (Direct / Delegated / Autonomous) maps to a CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy, so higher unattended-spend tiers demand a posted bond, a locked reserve, and a higher runtime-assurance tier before the kernel lets the agent transact.
ideas.description: GovernedAutonomyTier already ladders Direct->Delegated->Autonomous with rising minimum RuntimeAssuranceTier. Surface it as a dial; the selected tier configures a CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (maximum_autonomy_tier, minimum_runtime_assurance_tier, require_locked_reserve, deny_if_bond_not_active, deny_if_outstanding_delinquency). The sidecar evaluates it before each paid call and returns CreditBondedExecutionDecision::Deny with typed findings (ReserveNotLocked, RuntimeAssuranceBelowAutonomyMinimum, OutstandingDelinquency). A global kill_switch on the policy is the fleet-wide stop button. Crucially, CreditBondedExecutionSimulationReport lets the UI preview the decision delta before flipping the dial, so an operator sees exactly what raising a tier would newly allow or block.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy + CreditBondedExecutionEvaluation + simulation report (capital_and_execution.rs), chio-core-types GovernedAutonomyTier (governance.rs)
ideas.orca_surface: Per-agent settings card in the renderer (an autonomy dial plus a fleet-level kill-switch toggle in the top bar); simulation delta shown inline before apply.
ideas.user_value: Operators trade autonomy for assurance on a single control: letting an agent spend unattended at the top tier provably requires a bond, a locked reserve, and an attested runtime, and one switch halts the whole fleet.
ideas.moat: Tying an unattended-spend tier to a posted bond, a reserve lock, delinquency state, and a TEE-grade runtime assurance tier, with a shadow simulation of the policy change, is a capital-governance primitive no agent runner has.
ideas.risk: require_locked_reserve and the bond lifecycle are accounting-authoritative but custody-neutral; the locked reserve is real only once a settlement rail (chio-settle crypto) or external custodian actually holds it.

ideas.title: Fan-out budget pool that pre-rejects over-allocation before any agent runs
ideas.one_liner: When a user fans one prompt across N agents, Orca materializes a WorkflowPreflightPlan so the N worktrees draw capped slices of one shared pool, and the orchestration is refused client-side if the slices exceed the pool.
ideas.description: Orca's signature move is fan-one-prompt-across-N-agents, merge the winner. Map it onto chio-workflow-preflight: a WorkflowBudgetPool with a parent_task and child_tasks, each carrying budget_minor in a coherent currency. The preflight validation rejects with workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded before a single agent starts if the children over-allocate the pool. Each child slice then instantiates a worktree wallet (idea 1) via budget_share_bps on the issued capability token, so the parent budget splits proportionally and no losing branch can overrun the shared envelope. The result is shown as a pool gauge above the parallel-worktree grid.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-workflow-preflight WorkflowBudgetPool / WorkflowPreflightPlan (types.rs), chio-core-types budget_share_bps on CapabilityToken
ideas.orca_surface: The parallel-worktrees / fan-out launch dialog and the worktree grid header (a shared-pool gauge), in the renderer orchestration surface.
ideas.user_value: A user can say spend at most X total across these 8 attempts and trust that the split is enforced and validated before launch, never discovering an overrun after 8 agents already burned budget.
ideas.moat: A currency-coherent, parent-and-children pre-validated budget pool wired to the exact fan-out UX Orca already ships is a one-to-one fit competitors cannot match without the preflight + capability budget-share primitives.
ideas.risk: Preflight only validates the plan shape and pool coherence; converting an approved plan into live per-worktree draws still needs the durable shared ledger from idea 1 to enforce slices at runtime.

ideas.title: Time-boxed wallet leases with one-click revocation and a live spend ledger
ideas.one_liner: Each wallet grant is a capability token with an expires_at and a RestrictTimeWindow caveat; a Revoke button kills it instantly, and every spend posts a signed IOU into a per-agent ledger view.
ideas.description: CapabilityToken already carries issued_at/expires_at and supports a RestrictTimeWindow caveat, so a wallet can be granted for, say, the next 2 hours of a work session and auto-expire. A Revoke control disables the leaf BudgetNode (enabled: false denies the whole subtree) and lets the token lapse, giving immediate fail-closed cutoff without waiting for expiry. Meanwhile chio-credit's CreditEvaluatorHook mints a signed IouEnvelope (chio.credit.iou-envelope.v1) on every finalized paid receipt, binding amount_units/currency to the receipt id; the commerce panel renders these as a running ledger of what the agent actually spent, line by line, each cryptographically tied to its receipt. This turns budgets from a static cap into a time-bounded, revocable, fully-itemized wallet.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-core-types CapabilityToken expires_at + RestrictTimeWindow caveat (token.rs, caveat.rs), chio-metering BudgetNode enabled flag, chio-credit CreditEvaluatorHook / IouEnvelope (hook.rs)
ideas.orca_surface: A wallet detail drawer in the worktree commerce panel: TTL countdown, a Revoke button, and a scrolling signed-IOU spend ledger; mirrored read-only on mobile AccountUsage.
ideas.user_value: Authority is grantable for a window, killable on a whim, and every dollar an agent spent is itemized with a verifiable receipt link, so revocation is instant and the spend trail is audit-grade.
ideas.moat: Time-boxed expiry plus subtree-disable revocation plus per-spend signed IOUs is a wallet whose every line item is independently verifiable - a property card-network agent wallets and dashboards structurally lack.
ideas.risk: Caveats today are documented as not enforced by admission (rejected fail-closed) for plain v1 tokens, so RestrictTimeWindow enforcement must be wired into the sidecar gate rather than assumed; revocation latency depends on the sidecar being in the call path.
