ideas.bold_bet: Make the Orca per-agent autonomy dial a hardware-grade capital governor: the slider from Direct to Autonomous is not a UI preference but a CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy the kernel enforces before every paid tool call, where unattended spend at the top tier is provably impossible unless the agent has a posted bond, a locked reserve, no outstanding delinquency, and a TEE-attested runtime - with a CreditBondedExecutionSimulationReport showing the operator exactly what raising the dial would newly permit, and a single fleet-wide kill_switch that halts all agent spend instantly. This converts the market's admitted white space (out-of-agent runtime enforcement, the 47k runaway-agent problem) into a one-control product surface no MIT agent runner can ship, because it requires Chio's bonded-execution, autonomy-tier, runtime-assurance, and signed-receipt stack underneath.

ideas.title: Bazaar with bonds: a quick-open marketplace where the price tag is signed and the seller has posted slashable collateral
ideas.one_liner: An in-cockpit tool/data/compute marketplace where every listing carries an operator-signed price + SLA + live revocation rate, and only sellers who posted a slashable bond can rank above 'public untrusted'.
ideas.description: Replace x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray model. A new 'Marketplace' tab (and `orca commerce search --scope tools:search --max-price 50 --json`) calls chio-listing::discovery::search() over GenericListingReport sets, pairing each surviving listing with its SignedListingPricingHint (price_per_call, ListingSla{max_latency_ms, availability_bps, throughput_rps}, revocation_rate_bps, recent_receipts_volume). Sellers are ranked by chio-listing GenericTrustAdmissionClass: PublicUntrusted listings render greyed and unbuyable until the agent explicitly trust-activates, BondBacked listings (those covered by a chio-open-market OpenMarketBondRequirement{slashable:true}) get a green 'bonded' badge and float to the top. The whole surface stays visibility-only (GenericListingBoundary enforces explicit_trust_activation_required), so listing is never the same act as trusting. The differentiator vs every competitor: the seller has money at stake that chio-open-market::penalty can SlashBond on signed evidence of FraudulentListing/UnverifiableListingBehavior.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-listing (discovery::search, ListingPricingHint, ListingSla, GenericTrustAdmissionClass, GenericListingBoundary); chio-open-market (fee_schedule::OpenMarketBondRequirement, penalty::OpenMarketPenaltyAction::SlashBond)
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Marketplace' tab reachable from quick-open (Cmd-K -> 'find a tool'); new `orca commerce search/compare` CLI verbs in src/cli/specs + src/cli/handlers; bonded/untrusted badges in the listing rows
ideas.user_value: An agent (or human) can discover a metered tool/dataset/API at runtime and instantly see who is financially accountable for it, instead of trusting an anonymous endpoint. Bad sellers lose their bond, so the marketplace self-cleans.
ideas.moat: x402 Bazaar, AgentCore Payments, and card-network agent rails have discovery + pay-per-call but no quality bonds, no slashing, and no signed SLA bound to the price. The bonded-vs-untrusted ranking on top of a fail-closed visibility-only surface is unique to Chio's listing+open-market crates and is hard to retrofit onto a pure payment rail.
ideas.risk: Needs a running registry that publishes/indexes GenericListingReports; the repo has the types and search but no live registry service, so the fork must stand up a thin signed-report aggregator (could start file/git-backed per workspace before a hosted registry).

ideas.title: True-cost meter: bill the agent on what the tool actually consumed, not a flat sticker price
ideas.one_liner: Every paid tool call an agent makes is metered along real cost dimensions (compute-ms, bytes, upstream API spend, warehouse bytes-scanned) and debited against the worktree budget, with the cost line shown inline in the diff review.
ideas.description: Manifests advertise a ToolPricing model (chio-manifest PricingModel::Flat/PerInvocation/PerUnit/Hybrid with base_price/unit_price/billing_unit). At call time the agent-hooks bus fires a post-invocation event that assembles a chio-metering CostMetadata from real CostDimension samples: ComputeTime{duration_ms}, DataVolume{bytes_read/written}, ApiCost{amount, provider}, and crucially WarehouseQuery{bytes_scanned, estimated_cost_usd} for BigQuery/Snowflake/Redshift pulls. For PerUnit/Hybrid listings the final charge is unit_price * measured units; that charge is debited through chio-metering BudgetEnforcer and, for fleets, the org->dept->team->agent BudgetTree, failing closed when a node is exhausted. The resulting cost lands on the signed receipt and renders as a '$0.0143 - 2.1M warehouse bytes scanned' line in Orca's annotate-AI-diffs pane next to the code the agent produced.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-metering (cost::CostDimension/CostMetadata, budget::BudgetEnforcer, budget_hierarchy::BudgetTree); chio-manifest (ToolPricing, PricingModel)
ideas.orca_surface: Agent-hooks subsystem (src/main/agent-hooks) as the per-tool-call metering hook; cost line rendered in the diff/annotate review pane (src/renderer review surfaces); per-worktree spend reflected in the usage panel (src/main/rate-limits)
ideas.user_value: Hybrid/usage-based pricing (the dominant model for real data + compute) is actually enforced, so a data pull that scans 2M rows costs more than one that scans 200, and the human reviewing the diff sees exactly what each agent action cost.
ideas.moat: Orca's existing 'usage' modules only read provider token quota; they cannot meter or charge for arbitrary tool calls. The WarehouseQuery cost dimension (dry-run bytes-scanned -> dollars) and the Hybrid unit metering tied to a signed manifest price is a Chio-native capability no agent runner has.
ideas.risk: CostMetadata is a container the host must fill; deriving true cost for an arbitrary CLI agent run needs per-tool collectors (token counts, GPU-seconds, vendor invoices). Start with the dimensions that are cheap to capture (warehouse dry-run, wall-clock, byte counts) and mark others best-effort.

ideas.title: Reputation-priced checkout: the same tool costs your agent less because your fleet behaves
ideas.one_liner: A buy flow that takes the seller's manifest base price and applies a deterministic reputation-tier discount to the agent's fleet before minting a scoped, cost-capped capability token for exactly that purchase.
ideas.description: When an agent clicks/calls buy on a marketplace listing, the cockpit computes the final price via chio-appraisal::marketplace_pricing::compute_marketplace_invocation_price, feeding a MarketplaceBasePrice from the manifest and a MarketplacePricingContext carrying the buyer's MarketplaceReputationTier (TIER_DISCOUNT_PER_HUNDRED = [0,5,10,20], so Tier3 fleets pay 20% less). The discounted quote is then handed to chio-open-market::bid(), which mints a scoped CapabilityToken (server_id/tool_name, max_invocations, max_cost_per_invocation = the quoted price, max_total_cost) bound to that worktree's agent key, and accept() only succeeds against a signature-verified VerifiedReservationReceipt covering the total liability. The result is a 'wallet chip' in the worktree sidebar showing the live capability the agent just bought and how much of its cap remains. Sellers reward trusted buyers automatically; the discount is reproducible and audit-preserved (applied_tier on the price record).
ideas.chio_capability: chio-appraisal (marketplace_pricing::compute_marketplace_invocation_price, MarketplaceReputationTier, TIER_DISCOUNT_PER_HUNDRED); chio-open-market (bidding::bid/accept, scoped CapabilityToken)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Buy' action on each marketplace listing row; `orca commerce buy <listing> --max-invocations N`; a per-worktree capability 'wallet' chip in the sidebar showing remaining cap
ideas.user_value: Pricing becomes dynamic and behavior-linked instead of one flat rate for everyone, and the purchase is automatically converted into a kernel-enforced spend ceiling so the agent can never exceed what it bought.
ideas.moat: Binding a deterministic, audit-preserved reputation discount directly to capability-token minting (price -> scoped, cost-capped token in one signed flow) is something only Chio's appraisal + open-market + capability crates can do; card networks issue tokens but do not reputation-price the buyer at mint time.
ideas.risk: Tier assignment must be trustworthy; if reputation is gameable the discount is exploitable. Mitigate by sourcing the tier from chio-reputation's Sybil-resistant per-feed-floor tiering rather than a self-asserted value.

ideas.title: List-to-sell wizard: turn any worktree tool into a signed, priced, underwritten marketplace listing in one command
ideas.one_liner: A seller-side flow that signs a tool manifest with a pricing model, attaches a pricing+SLA hint, picks a trust admission class, and gets a reputation-weighted credit ceiling on how much it is allowed to sell, all from `orca commerce list`.
ideas.description: The forked cockpit lets an operator publish a tool/dataset/compute endpoint as a first-class listing. The wizard (a) builds and Ed25519-signs a chio-manifest ToolManifest with a ToolPricing block (choose Flat / PerInvocation / PerUnit / Hybrid, set base_price/unit_price/billing_unit), (b) emits a SignedListingPricingHint (price_per_call + ListingSla + advertised revocation_rate_bps), (c) chooses a GenericTrustAdmissionClass and, for BondBacked, references the posted chio-open-market bond, and (d) runs chio-underwriting::marketplace_limits::compute_marketplace_credit_limit to set the seller's exposure ceiling (MARKETPLACE_TIER_LIMIT_UNITS = [10k,50k,250k,1M] minor units by tier, fail-closed to deny if the publisher is revoked on the sparse-Merkle root). The listing then appears in the Bazaar (idea 1). This is the supply side that makes the whole marketplace two-sided inside the same product agents already run in.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-manifest (ToolManifest signing, ToolPricing/PricingModel); chio-listing (discovery::SignedListingPricingHint, trust_activation::GenericTrustAdmissionClass); chio-underwriting (marketplace_limits::compute_marketplace_credit_limit, MARKETPLACE_TIER_LIMIT_UNITS)
ideas.orca_surface: `orca commerce list` CLI verb (src/cli/specs + handlers) plus a 'Publish listing' panel behind the new commerce:* IPC namespace; the signing step reuses Orca's tweetnacl keypair/device-registry
ideas.user_value: Anyone running agents can become a seller of a metered capability without leaving the cockpit, with the price model, SLA, and a fail-closed exposure cap all generated and signed for them.
ideas.moat: A signed-manifest + pricing-hint + admission-class + underwritten-ceiling pipeline as a one-command publish flow is unique; it makes Chio-on-Orca a two-sided marketplace, not just a buyer cockpit, and the underwriting ceiling (revocation-aware) has no analog in MIT agent runners.
ideas.risk: Two-sided liquidity is the classic cold-start problem; early on there are few sellers. Seed with first-party Chio-wrapped MCP/OpenAPI tools as listings so the Bazaar is non-empty on day one.

ideas.title: SLA receipts that re-price the market: measured latency/availability feed back into a seller's advertised hint
ideas.one_liner: Every metered call produces a signed receipt whose measured latency and success are aggregated against the seller's advertised ListingSla, and breaches automatically degrade the seller's ranking and can trigger a bond hold.
ideas.description: Sellers advertise a ListingSla (max_latency_ms, availability_bps, throughput_rps) and a revocation_rate_bps inside their SignedListingPricingHint. The cockpit's metering hook timestamps each call and writes the observed latency/outcome onto the signed receipt; a background watchdog rolls those receipts up per seller and compares them to the advertised SLA. When measured availability falls below availability_bps or latency exceeds max_latency_ms over the window, two things happen: the seller's effective rank in chio-listing::discovery drops (freshness_affects_ranking is already a search input), and a chio-open-market::penalty OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact{abuse_class: UnverifiableListingBehavior, action: HoldBond} is proposed with the breaching receipts as OpenMarketEvidenceReference. The buyer-facing ListingComparison row shows advertised-vs-measured SLA side by side (price_index_bps already normalizes price; this adds an SLA-honesty column). Sellers can no longer advertise a fake SLA because their own signed receipts are the evidence.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-listing (discovery::ListingSla, ListingComparison, freshness ranking input); chio-open-market (penalty::OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact, OpenMarketEvidenceReference, HoldBond/SlashBond); chio-metering receipts as the measured-SLA source
ideas.orca_surface: Background watchdog wired into Orca's 'notify when an agent needs you' machinery (paging the operator only on a proposed penalty); an advertised-vs-measured SLA column in the marketplace compare view and the diff-review receipt card
ideas.user_value: SLAs become enforceable promises backed by the seller's own cryptographic receipts and bond, so buyers can trust the latency/availability numbers on a listing instead of treating them as marketing.
ideas.moat: Closing the loop from signed per-call receipts -> measured SLA -> ranking penalty + bond hold is the 'economic accountability for sellers' gap the whole agent-commerce landscape admits is unfilled. It requires Chio's receipt log + listing + open-market penalty crates together; no payment rail or Bazaar has it.
ideas.risk: Honest sellers could be penalized for client-side or network faults misattributed to them. Mitigate by attributing only kernel-measured latency, requiring a minimum receipt volume before a breach counts, and keeping the first penalty action HoldBond (reversible) rather than SlashBond.

ideas.bold_bet: SLA receipts that re-price the market (idea 5). The agent-commerce world has converged on payment rails (ACP, AP2, x402) and discovery (x402 Bazaar), but every grounding source flags the same unfilled white space: there is no economic accountability for sellers and no enforceable, tamper-evident link between what a tool promised and what it delivered. Chio is uniquely positioned because it already emits a signed receipt for every mediated call and already ships the seller-side primitives (ListingSla in the pricing hint, freshness-aware ranking in discovery, and a full bond/penalty/slash lifecycle in chio-open-market). Wiring measured latency/availability from the receipt log back into ranking and bond holds turns the marketplace from a catalog into a self-policing exchange where a seller's own cryptographic receipts are the evidence that re-prices or slashes them. That is the defensible reason a buyer would route agent spend through Chio-on-Orca rather than calling an x402 endpoint directly, and it is the feature no competitor can copy without rebuilding Chio's receipt + listing + open-market stack.

ideas.lens: Agent-to-agent commerce: agents hiring/subcontracting other agents, escrow, deliverable verification, and settlement between agents inside the forked Orca cockpit

ideas.title: Subcontract-a-worktree: the bid/ask/accept hire button
ideas.one_liner: One Orca worktree-agent hires another (local or remote) for a sub-task by minting a scoped, cost-capped capability token against a verified funds reservation, not by sharing an API key.
ideas.description: Add an 'Outsource' action on any worktree task. The hiring agent emits a SignedBidRequest (server_id/tool, max_invocations, max_cost_per_invocation, a RequestedScope and deadline); the contractor side runs bid() to mint a scoped CapabilityToken bound to the contractor's did:chio subject and returns a SignedAskResponse. accept() only records the hire once a signature-verified VerifiedReservationReceipt covers the token's total liability, so the kernel refuses the contractor's first paid call if funds were never reserved. This turns Orca's 'fan a prompt across N agents' into 'agent A pays agent B to do the sub-task', with scope (not a bearer secret) as the unit of delegation.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-open-market/bidding.rs (bid/accept, SignedBidRequest, SignedAskResponse, VerifiedReservationReceipt) minting a chio-core-types CapabilityToken bound to a chio-did subject
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Outsource sub-task' affordance in the renderer worktree tree (src/renderer) plus an `orca commerce hire <worktree> --scope <tool> --cap <amount>` verb (src/cli/specs + src/cli/handlers) that shells to a `chio market bid/accept` subcommand; the minted token shows as a 'job token' chip on the contractor worktree.
ideas.user_value: An agent can delegate work it should not do itself and pay for exactly that scope, with a hard, kernel-enforced spend cap. The hiring human sees who was hired, for what scope, and for how much before any work runs.
ideas.moat: The hire is a cryptographically scoped capability against a verified reservation, not a shared key. Competing agent runners pass raw credentials; Chio passes a fail-closed, cost-capped, time-bounded token the kernel itself enforces, so a subcontracted agent cannot exceed its mandate.
ideas.risk: Requires per-worktree agent identity keys and a reservation source wired before any hire; the accept() check is only as strong as the pinned reservation-authority key.

ideas.title: Escrow-on-delivery: pay the contractor only against a co-signed deliverable receipt
ideas.one_liner: Funds for a subcontracted job sit in on-chain escrow and release only when both kernels co-sign the delivery receipt; a failed deliverable refunds automatically.
ideas.description: When a hire is accepted, dispatch an EscrowBacked job via chio-settle prepare_web3_escrow_dispatch (USDC escrow create) instead of paying up front. The contractor's output is captured as a ChioReceipt; both kernels sign the same CoSigningBody to produce a chio-federation DualSignedReceipt proving delivery was accepted bilaterally. Release with prepare_dual_sign_release / prepare_merkle_release only against that proof; if the deadline passes, prepare_escrow_refund returns the money. This closes the loop x402/ACP leave open: they move money but do not bind release to a verifiable bilateral delivery proof.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle EVM escrow (prepare_web3_escrow_dispatch, prepare_dual_sign_release, prepare_merkle_release, prepare_escrow_refund) + X402SettlementMode::EscrowBacked, gated by a chio-federation DualSignedReceipt as the delivery proof
ideas.orca_surface: Orca's annotate-AI-diffs review pane gets an 'Accept deliverable' button: accepting co-signs the receipt and triggers escrow release; the worktree 'Attested Receipts' tab shows escrow state (locked -> released/refunded). CLI: `orca commerce accept-delivery <job>` and `orca commerce dispute <job>`.
ideas.user_value: A contractor agent gets paid only for work the buyer's kernel actually accepted, and a buyer never loses funds for an undelivered or rejected sub-task. Both sides hold a non-repudiable, replayable proof.
ideas.moat: Capability-gated escrow whose release key is a bilateral cryptographic delivery proof. This is the 'enforcement plus attested release' white space the market admits no payment rail fills; defensible because the release condition is a co-signed receipt, not a dashboard click.
ideas.risk: Requires the web3 feature and a funded operator treasury/custodian; real on-chain escrow means gas, finality, and reorg handling. The custody-neutral default means fiat jobs still emit only signed instructions a human must execute.

ideas.title: Deliverable-verified settlement: the fulfillment_attested gate as a live order engine
ideas.one_liner: Every agent-to-agent job runs forward through the commerce-order state machine where settlement is structurally impossible until fulfillment_attested is reached.
ideas.description: Drive each subcontract job through the chio-commerce-order replay state machine (intent_recorded -> provider_admitted -> quote_bound -> mandate_bound -> budget_reserved -> payment_verified -> fulfillment_attested -> settlement_dispatched -> settlement_reconciled -> completed). The edge into settlement_dispatched is only legal after fulfillment_attested, so deliverable acceptance is a required state transition with evidence_refs binding the quote, mandate, and payment ids, not an advisory log line. The repo has the bundle verifier but not the producer; the opportunity is the missing forward-driver that advances a live job through these states from inside Orca and assembles the SHA-256-pinned bundle for audit.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-commerce-order/replay.rs fixed state machine (fulfillment_attested gate, evidence_ref binding) + mandate.rs CommerceMandateLedger binding ap2/acp hashes with occurrence and max-amount limits
ideas.orca_surface: A per-worktree 'Commerce' panel renders the live job as a state ladder (states done, state blocked) with the verified mandate->payment->fulfillment->settlement chain; reviewers replay the assembled bundle. Mobile companion (mobile/app/review) surfaces the same ladder for phone approval of the fulfillment_attested step.
ideas.user_value: A human or auditor sees at a glance that a contractor was paid only after attested delivery, and can replay the whole order offline. No money moves out of state order.
ideas.moat: A neutral, rail-agnostic order engine that makes deliverable verification a structural precondition of settlement and binds AP2/ACP mandate hashes into one signed ledger. It verifies across ACP/AP2/x402 rather than competing with any of them.
ideas.risk: The repo has the verifier but not the live forward-driver; building the producer that calls a real PSP/settlement and assembles the bundle is net-new and the largest lift here.

ideas.title: Fan-out budget pool: one mandate sliced across N competing agents
ideas.one_liner: When Orca fans one prompt across N worktree-agents, they all draw from one signed budget pool and over-allocation is rejected before any agent (or any hire) runs.
ideas.description: Materialize Orca's parallel-worktrees run as a chio-workflow-preflight WorkflowPreflightPlan: a parent_task with a WorkflowBudgetPool and one child_task per worktree, each with its own budget_minor slice. Preflight validation rejects the run (workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded) if the parent plus children exceed the pool or mix currencies. Each child's slice becomes the reservation ceiling that backs that worktree's hire/escrow actions, so subcontracting spend across the whole fan-out is bounded by one mandate. Losing branches whose intermediate artifacts get reused can later be credited via the settlement path.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-workflow-preflight/types.rs WorkflowBudgetPool + WorkflowPreflightPlan (parent_task/child_tasks, budget_minor, currency coherence, workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded)
ideas.orca_surface: The existing 'fan across N agents' launch dialog gains a 'Budget pool' field; each worktree card shows its allocated slice and remaining draw. Over-allocations block launch with the preflight error. CLI: `orca commerce pool set <total>` before an orchestration run.
ideas.user_value: Answers the '$47k runaway agent' fear for the parallel case: a whole fleet of agents, each able to hire others, cannot collectively exceed one human-set pool, and over-allocation fails before launch rather than after spend.
ideas.moat: Maps one-to-one onto Orca's signature parallel-orchestration UX, which no other commerce stack targets. The budget envelope is signed and checked pre-flight, so enforcement precedes execution rather than reacting to it.
ideas.risk: WorkflowBudgetPool validation is against a caller-supplied plan; without a shared, durable, concurrency-safe ledger, two worktrees drafting against the same pool concurrently could race unless serialized through the sidecar.

ideas.title: Bonded, slashable contractor reputation: pick (and punish) the agent you hire
ideas.one_liner: Before an agent subcontracts, Orca ranks candidate contractors by signed reputation tier and required bond; bad delivery slashes the bond and re-prices the seller from receipts.
ideas.description: When choosing whom to hire, rank contractors by chio-reputation ReputationTier (Tier0-3, where Tier3 needs both a 0.90 composed score and every feed clearing the 0.80 per-feed floor, so flooding one signal cannot fake top tier). Higher-value jobs require the contractor to post a bond (chio-open-market fee_schedule bond classes). On a rejected/failed deliverable, issue an OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact (slash, with a reverse_slash path if adjudication is overturned) so the bond is forfeited and the seller's price/tier degrade from signed receipt evidence. Strictly stronger than x402 Bazaar pay-and-pray: sellers carry skin in the game and accountability is receipt-derived.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-reputation/tier.rs ReputationTier with per-feed floor + chio-open-market/penalty.rs OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact (slash/reverse_slash, bond classes) and fee_schedule bond requirements
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Contractor picker' modal (extending Orca's native marketplace/account-switcher UI) lists candidate agents/tool servers ranked by tier, bond posted, revocation freshness, and price, with an auto-bid button. A contractor worktree shows a 'bond posted / at risk' chip; a slash event posts a notification.
ideas.user_value: Buyers transact with provably reputable, bonded counterparties and recover value when a contractor underdelivers. Good contractors earn cheaper, more visible access; bad ones are economically penalized, not just downranked.
ideas.moat: Economic accountability for sellers in an agent tool market, tied to tamper-evident receipts and a Sybil-resistant tier with a per-feed floor. The bond plus slash loop is the gap competitors (Bazaar, plain card rails) explicitly lack.
ideas.risk: Reputation is local-corpus-only by design, so cross-operator scores need a signed reputation-snapshot exchange at deal time; slashing requires a trusted adjudication input and the governance/fee-schedule operator keys to issue penalties.

ideas.title: Peer settlement with FX evidence: A pays B across currencies with a signed conversion proof
ideas.one_liner: An agent-to-agent payment where buyer and contractor price in different currencies settles at an oracle rate captured as signed conversion evidence attached to the receipt.
ideas.description: Make agent-to-agent payment a first-class object distinct from buying a capability. The hiring agent's pool is in currency X, the contractor quotes in currency Y; chio-link converts using a Chainlink/Pyth feed behind a circuit-breaker and emits OracleConversionEvidence (rate, source, margin_bps, freshness) signed under CHIO_LINK_ORACLE_AUTHORITY. That evidence attaches to FinancialReceiptMetadata.oracle_evidence and the settlement executes via a chio-credit capital_and_execution instruction (Disburse/Release) with an OperatorTreasury+Custodian authority chain, simulation-first by default so the crypto rail (chio-settle) or a manual fiat rail actually moves funds. The peer payment is auditable down to the exchange rate used.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-link OracleConversionEvidence (Chainlink/Pyth, circuit-breaker, CHIO_LINK_ORACLE_AUTHORITY) + chio-credit/capital_and_execution.rs Disburse/Release ledger ops with OperatorTreasury+Custodian authority chain, settled via chio-settle
ideas.orca_surface: The receipt/diff review pane shows a cross-currency job line: 'paid 0.42 USDC = 0.39 EUR at rate R (Pyth, 12s old, margin 30bps)'. CLI: `orca commerce settle <job>` emits the signed capital-execution instruction; a 'rate stale / circuit-breaker tripped' state blocks settlement and pages via notifications.
ideas.user_value: Agents in different currency regimes transact and settle with a provable, freshness-bounded exchange rate, removing a silent dispute source. The buyer sees exactly what rate moved their money.
ideas.moat: Most rails assume single-currency and hide FX. Binding a signed, circuit-breaker-guarded conversion proof to the settlement receipt is regulator-grade cross-currency audit, and the simulation-first authority chain keeps Chio non-custodial (instruction-emitting) until a licensed rail executes.
ideas.risk: No fiat custody execution exists in-repo, so the EUR leg emits only a signed instruction a human/custodian must run; only the crypto leg auto-settles. Oracle dependency adds a freshness/availability failure mode that must fail closed.

ideas.bold_bet: Escrow-on-delivery (idea 2) is the boldest bet: make the forked Orca the first agent cockpit where a subcontracted job's funds sit in on-chain USDC escrow (chio-settle EVM) and release only against a bilaterally co-signed deliverable receipt (chio-federation DualSignedReceipt), with automatic refund on a missed deadline. It seizes the market's openly-admitted white space (out-of-agent enforcement plus attested, condition-gated release that no payment rail fills) and is end-to-end demoable today because chio-settle already executes escrow create / dual-sign-release / refund on EVM behind the web3 flag. The pitch: agents on Chio-Orca cannot be stiffed and cannot overpay, because the money moves only when both kernels sign that the work was delivered.

ideas.title: Shop-and-Compare board: signed price discovery as a worktree fan-out
ideas.one_liner: A procurement board where a buyer agent searches live signed listings, then renders a cheapest-first side-by-side that a human picks the winner from, mirroring Orca's compare-N-agents UX.
ideas.description: chio-listing/discovery.rs already ships search() (filter live signed listings by capability_scope_prefix, max_price_per_call, provider, freshness, fail-closed on revoked/stale/tampered hints) and compare() (normalized price_index_bps in basis points vs the cheapest row, plus SLA, revocation_rate_bps, recent_receipts_volume). Wrap this as `orca commerce shop <scope> --max-price` so a buyer agent populating a worktree group materializes one Listing row per candidate provider. Each row is a card in Orca's existing parallel-results compare pane: cheapest is rank 1, an index column shows 1.4x/2.0x relative price, and revocation rate plus signed receipt volume sit beside price. The picked listing_id flows straight into the bid step. Reuses the exact compare-and-merge-the-winner muscle Orca built for code, applied to procurement.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-listing (discovery.rs search/compare, ListingComparison.price_index_bps, ListingPricingHint with SLA + revocation_rate_bps + recent_receipts_volume); ranking is cheapest-first then revocation then receipts
ideas.orca_surface: New `orca commerce shop` CLI verb (src/cli/specs + handlers); results rendered in the existing parallel-worktree compare/merge pane in src/renderer, one card per candidate listing, with a 'Buy this' button that fires the bid
ideas.user_value: The buyer agent does not just pick the first vendor an LLM hallucinates; the human sees a verifiable, signed, normalized price+SLA+reliability board and approves the winner with one click, exactly like merging the best code branch.
ideas.moat: The comparison rows are cryptographically signed pricing hints bound to a verified namespace owner and filtered fail-closed, not scraped prices. x402 Bazaar and ChatGPT shopping show prices with no provenance; here every cell is attestable and stale/revoked vendors silently drop out.
ideas.risk: Needs a populated listing registry to be useful; the grounding notes there is no running marketplace registry in-repo, so early value depends on Chio-operated seed listings or wrapping x402 Bazaar endpoints into signed ListingPricingHints.

ideas.title: Mandate-gated checkout passport in the AI-diffs review pane
ideas.one_liner: Every autonomous purchase an agent makes is replayed through the commerce-order state machine and rendered as an approve/reject 'receipt diff' next to code diffs, so a human ratifies an attested transaction, not a log line.
ideas.description: chio-commerce-order replays a SHA-256-pinned event log through a fixed state machine (record_intent -> admit_provider -> bind_quote -> bind_mandate -> reserve_budget -> verify_payment -> attest_fulfillment -> dispatch_settlement -> reconcile_settlement -> complete_order) and binds the AP2 checkout-mandate hash, AP2 payment-mandate hash, and ACP delegated-payment-token hash in CommerceMandateLedger, enforcing that capture time falls inside the mandate window and amount/currency match the quote. Surface the resulting passport as a first-class entry in Orca's annotate-AI-diffs review surface: the reviewer sees the ordered state timeline, the bound mandate hashes, the priced quote, and the payment lifecycle (PSP, manual-capture-before-expiry, fraud/dispute/refund states) rendered like a diff, and clicks Approve to release. Because the verifier is post-hoc, Orca becomes the producer that drives a live order forward through those states and assembles the bundle the crate verifies.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-commerce-order (replay.rs is_allowed_transition state machine, mandate.rs validate_mandate_ledger binding ap2_checkout/payment + acp_delegated_payment_token hashes with window+amount enforcement, payment.rs lifecycle with manual capture-before-expiry and fraud/dispute/refund/chargeback states)
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Purchases' tab beside the existing AI-diff review UI in src/renderer (and mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx); each agent purchase is a reviewable passport card with an Approve/Reject gate that drives the bind_mandate/verify_payment transitions
ideas.user_value: A runaway buyer agent cannot complete a purchase the human did not ratify: the order is stuck at mandate_bound until someone approves the attested passport, and the approval is itself a signed artifact, attacking AP2's consent-and-intent ambiguity dispute driver directly.
ideas.moat: This is the out-of-agent attestation+audit layer the market admits is missing. The cockpit binds AP2 and ACP artifacts into one replayable signed ledger and gates release on it; no payment rail (ACP/AP2/x402) enforces budgets or ratifies intent at review time, and none produces a court-replayable buyer passport.
ideas.risk: chio-commerce-order verifies an already-assembled bundle; Orca must build the live order engine and PSP integration that produces the event log, payment_intent, and bundle. That producer side is net-new work the repo explicitly does not have.

ideas.title: Procurement autonomy dial: Shadow / Advisory / Active auto-buy
ideas.one_liner: A per-worktree slider that decides whether the buyer agent only proposes purchases, waits for human approval, or auto-buys within a signed envelope, backed by the autonomy decision crate.
ideas.description: chio-autonomy/model.rs defines AutonomousAutomationMode (Shadow, Advisory, Active) and AutonomousDecisionReviewState (AutoApproved, HumanReviewRequired, ShadowOnly, Blocked), plus an authority envelope (OperatorPolicy / RegulatedRole / DelegatedMarketAuthority) and a BindWithinEnvelope disposition. Repurpose that decision shape for procurement: Shadow means the agent logs what it would have bought, Advisory means every buy becomes a HumanReviewRequired card in the Purchases tab, and Active means the agent may BindWithinEnvelope (auto-complete) when the quote is under a signed price/per-vendor/category envelope and the vendor is unrevoked, escalating to HumanReviewRequired otherwise. The dial lives on each worktree so a high-trust 'renew my known SaaS' agent can run Active while an exploratory 'find me a new data vendor' agent is pinned to Advisory.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-autonomy (AutonomousAutomationMode Shadow/Advisory/Active, AutonomousDecisionReviewState AutoApproved/HumanReviewRequired/ShadowOnly/Blocked, BindWithinEnvelope disposition, signed AutonomousPricingAuthorityEnvelope)
ideas.orca_surface: A per-worktree autonomy dial in the worktree/agent header in src/renderer (next to the budget chip), persisted per worktree; Active-mode auto-completions still post a passport card to the Purchases tab for after-the-fact audit
ideas.user_value: Users get a single, legible safety control for buyer agents: try in Shadow, supervise in Advisory, let it run in Active only inside a cryptographically scoped envelope, with auto-escalation to a human when a buy exceeds the envelope.
ideas.moat: The autonomy level is bound to a signed authority envelope and emits an evidence-referential decision artifact, so 'the agent was allowed to auto-buy this' is provable after the fact. Plain agent runners expose at best a checkbox with no attestation of who authorized the autonomy tier.
ideas.risk: chio-autonomy's vocabulary is built around insurance pricing/capital decisions; mapping it onto generic goods/SaaS procurement is a reinterpretation, and Active-mode auto-buy raises the regulatory custody bar (must stay non-custodial, settle over a licensed rail).

ideas.title: Fair-price guard: appraisal + reputation-weighted spend ceiling before any buy
ideas.one_liner: Before the buyer agent commits, the kernel checks the quoted price against an independent fair-value appraisal and against a reputation-tiered credit ceiling, blocking overpriced or over-budget buys fail-closed.
ideas.description: Two existing helpers compose into a pre-purchase guard. chio-appraisal/marketplace_pricing.rs computes a deterministic reference invocation price from a manifest base price plus tenant context, giving an independent 'fair price' to compare the vendor's quote against; if the quote exceeds the appraisal by more than a policy band, the buy is flagged or blocked. chio-underwriting/marketplace_limits.rs emits a MarketplaceCreditLimitDecision keyed off reputation tier with hard ceilings (MARKETPLACE_TIER_LIMIT_UNITS = 10k / 50k / 250k / 1M minor units) and denies outright when the publisher is revoked (publisher_revoked fail-closed). Wire both as a guard that fires on the agent-hooks bus the moment a buyer agent proposes a purchase: the hook calls the kernel, which returns allow/deny with a reason (price_above_appraisal, over_tier_ceiling, publisher_revoked). Surface the verdict inline so the human sees 'agent wanted to pay 240 USD; fair value 90 USD; blocked'.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-appraisal (marketplace_pricing.rs deterministic reference price) + chio-underwriting (marketplace_limits.rs MARKETPLACE_TIER_LIMIT_UNITS tier ceilings, compute_marketplace_credit_limit with publisher_revoked fail-closed deny)
ideas.orca_surface: A blocking capability-gate on the agent-hooks bus (src/main/agent-hooks) that intercepts proposed purchases; the deny reason renders as a red banner in the Purchases tab and the worktree terminal, turning the fire-and-forget hook into a synchronous allow/deny
ideas.user_value: The buyer agent cannot be talked into overpaying or buying from a revoked vendor: an independent appraisal and a hard reputation-tier ceiling sit between the agent's intent and the money, both producing a human-readable reason.
ideas.moat: Independent fair-value appraisal plus revocation-aware credit ceilings as an out-of-agent gate is exactly the enforcement (not observability) white space. The runaway-agent story had dashboards; this refuses the next overpriced call in the kernel before funds move.
ideas.risk: Requires bumping the Orca agent-hook protocol to a blocking decision-returning contract (the grounding flags the hook bus is currently fire-and-forget); the appraisal helper also needs a manifest base price, so fair-value coverage is only as good as the catalog feeding it.

ideas.title: Bonded recourse + one-click dispute when the goods are bad
ideas.one_liner: If a vendor delivers junk or never delivers, the buyer surfaces a 'Dispute' button that holds or slashes the vendor's posted bond using signed evidence pulled from the purchase passport.
ideas.description: chio-open-market/penalty.rs defines OpenMarketAbuseClass (FraudulentListing, UnverifiableListingBehavior), OpenMarketPenaltyAction (HoldBond, SlashBond, ReverseSlash), and a penalty state machine (Proposed -> Enforced / Reversed / Denied) over a vendor's posted bond class (OpenMarketBondClass from fee_schedule.rs), all keyed to signed evidence references (OpenMarketEvidenceReference). Combine with chio-market's claim -> dispute -> adjudication lifecycle so a buyer who got a fraudulent or undelivered result clicks Dispute on the purchase passport; Orca assembles a signed penalty proposal whose evidence_refs are the very receipt/quote/fulfillment hashes already in the commerce-order passport, and the vendor's bond is held pending adjudication, then slashed on an upheld outcome. This gives buyer agents real post-purchase accountability instead of x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray model.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-open-market (penalty.rs OpenMarketAbuseClass/PenaltyAction HoldBond/SlashBond, OpenMarketBondClass bonds, OpenMarketEvidenceReference) + chio-market (claim/dispute/adjudication lifecycle)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Dispute' action on each passport card in the Purchases/review tab; clicking it emits a signed penalty proposal and shows bond status (Clear / BondHeld / Slashed) inline, with the adjudication outcome flowing back as a notification via Orca's existing notify machinery
ideas.user_value: Buyer agents are no longer exposed to vendors with no consequences: a bad delivery holds and can slash the seller's bond, and the dispute is built automatically from evidence already captured at purchase time.
ideas.moat: Quality bonds plus receipt-evidenced slashing for sellers in an agent tool marketplace is something every current agentic-commerce rail explicitly lacks. The dispute is non-repudiable because its evidence refs are the same signed hashes in the buyer's transaction passport.
ideas.risk: Needs vendors to actually post bonds (requires the open-market charter/fee-schedule/activation chain to be operational) and a neutral adjudicator binding, which the grounding flags as free-form today; without a trusted-arbiter registry the slash decision lacks an impartial signer.

ideas.title: Phone-tap mandate mint for high-value buys
ideas.one_liner: When a buyer agent wants to spend above a threshold, a push lands on the user's phone; approving it mints the signed AP2-style mandate that unlocks exactly that purchase and nothing more.
ideas.description: Reuse Orca's existing mobile pairing (E2EE tweetnacl device channel, QR pair flow) and notify-when-agent-needs-you machinery as the human consent step that binds an AP2/ACP mandate into the commerce-order ledger. When a buyer agent reaches mandate_bound for a buy over the user's threshold, Orca pushes 'Agent X wants to spend 180 USD at Vendor Y for <scope>' to the phone; the tap signs a scoped mandate (max_amount_minor, currency, single_use or max_occurrences, valid_from/expires_at) whose hash is exactly what chio-commerce-order/mandate.rs verifies against the quote and capture time. Because AP2's agent_mode already distinguishes human-present from human-not-present (chio-agent-web-interop/ap2.rs), the approval records which mode the buy ran in. The mandate is the same key the kernel later meters against, so the human's tap and the spend authority are cryptographically one object.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-commerce-order (mandate.rs CommerceMandateLedger: max_amount_minor, single_use, max_occurrences, validity window bound to capture time) + chio-agent-web-interop (ap2.rs agent_mode human-present/human-not-present, checkout+payment mandate digests)
ideas.orca_surface: Orca's mobile companion (mobile/app pair*.tsx + notifications): a high-value buy pushes an approval card; the tap mints the mandate and releases the worktree's purchase, while denial leaves the order frozen at mandate_bound
ideas.user_value: Autonomous commerce with a human circuit-breaker in your pocket: agents run unattended for small buys but a phone tap is the hard gate for anything large, and that tap is a verifiable consent artifact, not a logged click.
ideas.moat: Binding the human consent moment to a cryptographic mandate that is the same key the kernel meters and that the order verifier checks against capture time is unique. It turns AP2's biggest dispute driver (consent ambiguity) into a replayable signed approval tied to human-present mode.
ideas.risk: Depends on the live order engine existing to reach mandate_bound, and on a non-custodial design so the phone-approved mandate authorizes a licensed rail rather than Orca moving funds (custody is the regulatory bright line).

ideas.bold_bet: Make the forked Orca the neutral buyer-side checkout VERIFIER, not another wallet: every autonomous purchase is driven through chio-commerce-order's pinned state machine, binds the AP2 checkout/payment mandate and ACP delegated-payment-token hashes, and lands as an approve/reject 'purchase passport' diff in the same review pane Orca already uses for code. The boldest move is to gate fund release on that human ratification at the bind_mandate state so a runaway buyer agent literally cannot complete an unapproved buy, and to back the auto-buy path with a signed autonomy envelope (Shadow/Advisory/Active) plus an out-of-agent fair-price + reputation-ceiling guard on the hooks bus. That is the out-of-agent enforcement and court-replayable audit layer the entire 2026 agentic-commerce market admits nobody owns, and it is defensible precisely because Chio already binds all three competing standards (AP2, ACP, x402) into one signed, replayable ledger instead of competing with any of them.

ideas.title: Ledger of Record: the verified mandate -> payment -> settlement -> anchor strip
ideas.one_liner: A right-rail 'Settlement' tab per worktree that renders each paid agent action as a single verified row: cost charged, settlement state, on-chain tx, and a green 'anchored' lock once the receipt is Merkle-proven into a signed checkpoint.
ideas.description: Every paid tool call already terminates in a FinancialReceiptMetadata (cost_charged, currency, budget_remaining, root_budget_holder, SettlementStatus, oracle_evidence) and, for on-chain settlement, a Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact with settlement_reference and an optional reconciled_anchor_proof. The dashboard runs verify_public_settlement_proof over the assembled PublicSettlementProofBundle and shows the resulting PublicSettlementVerifierReport.verified_claims as discrete badges (order_binding_verified, chain_context_verified, finality_verified, oracle_conversion_bound, dispute_posture_bound). A row is only marked 'final' when finality_report_status returns 'final', so the UI never claims settled before observed_confirmations >= required_confirmations. This is the headline financial control surface and it ships almost entirely by rendering existing verifier output.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-web3 settlement.rs (Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact, Web3SettlementLifecycleState) + settlement_proof.rs (verify_public_settlement_proof -> PublicSettlementVerifierReport); chio-core-types FinancialReceiptMetadata
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Settlement' tab beside the existing annotate-AI-diffs review pane in src/renderer; rows hydrated over a new commerce:* IPC namespace (src/main/ipc/commerce.ts) that shells the chio CLI verifier
ideas.user_value: A reviewer approves a cryptographically attested transaction (mandate-bound, finality-checked, anchor-proven) instead of a raw log line, and can see at a glance which agent spend is final vs pending vs disputed.
ideas.moat: No agent cockpit shows a per-action chain that is independently re-verifiable offline. The verifier is fail-closed Rust that re-derives finality and order binding, not a status string scraped from a PSP webhook.
ideas.risk: Producing the PublicSettlementProofBundle requires assembling chain_snapshot/block_snapshot/bond_snapshot; the in-repo path verifies bundles but does not collect them, so a thin indexer/collector behind the sidecar must be built.

ideas.title: Anchor receipt drawer: tap any spend to see its Merkle inclusion proof up to a Bitcoin block
ideas.one_liner: Click a settled row to expand a proof drawer that walks receipt -> Merkle leaf -> signed checkpoint statement -> EVM chain anchor -> optional Bitcoin OpenTimestamps super-root, each step rendered as a verified/failed step with the kernel key and tx hash.
ideas.description: AnchorInclusionProof + verify_anchor_inclusion_proof already recompute the receipt's canonical leaf hash, verify the Merkle path to the checkpoint merkle_root, verify the kernel signature on the Web3CheckpointStatement, and (when present) verify the super-root path plus require Web3BitcoinAnchor OTS metadata. The drawer renders this as a vertical proof ladder: receipt.id, leaf_index/tree_size, checkpoint_seq, anchored_merkle_root, chain_anchor.tx_hash/block_number, and bitcoin_block_height. A 'Re-verify now' button reruns verify_anchor_inclusion_proof client-side via the sidecar so the user watches the proof pass live. This turns the abstract 'append-only Merkle receipt log' into a tangible, inspectable artifact tied to a real dollar amount.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-web3 anchors.rs (AnchorInclusionProof, Web3CheckpointStatement, Web3ChainAnchorRecord, Web3BitcoinAnchor, verify_anchor_inclusion_proof, verify_checkpoint_statement)
ideas.orca_surface: Expandable proof drawer inside the Settlement tab row; also exposed as `orca commerce anchor verify <receipt-id>` CLI verb (src/cli/specs + src/cli/handlers) so agents can self-prove
ideas.user_value: Turns 'trust me, it is logged' into a step-by-step cryptographic chain a developer or auditor can replay, including timestamping to Bitcoin for the highest-assurance spend.
ideas.moat: Tamper-evident, replayable, cross-anchor (EVM + Bitcoin OTS) receipt proofs are exactly the audit-trail standard the commerce landscape openly admits does not exist; competitors have PostHog analytics, not Merkle proofs.
ideas.risk: Bitcoin OTS anchoring is batch/super-root based, so most receipts only have an EVM chain anchor in the near term; the Bitcoin step is often empty and the UI must degrade gracefully.

ideas.title: Settlement health rail with a global kill switch (RefundOnly / Halted)
ideas.one_liner: A persistent status strip showing per-chain lane health, indexer lag, queued recoveries, and live incident alerts, with a one-click emergency-mode control that flips the whole settlement runtime into DispatchPaused, RefundOnly, RecoveryOnly, or Halted.
ideas.description: chio-settle ops.rs already defines the entire control plane: SettlementRuntimeReport (lanes, indexers, recoveries, incidents), SettlementLaneRuntimeStatus via classify_settlement_lane, SettlementIndexerCursor with lag_blocks and Lagging/Drifted/Failed status, SettlementIncidentAlert with severity, and SettlementEmergencyControls whose modes gate which SettlementOperationKind are allowed (ensure_settlement_operation_allowed is fail-closed). The dashboard renders the report and exposes apply_change so an operator can set the mode; every flip writes a SettlementControlChangeRecord (actor, source, before/after, reason) into the trace history, giving a signed audit of who paused settlement and why. This is the direct, demo-able answer to the '$47k runaway agent with dashboards but no kill-switch' story: here the kill switch is in the settlement kernel and refuses the next escrow dispatch.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle ops.rs (SettlementRuntimeReport, SettlementEmergencyControls, SettlementEmergencyMode, classify_settlement_lane, ensure_settlement_operation_allowed, SettlementControlChangeRecord)
ideas.orca_surface: Always-visible settlement status strip in the renderer header (reusing the src/main/rate-limits usage UI host) + a guarded 'Emergency mode' menu; mirrored to mobile AccountUsage.tsx so an operator can Halt from a phone
ideas.user_value: Operators get a real out-of-agent circuit breaker: when an indexer drifts or an agent misbehaves, one tap moves all chains to RefundOnly or Halted and new dispatch is denied at the kernel, not the prompt.
ideas.moat: This is the white space every grounding source names (enforcement must live outside agent code). The mode change is a fail-closed Rust gate with a signed change record, not a UI toggle that hopes the agent obeys.
ideas.risk: The control state must be the single source of truth shared by the sidecar that actually performs dispatch; if the executor does not consult SettlementEmergencyControls atomically, the kill switch is theater.

ideas.title: Reconciliation panel: observed vs intended, FX evidence, and partial/reversed/charged-back
ideas.one_liner: A reconciliation view that flags any settlement where observed amount, settled amount, or oracle-converted cost diverges from the intended capital instruction, and surfaces partial_settled / reversed / charged_back / timed_out rows for human resolution.
ideas.description: The execution-receipt validator already enforces the hard reconciliation invariants (observed_execution.amount must equal settled_amount, currencies must match the dispatch, observed_at must fall inside the execution window, and FX-sensitive paths must carry OracleConversionEvidence). The panel turns those same fields into a ledger: for each row it shows intended settlement_amount vs settled_amount, the lifecycle_state, and for cross-currency spend it renders the oracle_evidence (base/quote, rate, source, cache_age vs max_age) so a reviewer can see the exact price used and that it was fresh. PartiallySettled rows display the shortfall, Reversed/ChargedBack rows show reversal_of, and TimedOut/Failed/Reorged rows show failure_reason. It cross-checks against FinancialReceiptMetadata.cost_breakdown so the metered cost, the charged cost, and the on-chain settled cost line up in one place.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-web3 settlement.rs (validate_web3_settlement_execution_receipt reconciliation rules, CapitalExecutionObservation, reversal_of/failure_reason) + anchors.rs OracleConversionEvidence (validate_oracle_conversion_evidence); chio-core-types FinancialReceiptMetadata.cost_breakdown
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Reconciliation' sub-view in the Settlement tab with a 'Needs attention' filter; unreconciled/timed-out rows raise a notification through Orca's existing 'agent needs you' machinery
ideas.user_value: Finance and ops see a real reconciliation board (intended vs observed vs settled, with the FX rate that was applied) instead of trusting that the number the agent reported matches what actually moved on-chain.
ideas.moat: Binding the metered cost, the charged receipt, the oracle FX evidence, and the on-chain settled amount into one reconciled row is unique; payment rails reconcile money but have no link back to the attested tool-call cost or the freshness-checked oracle price.
ideas.risk: FX rows depend on chio-link/Chainlink/Pyth oracle evidence being populated at charge time; without a live oracle feed wired into metering, the conversion column is empty for most fiat-denominated spend.

ideas.title: Finality watchdog notifications: page a human only on ManualOverrideRequired
ideas.one_liner: Background settlement watchdogs (escrow timeout, finality observation, bond expiry) run as Orca tasks and stay silent on DuplicateSuppressed/DelayedButSafe, pushing a phone notification only when an outcome is ManualOverrideRequired.
ideas.description: build_settlement_watchdog_job and build_bond_watchdog_job already mint signed SettlementWatchdogJob artifacts (FinalityObservation / BondExpiry, cron-driven, with a state_fingerprint and operator_override_required=true), and assess_watchdog_execution validates each run fail-closed: it rejects fingerprint drift, rejects delays beyond replay_window_secs unless explicitly DelayedButSafe, and requires operator_override_used when the job demands it. Wired into Orca's scheduled-task/notification subsystem, these become the autonomous settlement brain: most fires are suppressed duplicates or safe delays and produce nothing, but a ManualOverrideRequired outcome (an escrow that did not finalize, a bond about to expire under-collateralized) pushes a signed approval request to the mobile companion. The human taps to authorize the override, which is itself recorded.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle automation.rs (SettlementWatchdogJob, SettlementWatchdogKind, build_settlement_watchdog_job, build_bond_watchdog_job, assess_watchdog_execution, SettlementAutomationOutcome)
ideas.orca_surface: Mapped onto Orca's scheduled-tasks/cron + agent-hooks notification path; ManualOverrideRequired raises a push to mobile pair/notification flow, resolved with a signed override
ideas.user_value: Settlement babysits itself: humans are paged only for the rare case that genuinely needs a decision (stuck escrow, expiring bond), with the approval captured as a verifiable override, not a Slack message.
ideas.moat: A duplicate-suppressed, replay-windowed, operator-override-gated settlement watchdog with signed execution assessment is a real automation primitive; alerting dashboards in the market are fire-and-forget and have no fail-closed override semantics.
ideas.risk: Orca's agent-hooks bus is best-effort fire-and-forget today; making the override step blocking/authoritative is a wire-protocol change (the codebase reserves the next ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump for exactly this).

ideas.title: One-click signed audit export for any spend window (EU AI Act / PCI-DSS pack)
ideas.one_liner: Select a date range or a single worktree and export a signed EnterpriseExportBundle of all settlement receipts, anchor proofs, FX evidence, and emergency-control history, re-verifiable offline with verify_enterprise_export.
ideas.description: The compliance substrate is already built: chio-enterprise-export produces an EnterpriseExportBundle and verify_enterprise_export re-checks it, FinancialReceiptMetadata carries the full budget-hold lineage (authorize/terminal exposure, realized_spend_units, root_budget_holder), AnchorInclusionProof gives tamper-evidence, and SettlementControlChangeRecord gives the who-paused-what trail. The export action bundles these for a chosen scope into one file that an auditor or regulator replays with the offline buyer/auditor verifier (chio-attest-buyer) to confirm every dollar an autonomous agent spent was mandate-gated, finality-checked, and anchored. This directly operationalizes Chio's existing EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 / PCI-DSS v4 mappings as a downloadable artifact rather than a doc.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-enterprise-export lib.rs (EnterpriseExportBundle, verify_enterprise_export); chio-attest-buyer offline replay; chio-core-types budget-hold lineage; chio-web3 anchors for tamper-evidence
ideas.orca_surface: An 'Export attested ledger' button in the Settlement tab and an `orca commerce export --since <ts> --scope <worktree>` CLI verb, reusing Orca's existing enterprise-export-style flow scaffolding
ideas.user_value: Compliance teams get a single signed, offline-verifiable evidence pack of all autonomous spend for a period, defensible in the (legally untested) dispute and regulator setting.
ideas.moat: An MIT agent runner with no money concept cannot produce this; the differentiator is provably-bounded, mandate-gated, anchor-backed spend exported for regulators, which sells directly into the production/compliance blocker.
ideas.risk: Export scope must be assembled across several crates (receipts, anchors, control history); defining the canonical bundle membership and ensuring nothing material is omitted is the real work, and a partial export undermines the audit claim.

ideas.bold_bet: Make the forked Orca the neutral settlement Ledger of Record: a per-worktree Settlement tab where every autonomous agent payment renders as a verified mandate -> payment -> finality -> Merkle-anchored row (driven by verify_public_settlement_proof and verify_anchor_inclusion_proof), backstopped by a global, fail-closed kill switch (SettlementEmergencyControls) that the kernel honors before the next escrow dispatch. This fuses the two things the entire 2026 commerce landscape admits are missing - out-of-agent enforcement and a tamper-evident, replayable audit trail - into one financial control surface, positioning Chio-on-Orca as the rail-agnostic verifier and audit plane across ACP/AP2/x402 rather than yet another wallet.

ideas.lens: Turn any tool/MCP server into a paid metered endpoint (x402-style): "Stripe for agent tools"
ideas.bold_bet: `orca commerce wrap --meter` as the "Stripe Atlas moment" for agent tools: one Orca CLI verb takes any stdio MCP server or OpenAPI spec and emits a signed, priced, metered Chio tool server whose every call is gated against a capability token (chio-mcp-adapter `mcp wrap` injecting `_meta.chio_verified`), costed per CostDimension (chio-metering), and settled over HTTP-402/USDC (chio-settle `build_x402_payment_requirements`) with a signed IOU minted per finalized receipt (chio-credit `CreditEvaluatorHook`). The pieces already exist in-repo as separately verified primitives; fusing them behind one verb makes Orca the first cockpit where a developer monetizes a tool in 60 seconds and an agent in another worktree pays per call with a cryptographic receipt, with no merchant account and enforcement living in the kernel rather than the prompt. That is the defensible wedge into the white space the market admits is empty: out-of-agent metering plus attested settlement, rail-agnostic, MIT-cockpit plus Rust-protocol.

ideas.title: One-verb tool monetization: `orca commerce wrap --price`
ideas.one_liner: Wrap any stdio MCP server or OpenAPI spec into a priced, metered, capability-gated Chio tool server with a single Orca CLI verb.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-mcp-adapter (`chio mcp wrap` stdio loop, `_meta.chio_verified` injection, `urn:chio:error:capability:scope-exceeded` deny) + chio-openapi-mcp-bridge (`OpenApiMcpBridge::from_spec` -> signed ToolManifest, `BridgeToolServer`) + chio-metering CostMetadata
ideas.orca_surface: New `orca commerce wrap <mcp-cmd | openapi.json> --price` verb under src/cli/specs + src/cli/handlers, shelling to the `chio` binary's existing `mcp wrap` / OpenAPI bridge; result registers as a tool server in the worktree's MCP config with a 'Metered' badge in the renderer tool list.
ideas.description: Today `chio mcp wrap` already runs a real MCP server over stdio, gates each tools/call against capability scope, and injects a `_meta.chio_verified` attestation header (denying with `urn:chio:error:capability:scope-exceeded`). `OpenApiMcpBridge::from_spec` does the same for any OpenAPI spec, producing a signed ToolManifest. This idea fuses those two with a price rule so the wrap output is a billable endpoint, exposed as one Orca CLI verb.
ideas.user_value: A developer turns a tool they already run into a billable endpoint in one command: no Stripe account, no merchant onboarding, no billing code. The wrap is the same artifact agents in other worktrees discover and call.
ideas.moat: The wrap is the kernel capability gate plus a signed ToolManifest, not a reverse proxy with bolted-on auth. Every call is scope-checked and attestable; a plain MCP billing proxy cannot emit a `_meta.chio_verified` header or a deny reason code grounded in a verifiable capability token.
ideas.risk: The `mcp wrap` loop gates on scope but the per-call price -> settlement binding is assembled from separate crates; making the wrapped server emit a live X402PaymentRequirements per call (not post-hoc) needs new glue between the adapter loop and chio-settle.

ideas.title: 402 paywall on the wrapped endpoint, paid in USDC mid-call
ideas.one_liner: A wrapped tool replies HTTP 402 with Chio-built payment requirements; the calling agent signs a stablecoin transfer and retries, the x402 pattern but capability-bound.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle `build_x402_payment_requirements` (emits version/chain_id/pay_to/amount_minor_units/accepted_tokens/settlement_mode from a Web3SettlementDispatchArtifact) + `prepare_transfer_with_authorization` (EIP-3009) + chio-agent-web-interop x402.rs verifier (binds resource/payment_requirements/payment_proof/settlement digests to a chio_payment_receipt_ref)
ideas.orca_surface: When an agent in worktree B calls a metered tool published from worktree A, Orca's agent-hooks bus intercepts the 402, surfaces 'Pay 0.0012 USDC to call fetch_url?' in the worktree's Commerce panel, and on the configured autonomy tier auto-signs and retries; the settled call shows a green attested-receipt chip in the annotate-AI-diffs review pane.
ideas.description: chio-settle already builds x402 PaymentRequirements from a settlement dispatch artifact and prepares an EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization; chio-agent-web-interop already verifies the x402 resource/payment/settlement digests and binds them to a Chio payment receipt ref. This wires that canonical pay-and-retry loop to a wrapped tool so an agent pays per call.
ideas.user_value: Agents transact per call with no subscription and no account: the canonical x402 pay-and-retry flow, but the payment is bound to a Chio capability and a receipt, so the buyer can prove it paid and the seller can prove it delivered.
ideas.moat: x402 Bazaar gives pay-per-call with no enforcement and no delivery proof. Here the 402 is issued by the kernel only when the caller lacks a valid funds-reserved capability, and the settlement digest is cross-checked back to a governed receipt id. This is x402 plus attestation, which the x402 spec explicitly punts on.
ideas.risk: Real on-chain settlement needs the web3 feature flag and a funded operator treasury; the fiat rail only emits a signed instruction a custodian must execute, so the live demo is USDC-on-Base first.

ideas.title: Per-call meter readout in the usage panel, billed by CostDimension
ideas.one_liner: Reuse Orca's per-provider usage/rate-limit UI to show a live, per-tool spend meter where each metered call is priced by real cost dimensions (compute ms, bytes, upstream API cost, tokens).
ideas.chio_capability: chio-metering CostDimension (ComputeTime/DataVolume/ApiCost/WarehouseQuery/Custom{tokens}) + CostMetadata per receipt + `CostQuery` aggregation (by session/agent/tool/time) + `create_billing_export` (BillingRecord/BillingExport)
ideas.orca_surface: Extend src/main/rate-limits and mobile AccountUsage.tsx with a 'Metered tools' tab: a running total per worktree/agent/tool fed by `chio receipts cost` (CostQuery), plus a one-click 'Export billing' that emits a BillingExport for the period, mirroring the existing usage fetchers.
ideas.description: chio-metering already models typed cost dimensions per receipt, a CostQuery aggregator across session/agent/tool/time (capped at 500), and a create_billing_export producing BillingRecord/BillingExport. Orca already has read-only per-provider usage UI. This idea joins them so the existing quota panels become a real, exportable spend ledger.
ideas.user_value: Both the tool seller and the agent operator see exactly what each call cost and what it was billed, by dimension, in real time, and can export a billing statement. Turns the read-only quota UI into a spend ledger.
ideas.moat: Cost is derived from typed dimensions captured on each signed receipt (WarehouseQuery dry-run bytes, ApiCost with the upstream provider named), so the billing export is auditable line-by-line rather than an opaque markup invoice.
ideas.risk: CostMetadata is a container the kernel/guards must populate; for an arbitrary wrapped CLI tool there is no automatic collector of true upstream cost, so sellers declare a pricing rule (per-call, per-byte) at wrap time and only some dimensions auto-fill.

ideas.title: Signed IOU and receipt per call, replayable in the review pane
ideas.one_liner: Every metered call mints a signed IOU bound to the receipt and its policy/content hashes, rendered as an attestable line item a human or auditor can replay offline.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit `CreditEvaluatorHook::evaluate` (mints `chio.credit.iou-envelope.v1` IouEnvelope per finalized non-zero-price receipt, binding amount_units/currency to receipt_id + content/policy hashes; zero-price skips) + chio-attest-buyer offline replay
ideas.orca_surface: A new 'Attested Receipts' tab beside the existing AI-diff review (src/renderer review surfaces, mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx): each metered call shows cost_charged, the IOU id, settlement status, and a 'Verify offline' button that runs the chio-attest-buyer replay path; auditors get a self-contained proof bundle.
ideas.description: The kernel already invokes CreditEvaluatorHook on each finalized signed receipt to mint a signed IOU binding amount/currency to the receipt id and content/policy hashes (zero-price receipts skip). chio-attest-buyer already provides an offline replay/verify boundary. This surfaces those artifacts as reviewable, replayable line items in Orca.
ideas.user_value: Spend stops being a log line and becomes a verifiable financial artifact: a reviewer approves a cryptographically attested transaction; a regulated buyer exports it for PCI-DSS / EU AI Act evidence.
ideas.moat: The IOU binds the charge to the exact policy and content hashes of the receipt, so the bill cannot be detached from what happened. No agent-tool-billing competitor produces a replayable, hash-bound IOU; this is the audit-trail standard the market admits does not exist.
ideas.risk: Mostly presentation work over existing crates; the main risk is UX clutter (one IOU per call is noisy), so it needs roll-up by tool/session in the panel.

ideas.title: Priced listing card so agents discover and auto-bid for a tool
ideas.one_liner: Publishing a wrapped tool emits a signed price listing; an agent that needs the tool searches, compares price/SLA, and auto-bids for a scoped, cost-capped capability token.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-listing (SignedListingPricingHint, ListingSla, ListingComparisonRow, ListingQuery/SearchResponse) + chio-open-market `bidding.rs` (`bid() -> SignedAskResponse` minting a scoped CapabilityToken with max_invocations/max_cost_per_invocation/max_total_cost against a VerifiedReservationReceipt)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Tool Market' surface in quick-open / the account-switcher area: wrapping a tool with `--publish` posts a SignedListingPricingHint; another worktree's agent picks a tool via a ranked comparison (price, SLA, reputation) and the cockpit shows the minted capability token as a 'wallet' chip in the sidebar.
ideas.description: chio-listing provides signed pricing hints, SLA, and comparison/search types; chio-open-market bidding already mints a scoped, cost-capped CapabilityToken via bid()->SignedAskResponse against a verified funds reservation, fail-closed against revoked/stale/expired listings and scope widening. This makes a wrapped endpoint shoppable, not just callable.
ideas.user_value: The wrapped endpoint is shoppable: an autonomous agent finds the cheapest acceptable provider of a capability and buys exactly the scoped access it needs (N invocations, capped cost) and no more.
ideas.moat: Bidding is fail-closed against revoked/stale/expired listings, scope widening, currency mismatch, and under-priced bids, and the token is cost-capped at the protocol level: an accountable marketplace with funds reserved before mint, versus x402 Bazaar's account-less pay-and-pray catalog.
ideas.risk: chio-listing gives types and search primitives but no running registry service that indexes live listings across operators; a thin local/shared registry must be built, and cross-machine price discovery needs federation.

ideas.title: Hard per-worktree spend mandate that fails the next paid call closed
ideas.one_liner: Set a signed spend cap per worktree/agent; when a metered tool would exceed it, the kernel refuses the next paid call instead of a dashboard merely warning, killing the runaway-agent failure mode.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-metering BudgetEnforcer/BudgetPolicy (max_total + per-session/agent/tool, saturating arithmetic, typed BudgetViolation) + chio-metering budget_hierarchy BudgetTree (org->dept->team->agent BudgetDecision) + chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy kill switch
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Spend mandate' control in the per-worktree budget panel and an `orca commerce budget set --cap` CLI verb; the agent-hooks gate consults the BudgetEnforcer before releasing a metered tool call, and an exceeded cap surfaces a BudgetViolation in the Commerce panel and pages the phone only on the hard stop.
ideas.description: chio-metering BudgetEnforcer enforces max_total plus per-session/agent/tool limits with saturating arithmetic and typed violations; BudgetTree enforces hierarchical caps with a fail-closed BudgetDecision; chio-credit ships a bonded-execution kill switch. Wiring these into the agent-hooks gate makes the spend ceiling refuse the next paid call rather than just warn.
ideas.user_value: Directly answers the widely-cited $47k runaway-agent story: an Orca-Chio agent cannot overspend because the cap is enforced in the kernel at call time, not asserted in the prompt or watched on a chart.
ideas.moat: This is the out-of-agent enforcement loop the market openly says no standard owns; AP2/ACP/x402 define authorization artifacts but explicitly do not revoke or refuse at execution time. Pairing budget refusal with the capability gate makes the ceiling cryptographically bound, not advisory.
ideas.risk: BudgetEnforcer holds counters in process memory and BudgetTree takes a caller-supplied SpendSnapshot; parallel worktrees drafting against one cap need a shared, durable, concurrency-safe ledger that does not exist yet (the chio-store-sqlite snapshot is out of scope of chio-metering).

ideas.title: Per-worktree non-custodial USDC wallet with x402 prepaid authorization
ideas.one_liner: Every Orca git worktree gets its own did:chio key and a stablecoin spend authority that pays x402-priced endpoints per call, never holding custody.
ideas.description: When Orca spins up an isolated worktree, mint a did:chio identity and bind it to an EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization signed offline (PreparedTransferWithAuthorization in chio-settle/payments.rs), capped by the worktree's budget slice. When an agent hits an HTTP 402, chio-settle builds X402PaymentRequirements (PrepaidAuthorization mode) and the kernel meters the call. Funds move agent-wallet -> provider on Base/Solana with no Chio-held balance, so the product stays out of money-transmitter scope (custody_boundary_explicit / external_execution_authoritative=false). The worktree sidebar shows a 'wallet' chip with remaining USDC and a live tx feed.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle (payments.rs: X402PaymentRequirements, X402SettlementMode::PrepaidAuthorization, Eip3009Domain, prepare_transfer_with_authorization), chio-did
ideas.orca_surface: New commerce:* IPC namespace + worktree sidebar 'wallet' chip; an `orca commerce buy <url>` CLI verb in src/cli/specs that an agent invokes when it gets a 402
ideas.user_value: An autonomous agent can pay for a paid API/data/compute call mid-run with a hard, cryptographically-capped USDC budget, and the operator never has to pre-fund a custodial account or hand the agent a raw card.
ideas.moat: The EIP-3009 authorization is signed by the same did:chio key the kernel meters and the capability token binds (one key for identity, payment, and authorization). Competitors hand agents an API key into a hosted wallet; Chio's spend is non-custodial and kernel-enforced, not prompt-trusted.
ideas.risk: Requires a real on-chain leg (feature=web3) and a funded operator-side EOA per worktree or an ERC-4337 paymaster; gas/relayer UX and key custody for the wallet seed must be solved without becoming custodial.

ideas.title: On-chain anchored receipt tab: every paid agent action gets a Bitcoin/Solana inclusion proof
ideas.one_liner: Orca's review pane shows each settlement receipt with a one-click cryptographic anchor proof to a public chain, so spend is tamper-evidently auditable.
ideas.description: After a paid tool call finalizes, the Chio receipt is folded into an AnchorBatch (chio-anchor/batch.rs) and published as an OpenTimestamps Bitcoin attestation (prepare_ots_submission) or a Solana memo (prepare_solana_memo_publication). The Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact carries the reconciled AnchorInclusionProof. In the diff/review surface next to AI diffs, add an 'Attested Receipts' tab that renders each receipt's lifecycle state (Web3SettlementLifecycleState: Settled/Reversed/ChargedBack...) plus a verified inclusion-proof badge an auditor can replay offline. Batching amortizes one Bitcoin anchor across thousands of receipts.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-anchor (batch.rs AnchorBatch/build_anchor_batch, bitcoin.rs prepare_ots_submission, solana.rs prepare_solana_memo_publication, witness.rs WitnessPolicy), chio-web3 (anchors.rs AnchorInclusionProof, verify_anchor_inclusion_proof)
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Attested Receipts' tab beside the existing annotate-AI-diffs review UI in src/renderer; mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx mirrors the badge
ideas.user_value: A regulated buyer can prove, against a public chain, exactly what each autonomous agent bought and that the audit log was not edited after the fact - the tamper-evident trail the market admits does not exist.
ideas.moat: Receipt-to-public-chain anchoring with replayable non-inclusion/inclusion proofs and a WitnessPolicy freshness ceiling is the audit-trail standard nobody else ships; payment rails (ACP/AP2/x402) explicitly punt on tamper-evident logs.
ideas.risk: Bitcoin OTS confirmation latency means anchors are eventually-final, not instant; the UI must clearly distinguish 'submitted' from 'confirmed' so reviewers do not over-trust a pending anchor.

ideas.title: Settlement watchdog as an Orca background task that pages a phone only on stuck money
ideas.one_liner: Wire chio-settle's escrow/finality/bond watchdog into Orca's 'notify me' loop so humans are interrupted only when funds are actually stuck.
ideas.description: chio-settle/automation.rs SettlementWatchdogJob already classifies EscrowTimeout, FinalityObservation, and BondExpiry events into outcomes (DuplicateSuppressed, DelayedButSafe, ManualOverrideRequired). Run it as an Orca background task behind the commerce sidecar. Reorgs, timed-out escrows, and chargebacks (Web3SettlementLifecycleState::Reorged/TimedOut/ChargedBack) surface as Orca notifications, but only ManualOverrideRequired pages the operator's phone via the existing mobile companion notification path. Everything else self-heals with duplicate suppression.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle (automation.rs SettlementWatchdogJob, SettlementWatchdogKind, SettlementAutomationOutcome), chio-web3 (settlement.rs Web3SettlementLifecycleState), chio-anchor (automation.rs AnchorAutomationJob for the anchor-publish side)
ideas.orca_surface: Background task behind commerce:* sidecar feeding Orca's existing notifications subsystem; mobile push to pair.tsx-paired device on ManualOverrideRequired
ideas.user_value: Cross-border stablecoin settlement runs unattended and self-corrects; the operator is woken only for genuinely stuck money (a reorg'd release or an expired escrow), not for routine confirmations.
ideas.moat: A settlement state machine with duplicate suppression and a human-circuit-breaker tied to a phone is the 'no $47k runaway agent' control loop; plain agent runners have dashboards, not an out-of-agent enforcement+notification loop.
