ideas.risk: False-quiet risk: tuning the DelayedButSafe vs ManualOverrideRequired threshold wrong either spams the operator or hides a real loss; needs conservative defaults and an operator override.

ideas.title: Cross-border instant settlement with oracle-attested FX evidence baked into the receipt
ideas.one_liner: Agent in one currency pays a provider quoting another; Chio settles in USDC and binds a signed Chainlink/Pyth FX conversion proof to the receipt.
ideas.description: For a cross-border agent-to-provider payment, chio-link/convert.rs converts the quoted amount and the settlement carries an OracleConversionEvidence (chio-web3/anchors.rs validate_oracle_conversion_evidence) that pins rate, denominator, source authority, and max_age. chio-link/circuit_breaker.rs ensure_within_threshold refuses to settle if the oracle diverges or is stale (Web3SettlementSupportBoundary.oracle_evidence_required_for_fx=true). The receipt is the auditable artifact showing the exact rate used. This is where web3 beats fiat: instant 24/7 cross-border settlement in USDC with a cryptographically attested FX rate, versus multi-day correspondent banking.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-link (convert.rs convert_units, circuit_breaker.rs divergence_bps/ensure_within_threshold, pyth.rs/chainlink.rs), chio-web3 (anchors.rs OracleConversionEvidence + validate_oracle_conversion_evidence, settlement.rs oracle_evidence_required_for_fx)
ideas.orca_surface: FX line rendered inside the 'Attested Receipts' tab showing source rate + age + divergence; an `orca commerce price <resource> --in <ccy>` CLI verb that previews the converted cost before the agent commits
ideas.user_value: Two agents/orgs in different currencies transact instantly and continuously, with the FX rate provably fair and fresh, instead of waiting days for a bank wire with an opaque spread.
ideas.moat: Settlement that refuses to execute on a stale or divergent oracle and embeds the rate proof in the receipt is a fairness guarantee no card/PSP rail offers; the circuit breaker is fail-closed, matching the house rule.
ideas.risk: Live oracle feeds (Pyth/Chainlink) add an external dependency and a new manipulation surface; aggressive divergence thresholds can block legitimate settlements during volatile markets.

ideas.title: When web3 vs fiat: a rail-routing 'Mullet' switch driven by the support-boundary flags
ideas.one_liner: Orca picks the rail per transaction - x402/USDC for high-volume agent-to-agent micropayments, signed fiat instruction for human-facing buys - and shows why.
ideas.description: Expose the Web3SettlementSupportBoundary and CapitalExecutionInstructionSupportBoundary flags as a routing decision: small, high-frequency, agent-to-agent calls go on-chain via chio-settle (x402/EIP-3009, ERC-4337 paymaster for gasless), while large or consumer-facing buys emit a SignedCapitalExecutionInstruction over a Manual/Wire fiat rail (CapitalExecutionRailKind) for a licensed custodian to execute. Because the credit layer is custody-neutral by default (automatic_capital_execution_supported=false), Chio never moves fiat itself - it routes and attests. The CLI/UI explains the choice (cost, finality, custody, jurisdiction).
ideas.chio_capability: chio-web3 (settlement.rs Web3SettlementSupportBoundary, Web3SettlementPath), chio-credit (capital_and_execution.rs SignedCapitalExecutionInstruction, CapitalExecutionRailKind Manual/Ach/Wire/Web3, support boundaries), chio-settle (payments.rs Erc4337PaymasterPolicy for gasless)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Settlement rail' selector + rationale chip in the worktree commerce panel; `orca commerce route <amount> <ccy>` returns the chosen rail and reason as signed JSON
ideas.user_value: Operators get the right rail automatically - cheap instant stablecoin for machine-to-machine spend, compliant fiat-with-custodian for the moments that need it - without hand-wiring either, and with a recorded justification.
ideas.moat: A single attested substrate that spans both rails (back-of-app stablecoin, front-of-app fiat) with the custody boundary explicit in signed artifacts is the developer-first alternative to closed hyperscaler stacks; the routing rationale is itself an auditable artifact.
ideas.risk: The fiat leg only emits an instruction; closing the loop still needs a licensed custody/BaaS partner, so 'fiat settlement' is not end-to-end in-repo and must be marketed honestly as partner-dependent.

ideas.bold_bet: Make the forked Orca the first agent cockpit where every paid action a worktree takes is a non-custodial USDC payment whose receipt is anchored to a public chain (Bitcoin OTS / Solana memo via chio-anchor) and carries an oracle-attested FX proof (chio-link) and a settlement lifecycle (chio-web3) - shipping the tamper-evident, out-of-agent enforcement + audit layer that the whole agentic-commerce market admits is missing, while staying off the money-transmitter bright line because Chio only signs instructions and proves settlement, never custodies funds.

ideas.title: Counterparty Trust Card (the headline 'who am I paying' surface)
ideas.one_liner: Before any agent transacts with another agent or paid tool server, Orca renders a live, verified trust card: did:chio identity, TrustTier, reputation tier, revocation freshness, and the exact gate that must pass.
ideas.description: Each worktree/agent gets a did:chio (Ed25519 key, self-certifying, no registry). When agent A is about to pay agent B or a tool server, Orca runs present_agent_passport against a create_passport_presentation_challenge over B's AgentPassport, synthesizes TrustTier (Unverified/Attested/Verified/Premier from trust_tier.rs), checks a chio-revocation-oracle non-inclusion proof for freshness, and renders a card. The card is not decorative: it shows pass/fail against a signed PassportVerifierPolicy (min_composite_score, min_reliability, issuer_allowlist, max_attestation_age_days). The kernel refuses the spend if the policy fails, so the card is the human-readable face of a fail-closed gate.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-did (DidChio), chio-credentials (present_agent_passport, AgentPassport, TrustTier, PassportVerifierPolicy), chio-revocation-oracle (NonInclusionProof)
ideas.orca_surface: New renderer panel docked to the worktree/agent view (sibling of the existing agent-trust.ts 'mark trusted' surface), fed by a new commerce:* IPC handler; a compact 'trust chip' in the worktree sidebar expands to the full card
ideas.user_value: A developer (or an autonomous agent) sees exactly who the counterparty is and whether it cleared policy before money moves, instead of a raw log line. Turns identity+reputation+revocation into one glanceable, gating decision.
ideas.moat: No agent runner has out-of-agent identity+reputation+revocation fused into a single fail-closed gate. The verifier policy is signed and the passport is cryptographically the same key that pays, so the card cannot be spoofed by the agent it describes.
ideas.risk: Counterparty must present a passport; for cold counterparties with no corpus the card is mostly 'Unverified', which could feel empty until reputation accrues.

ideas.title: Signed Verifier Policy as a per-worktree 'who you may pay' allowlist
ideas.one_liner: Operators set a signed PassportVerifierPolicy per worktree-group that hard-gates which counterparties an autonomous agent may transact with, by issuer, tier, reliability floor, and attestation freshness.
ideas.description: create_signed_passport_verifier_policy already produces a signed, time-bounded SignedPassportVerifierPolicy carrying issuer_allowlist, min_composite_score, min_reliability, min_delegation_hygiene, max_boundary_pressure, min_receipt_count, max_attestation_age_days, require_enterprise_identity_provenance, and require_active_lifecycle. Expose it as 'orca commerce policy set' plus a renderer editor. Every paid tool call from an agent in that group evaluates the counterparty passport against the active policy; ensure_signed_passport_verifier_policy_active enforces the validity window. This is the concrete, signed answer to the '$47k runaway agent' story: the agent literally cannot pay a counterparty outside the policy because enforcement is in the kernel, not the prompt.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credentials (SignedPassportVerifierPolicy, create_signed_passport_verifier_policy, ensure_signed_passport_verifier_policy_active, evaluate_agent_passport)
ideas.orca_surface: New 'orca commerce policy' CLI verb (spec+handler, mirroring src/cli/handlers); a renderer policy editor next to the rate-limit/usage settings; the active policy id shown on every Counterparty Trust Card
ideas.user_value: Operators get a signed, auditable, time-bounded counterparty allowlist for autonomous spend that survives across parallel worktrees and is enforced before settlement, not after.
ideas.moat: The policy is itself a signed artifact (non-repudiable: you can prove what the rule was at decision time) and the same evaluator already exists and is tested. Card-network consent rules map directly onto these fields.
ideas.risk: Policy authors can set floors too loose; needs sane signed defaults and a 'deny-by-default if no policy' fail-closed posture.

ideas.title: KYA credential: bind a did:chio agent key to a verified legal entity
ideas.one_liner: Add a Know-Your-Agent ReputationCredential subtype that binds an agent's did:chio key to a KYC-verified human or business principal, issued by a KYC provider whose issuer identity is pinned via chio-attest-verify and revocable through the revocation oracle.
ideas.description: This fills the single biggest gap in the trust layer: did:chio and passports prove key control and behavior but nothing binds the key to a verified legal person/org (the EnterpriseIdentityProvenance is IdP provenance, not KYC). Define a new credential in the existing ReputationCredential/AgentPassport machinery whose issuer is a KYA provider, pin that issuer's identity with chio-attest-verify (Fulcio chain + OIDC issuer pinning, the same module that handles Sigstore/TEE), and make presence-of-KYA a gate via PassportVerifierPolicy.issuer_allowlist + a require flag. High-value transactions then demand a KYA credential. Revocation rides the existing chio-revocation-oracle passport_bridge. This is exactly what Mastercard Agentic Tokens, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, and Travel Rule assume exists but do not provide a portable, rail-agnostic form of.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credentials (ReputationCredential, AgentPassport, issuer_allowlist), chio-attest-verify (issuer pinning for the KYA provider), chio-did (subject key binding), chio-revocation-oracle (passport_bridge)
ideas.orca_surface: Mobile QR pairing flow (mobile/app/pair*.tsx) becomes the human KYC step that mints the KYA credential to a worktree's did:chio; a 'Legal entity: verified by <issuer>' row on the Counterparty Trust Card; 'orca commerce kya present' CLI verb
ideas.user_value: Lets a Chio agent prove to a merchant or peer agent that it is a genuine, legally-accountable, mandate-backed customer without locking into one network's closed token, satisfying the human-principal assumption baked into KYC/AML.
ideas.moat: Portable, rail-agnostic legal-entity binding reusing the credential/tier/revocation stack already built; competitors offer this only inside a single card network or wallet silo. Directly answers the regulatory 'no identity for agents' gap.
ideas.risk: Requires integrating a real licensed KYC/identity-proofing provider; the credential is only as strong as that issuer, and onboarding friction is real.

ideas.title: Deal-time reputation handshake over the protocol adapters
ideas.one_liner: Expose a signed reputation-snapshot request/response so a counterparty agent can pull a fresh, integrity-checked reputation summary at the moment of transacting, served as a metered Chio tool over A2A/MCP.
ideas.description: Reputation today is local-corpus-only: compute_local_scorecard needs the caller to assemble a corpus, and portable_reputation.rs (PORTABLE_REPUTATION_SUMMARY_SCHEMA, plus PortableNegativeEventKind: PaymentDefault/FraudSignal/DisputeLoss) is a credential format, not a live feed. Wrap it in a request/response handshake: a relying agent asks 'show me your current reputation' and gets back a signed normalized LocalReputationScorecard summary (8 metrics: boundary_pressure, reliability, least_privilege, delegation_hygiene, etc.) it can verify offline, including any signed negative events. Serve it through chio-a2a-adapter / chio-mcp-adapter so external agents over A2A/MCP can request a Chio trust attestation as a paid, metered tool. This turns reputation into a discoverable, pull-at-deal-time signal, not a static badge.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-reputation (LocalReputationScorecard, compute_local_scorecard), chio-credentials (portable_reputation: PORTABLE_REPUTATION_SUMMARY_SCHEMA, PortableNegativeEventKind), protocol adapters (chio-a2a-adapter, chio-mcp-adapter)
ideas.orca_surface: 'orca commerce reputation pull <did>' CLI verb; the Counterparty Trust Card 'Reputation' section calls it live and renders the 8-metric breakdown plus negative-event flags; quick-open across worktrees can surface a peer's current tier
ideas.user_value: An agent can check a counterparty's current, signed reputation (including payment defaults and dispute losses) right before transacting, instead of trusting a stale or self-asserted badge.
ideas.moat: Receipt-derived, integrity-checked (unsigned receipts score zero), Sybil-resistant per-feed-floored reputation delivered as a live handshake is strictly better than x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray model, which has no seller reputation at all.
ideas.risk: Pull-time reputation can leak behavioral detail; needs the selective-disclosure path (chio-selective-disclosure / BBS+) so a counterparty proves a floor without exposing the full factor breakdown.

ideas.title: Pheromone swarm-trust meter for tool servers and peer agents
ideas.one_liner: Surface a live, decentralized 'is the swarm currently trusting this counterparty' signal in the Orca fleet view, computed from gossiped, cost-committed pheromone deposits.
ideas.description: chio-pheromone is a signed, Merkle-committed stigmergic substrate: operators emit PheromoneDeposit (with optional PheromoneCostCommitment so signals are not free to forge), and PheromoneConcentration aggregates total_strength, distinct_origin_pairs, and peak_confidence per subject_class across operators, with scarcity policy, newcomer_horizon_epochs (a newcomer-discount window), and a runtime trust-floor state. Gossiped via chio-federation pheromone_gossip. Render concentration as a real-time 'swarm trust' badge on the Counterparty Trust Card and as a heat indicator in the fleet/worktree list: a tool server that just started misbehaving across many operators lights up before its credential or static reputation reflects it. This is a behavioral-consensus channel distinct from credentials and reputation, and the cost-commitment + distinct-origin-pairs design resists a single operator flooding the signal.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-pheromone (PheromoneDeposit, PheromoneConcentration, PheromoneCostCommitment, PheromoneRuntimeTrustFloorState, newcomer horizon), chio-federation (pheromone_gossip)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'swarm trust' heat badge in the fleet/worktree list and on the Counterparty Trust Card; an optional notification when a counterparty a worktree depends on crosses a concentration threshold (reuses Orca's 'notify when an agent needs you' machinery)
ideas.user_value: Early, decentralized warning that a counterparty is going bad, sourced from many operators' real behavior rather than one party's say-so, with newcomers given a fair grace window rather than a cold-start zero.
ideas.moat: A cost-committed, Sybil-resistant, cross-operator emergent-trust signal is a channel no competing cockpit has; it complements (not duplicates) static credentials and is hard to replicate without the federation + signed-substrate plumbing already in-repo.
ideas.risk: Requires multiple operators gossiping to be meaningful (network-effect cold start); needs careful UI framing so an emergent signal is not read as a hard verdict on a single honest newcomer.

ideas.bold_bet: The KYA credential (idea 3): make did:chio the key that is both KYC-bound to a real legal entity and the key that signs payment and that the kernel meters. Today every agent-commerce stack (Mastercard Agentic Tokens, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, Skyfire KYA, Travel Rule) assumes a 'verified agent tied to a human principal' exists but each only delivers it inside its own closed token or wallet. Chio already has the three hard pieces (self-certifying did:chio identity, a signed-credential + tier + verifier-policy stack, and a sparse-Merkle revocation oracle) and is missing only the legal-entity binding. Add one KYA ReputationCredential subtype issued by a licensed KYC provider whose issuer is pinned via chio-attest-verify, gate high-value spend on it through PassportVerifierPolicy, mint it via the phone-tap pairing flow, and the forked cockpit becomes the first place an autonomous agent can prove to any counterparty, over any rail, that a real accountable entity stands behind it. That is the wedge that turns 'attested commerce' from a demo into something a regulated buyer can deploy.

ideas.lens: Compliance, audit & enterprise export (the CFO/CISO buyer)

ideas.title: Per-worktree Session Compliance Certificate on merge
ideas.one_liner: Every time an agent's worktree is merged, Chio emits a signed, auditor-verifiable certificate proving the whole session stayed in scope, in budget, and never bypassed a guard.
ideas.description: Orca's defining act is fan-out-then-merge-the-winner. Hook the merge path so that before a branch lands, the forked cockpit shells `chio cert generate --session <worktreeId> --receipt-db <db>` (the exact handler in crates/products/chio-cli/src/cert.rs) over that worktree's receipt log. The returned ComplianceCertificate (spec/COMPLIANCE-CERTIFICATE.md, schema chio.compliance.certificate.v1) asserts all signatures valid, chain continuous with no gaps, scope_compliant, budget_compliant, guards_compliant, and zero anomalies, signed Ed25519 over RFC-8785 canonical JSON. A red/green 'Session Certified' badge renders next to the merge button in the annotate-AI-diffs review pane; clicking opens `chio cert inspect`. A non-compliant session refuses to issue a cert (fail-closed typed BudgetExceeded/ScopeViolation/GuardBypass abort), so the badge cannot go green on a session that escaped its boundary.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-cli cert.rs + chio-acp-proxy generate_compliance_certificate / verify_compliance_certificate (spec/COMPLIANCE-CERTIFICATE.md)
ideas.orca_surface: annotate-AI-diffs review pane: a 'Session Certified' badge gating the merge button, plus a new `orca commerce cert` CLI verb wrapping `chio cert generate/verify/inspect`
ideas.user_value: A CISO gets a one-file, offline-verifiable proof that a merged AI change never overspent or bypassed a control, attached to the exact diff a human approved. No log-scraping, no trust in dashboards.
ideas.moat: The certificate is cryptographic and replayable without a running Chio node (FullBundle mode re-verifies every receipt signature). Plain MIT agent runners have no signed-session artifact, only telemetry. This is the artifact the market admits does not exist (no audit-trail standard for AI logs).
ideas.risk: Requires per-worktree receipt logs to actually be populated, which depends on the metering/gate sidecar landing first; without real receipts the cert is over an empty session (the EmptySession error path).

ideas.title: Stream every agent decision to the company SIEM as OCSF Authorization events
ideas.one_liner: A 'Compliance Sinks' settings panel pipes every Chio receipt (allow and deny) into Splunk/Sentinel/Elastic/Datadog as OCSF 1.3.0 Authorization events, live.
ideas.description: chio-siem already maps each ChioReceipt to a fully-formed OCSF 1.3.0 class_uid 3002 Authorization event (crates/observability/chio-siem/src/ocsf.rs) and ships shipping exporters: Splunk HEC, Elasticsearch bulk, Datadog, Sumo Logic, CEF, generic webhook, and an OCSF->AWS Security Lake sink, all with a dead-letter queue, rate limiting, and a redaction layer. Expose these as a 'Compliance Sinks' tab in the forked cockpit's settings (sitting beside the existing rate-limits/usage UI) where an admin pastes a Splunk HEC token or Sentinel/Elastic endpoint. The crate's OcsfAuthority logic is the differentiator: an Allow receipt whose signer is not a trusted kernel is exported as 'Unverified' / status Other, not a green Success, so a forged or untrusted decision can never masquerade as an authorized one in the SOC's dashboard.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-siem (ocsf.rs receipt_to_ocsf, exporters: SplunkHecExporter, ElasticsearchExporter, DatadogExporter, OCSF Security Lake sink, dlq.rs, ratelimit.rs, redaction.rs)
ideas.orca_surface: new 'Compliance Sinks' settings tab (next to rate-limits/usage panels) + a `commerce:siemConfig` IPC namespace; per-receipt fan-out fires from the agent-hooks bus
ideas.user_value: Agent activity lands in the tools the SOC already runs (Splunk/Sentinel/Chronicle via Security Lake) in the open standard their correlation rules speak, with deny events pre-tagged High severity for alerting.
ideas.moat: Out-of-the-box OCSF mapping with cryptographic trust grading (untrusted-signer Allow downgraded to Unverified) is unique. Competing cockpits emit PostHog analytics, not normalized, signed security events a SOC can alert on.
ideas.risk: OCSF schema and SIEM vendor APIs drift; the exporters need version pinning and the redaction layer must be enforced before egress so receipt parameters never leak PII to the SIEM.

ideas.title: One-click regulator evidence package (EU AI Act Art 19 / PCI-DSS Req 10)
ideas.one_liner: An 'Export Audit Package' button produces a tarball an auditor verifies offline, with Merkle inclusion proofs for every receipt and a control-map binding each Chio control to a named EU AI Act / PCI clause.
ideas.description: `chio evidence export` (docs/release/COMPLIANCE_EVIDENCE_EXPORT_PLAN.md) already emits a turnkey package: receipts.ndjson, child-receipts, checkpoints, capability-lineage, inclusion-proofs.ndjson (one Merkle proof per checkpointed receipt), retention.json, and the policy source, plus tenant-scoped disclosure notices that document exactly which cross-tenant aggregate fields a scoped export inherently reveals. Layer chio-enterprise-export's signed EnterpriseVerifierReport on top: it binds a ControlEvidenceMap (control_id + control_family + claim_ref + gate_ref, where the gate_ref must exist in the evidence graph or verification fails with 'control gate did not run'), a DataGovernanceReport (region-residency check, retention class, legal_hold must be not_held or export is blocked, and any PII-classified field must have export_action == redacted), an ApprovalCase (quorum of named approvers, not expired), and a TelemetryProjection requiring allow/denied_guard/risk_verifier events. The cockpit ships the prebaked EU AI Act Art 19, PCI-DSS v4, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF mapping docs (docs/compliance/*) as the human-readable control catalog the ControlEvidenceMap cites.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-enterprise-export (verify_enterprise_export, ControlEvidenceMap, DataGovernanceReport with forced-PII-redaction, ApprovalCase quorum) + `chio evidence export` (inclusion-proofs, disclosure notices) + docs/compliance/*
ideas.orca_surface: an 'Export Audit Package' action in the review/source-control surface and a `commerce:exportEvidence` IPC handler; the bundle downloads as a dir or tarball
ideas.user_value: When a regulator or PCI QSA asks 'show me what your autonomous agents did,' the buyer hands over one verifiable package that maps Chio controls to the exact Article/Requirement and proves no receipt was tampered with or omitted.
ideas.moat: Legal-hold enforcement, forced PII redaction, approval-quorum gating, and per-clause control mapping baked into a signed verifier report is years of compliance engineering. The export verifies with no running node, defeating the 'logs could have been edited' objection that the payment protocols punt on.
ideas.risk: The compliance mappings are drafts pending legal review; over-claiming 'EU AI Act compliant' is a liability. Frame it as evidence input to a RoC/SAQ, not certification.

ideas.title: Policy-as-code spend governor with diff-on-change in the cockpit
ideas.one_liner: A YAML HushSpec file in the repo defines hard per-agent spend velocity and approval thresholds; the cockpit shows a policy diff and the policy_hash that gets stamped into every receipt.
ideas.description: chio-policy compiles a HushSpec YAML (crates/guards/chio-policy/src/models.rs) into runtime guards, including a VelocityRule with max_spend_per_window in integer minor units, approve_above thresholds with currency, and BudgetExhausted as a first-class state-transition trigger. Surface the active policy file in a 'Spend Policy' panel; when an operator edits it, the cockpit renders a before/after diff (reusing the merge semantics in crates/guards/chio-policy/src/merge.rs) and computes the new policy_hash. Because every ChioReceipt embeds policy_hash, the review pane can prove which policy version authorized each spend, and a policy change becomes a reviewable, attributable event (PCI Req 6.5 'changes to systems are managed', mapped in docs/compliance/pci-dss-v4.md). Invalid policies reject at load time (fail-closed house rule), so a typo cannot silently disable a spend cap.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-policy (HushSpec models.rs VelocityRule max_spend_per_window / approve_above, BudgetExhausted trigger, compiler.rs, merge.rs, version.rs; policy_hash stamped per receipt)
ideas.orca_surface: a 'Spend Policy' editor panel with before/after diff and live policy_hash, wired to a `commerce:policy` IPC namespace and an `orca commerce policy lint/apply` CLI verb
ideas.user_value: The CFO sets spending rules as version-controlled code reviewed in PRs, not a dashboard slider, and every receipt cryptographically names the policy version that approved it.
ideas.moat: Policy-as-code where the policy hash is bound into the tamper-evident receipt is a closed-loop control-to-evidence chain. Dashboard spend caps (the '$47k runaway agent' anti-pattern) are observability; this is enforcement with attribution.
ideas.risk: HushSpec is a learning curve for non-engineers; needs sane shipped rulesets (the crate already ships strict/ai-agent/cicd presets) and a guided editor so a CFO is not hand-writing YAML.

ideas.title: Phone-tap approval that mints a signed, replayable consent artifact
ideas.one_liner: When an agent's spend trips an approval threshold, the Orca mobile companion pushes a request; the human's tap mints a signed ApprovalCase bound into the audit trail, closing AP2's 'consent ambiguity' dispute gap.
ideas.description: Reuse the mobile companion's existing notify-and-steer + QR-pairing flow as the human circuit-breaker. When chio-policy's approve_above threshold or a BudgetExhausted transition fires, the cockpit pushes 'Agent X wants to spend $Y' to the phone. The tap produces a chio-enterprise-export ApprovalCase (schema chio.enterprise.approval-case.v1: decision == approved, decision_subject, named approvers, required_quorum, issued_at < expires_at, all verified in crates/platform/chio-enterprise-export/src/artifacts.rs validate_approval_case) that becomes a node in the transaction passport's evidence graph and is required by the evidence export's CLAIM_EXPORT_APPROVAL_BOUND. The approval is thus not a log line but a quorum-checked, time-bounded, signed artifact an auditor (or a court, per the regulatory digest's 'untested authorization trails') can replay.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-enterprise-export ApprovalCase (validate_approval_case: quorum + non-expiry + approved decision) gated by chio-policy approve_above / BudgetExhausted; bound into chio-transaction-passport evidence graph
ideas.orca_surface: the mobile companion push-approval flow (pair*.tsx + notifications) mints the ApprovalCase; desktop review pane shows the consent artifact inline on the receipt
ideas.user_value: High-value autonomous spend always has a human in the loop, and that consent is a verifiable artifact tied to the exact transaction, not a Slack thumbs-up nobody can later prove.
ideas.moat: Binding the consent moment to a quorum-checked signed artifact that is a required claim in the evidence export directly attacks AP2's number-one named dispute driver (consent and intent ambiguity). No wallet or card-network rail produces a replayable consent object.
ideas.risk: The agent-hooks bus is currently fire-and-forget; making spend block on a synchronous phone approval requires the reserved ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION wire change to a blocking allow/deny gate, plus a sane offline/timeout fallback that fails closed.

ideas.title: Tamper-evidence monitor: continuous Merkle checkpoint verification with SOC alert
ideas.one_liner: A background task continuously re-verifies the receipt log's Merkle checkpoints and inclusion proofs; any gap, reorder, or broken root pages the SOC and freezes evidence export.
ideas.description: The audit log is only trustworthy if its integrity is actively checked, not assumed. Wire a cockpit background task (mirroring the terminal-daemon sidecar pattern) that periodically rebuilds inclusion proofs from stored receipt bytes against signed KernelCheckpoint roots (the exact mechanism documented in docs/compliance/eu-ai-act-article-19.md Annex IV Section 7 and exercised by inclusion_proof_verifies_against_stored_checkpoint). On any discontinuity it (a) emits a high-severity chio-siem alert (alerting.rs AlertSeverity, fanned to Datadog/webhook), and (b) flips the 'Export Audit Package' button to blocked because a tampered log must not produce a clean evidence bundle. chio-lineage (anchor.rs, diff.rs) provides the cross-source reconciliation so an operator can see exactly which seq range diverged.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-kernel checkpoint inclusion-proof verification (build_inclusion_proof / verify_checkpoint_signature) + chio-siem alerting.rs + chio-lineage (anchor.rs, diff.rs)
ideas.orca_surface: a persistent 'Audit Integrity' status chip in the cockpit chrome + a background Monitor task; integrity failure disables the evidence-export action and fires a SIEM alert
ideas.user_value: The buyer can prove the audit trail is not just signed once but continuously verified intact, so 'someone edited the logs' is a detectable, alerted, export-blocking event.
ideas.moat: Continuous tamper-evidence with an alert-and-freeze response turns a static Merkle log into a live integrity control (PCI Req 10.3 / 11.5). MIT runners have crash reporting, not cryptographic log-integrity monitoring.
ideas.risk: Re-verifying large logs is CPU-heavy; needs incremental verification windowed by checkpoint batch and a clear policy for what 'blocked export' means operationally so it does not become a nuisance that operators disable.

ideas.bold_bet: Make the forked cockpit the neutral, offline-verifiable AUDIT PLANE for autonomous agent commerce: every merged worktree ships a signed Session Compliance Certificate, every decision streams to the SOC as OCSF, and one button produces a regulator-ready evidence package whose ControlEvidenceMap binds each Chio control to a named EU AI Act / PCI-DSS clause with Merkle inclusion proofs that verify with no running node. The wedge is precisely the white space the market admits is empty (no audit-trail standard for AI logs, untested authorization trails) and it is sellable to the CFO/CISO today because the certificate, the OCSF exporters, the `chio evidence export` package, and the per-clause compliance mappings already exist in-tree (chio-cli cert.rs, chio-siem ocsf.rs, chio-enterprise-export, docs/compliance/*). Chio competes with nobody's payment rail and instead becomes the thing every rail needs: provable, exportable, court-defensible evidence that an autonomous agent stayed inside its authorized boundary.

ideas.lens: Mobile spend approvals (extend Orca mobile companion)

ideas.title: Secure-Enclave approver key: the phone IS the signer, biometrics ARE the approval
ideas.one_liner: Make the user's phone the sole holder of the GovernedApprovalToken approver key, so a Face ID / fingerprint unlock physically produces the signature that releases an agent's spend.
ideas.description: The kernel's HITL flow (crates/kernel/chio-kernel/src/approval.rs) already requires that the approver's private key sign a GovernedApprovalToken binding approver pubkey + subject pubkey + governed_intent_hash + request_id. Today that key would live on a server. Instead, generate the approver Ed25519 keypair inside the iOS Secure Enclave / Android Keystore during the existing Orca pairing flow (mobile/app/pair*.tsx), register only its PublicKey into the kernel's trusted_approvers set, and gate every signing operation behind LocalAuthentication / BiometricPrompt. The biometric unlock is not cosmetic: it is the literal precondition for GovernedApprovalToken::sign, so no Orca desktop, server, or compromised laptop can ever mint an approval. parameter_hash binds the signature to the exact tool+args+amount, so a mutated charge fails verify_against.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-core-types GovernedApprovalToken::sign + chio-kernel ApprovalRequest.trusted_approvers / ApprovalToken::verify_against
ideas.orca_surface: New mobile/app/approvals/[id].tsx review sheet; key minted in the existing QR pairing flow (mobile/app/pair-confirm.tsx); approver pubkey registered via a new commerce:* IPC handler in src/main/ipc/
ideas.user_value: A spend cannot be approved unless the human physically holds the phone and passes biometrics. Approval becomes a hardware-backed cryptographic act, not a button on a server someone could script.
ideas.moat: Competitors' mobile approvals are UI buttons that hit an API the server trusts; here the server literally cannot forge an approval because the only approver key is sealed in the phone's secure element. This is non-repudiation by construction, not by policy.
ideas.risk: Secure Enclave only does P-256 (secp256r1), not Ed25519. GovernedApprovalToken supports algorithm tagging + sign_with_backend, so this works via a SigningBackend, but you must wire a P-256 backend and confirm the kernel verifier accepts it. Key loss on device requires a re-pairing / approver-rotation path.

ideas.title: Push-to-approve channel: APNs/FCM as a first-class ApprovalChannel
ideas.one_liner: Implement a PushApprovalChannel that delivers each pending ApprovalRequest as a rich, actionable push notification with the full spend envelope, reusing Orca's existing 'notify when agent finishes' pipe.
ideas.description: chio-kernel's ApprovalChannel trait (approval_channels.rs) is a pluggable dispatch sink already implemented by WebhookChannel. Add a PushApprovalChannel whose dispatch() sends an APNs/FCM payload carrying approval_id, the agent subject, summary, triggered_by, and the governed_intent (max_amount, seller from GovernedCommerceContext, metered_billing quote). Render it as an iOS interactive notification with Approve / Deny actions and the dollar amount on the lock screen. The fail-closed property is preserved verbatim: push delivery failure leaves the request pending and queryable via GET /approvals/pending, so a dropped notification never silently approves or auto-denies. Tapping Approve deep-links (chio://approve/{id}) into the biometric sign sheet from idea 1.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-kernel ApprovalChannel trait + ApprovalRequest (governed_intent, triggered_by, expires_at); chio-http-core GET /approvals/pending as the reconciliation fallback
ideas.orca_surface: New PushApprovalChannel registered on the kernel sidecar; reuses Orca's mobile notification/device-registry plumbing (src/main/runtime/device-registry.ts) and the new chio:// deep-link protocol-client registration
ideas.user_value: The user is paged on their phone the instant an agent wants to spend over threshold, sees exactly what and how much, and can act from the lock screen without opening a laptop.
ideas.moat: Orca already has the mobile notification rails and device pairing; bolting the kernel's fail-closed approval semantics onto them yields a paged human circuit-breaker that the '$47k runaway agent' story sells directly against. Dropped pushes degrade safely to pending, never to spend.
ideas.risk: Push is best-effort; you must make the lock-screen action a deep-link into a signing flow, not a direct allow, or you reintroduce a server-trusted approval. APNs payload size caps mean large intents need a fetch-on-open.

ideas.title: Standing-allowance card: mint BatchApprovals from the phone with a slider
ideas.one_liner: Let the user pre-approve a class of agent spend (this server/tool, up to $X per call, $Y total, N calls, expiring in H hours) from a mobile sheet, so routine purchases stop paging them.
ideas.description: The kernel already models exactly this: BatchApproval (approval.rs) pre-approves a server_pattern + tool_pattern with max_amount_per_call, max_total_amount, max_calls, and a not_before/not_after window, and BatchApprovalStore.find_matching auto-satisfies in-policy calls without a fresh HITL round trip. Surface it as an Orca mobile 'Standing Allowance' card where the human drags sliders for per-call cap, total cap, and TTL, then biometric-signs the batch grant. Over-threshold or out-of-pattern calls still fall through to a single push approval (idea 2). A prominent Revoke control flips BatchApproval.revoked, instantly closing the standing allowance. This is the mobile expression of a budget change, signed by the same enclave key.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-kernel BatchApproval / BatchApprovalStore (find_matching, record_usage, revoke); amounts typed as chio-core MonetaryAmount
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Allowances' tab in the mobile companion (sibling to AccountUsage.tsx); live usage bar driven by BatchApproval.used_calls / used_total_units; Revoke button wired to BatchApprovalStore.revoke
ideas.user_value: The human sets a thumb-driven spending envelope once ('agents may buy compute up to $5/call, $50 total, for the next 4 hours') and only gets paged when something exceeds it. Tighten or kill it from the phone anytime.
ideas.moat: Pre-authorized, time-boxed, per-pattern allowances with live consumption metering and one-tap revoke map cleanly onto AP2's Intent-Mandate concept but are kernel-enforced at call time, which AP2/ACP explicitly do not do. It is a real mandate the runtime obeys, not a dashboard cap.

ideas.title: Autonomy dial with bonded-tier gating, set from the phone
ideas.one_liner: A per-agent slider (Direct / Delegated / Autonomous) on mobile that sets how far an agent may transact unattended, where each higher notch demands a posted bond and a higher attested-runtime tier before the kernel will allow it.
ideas.description: GovernedAutonomyTier (chio-core capability/governance.rs) already ladders Direct -> Delegated -> Autonomous with a built-in minimum_runtime_assurance() requirement (None -> Attested -> Verified), and CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (chio-credit capital_and_execution.rs) gates execution on kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier, minimum_runtime_assurance_tier, require_locked_reserve, deny_if_bond_not_active, and deny_if_outstanding_delinquency. Expose this as a mobile dial: sliding an agent to Autonomous is a biometric-signed act that raises its maximum_autonomy_tier but only succeeds if a bond is active and the runtime is attested at the matching tier, otherwise the kernel fails closed. A master Kill Switch toggle on the same screen flips kill_switch=true and stops all unattended spend instantly.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier, require_locked_reserve, deny_if_outstanding_delinquency) + chio-core GovernedAutonomyTier
ideas.orca_surface: Per-agent settings panel in the mobile companion's session/agent view (mobile/app/sessions); master kill switch in the companion header; changes pushed to the kernel via commerce:* IPC
ideas.user_value: The human decides per agent how much rope it gets, and the system refuses to grant more autonomy than the agent's bond and runtime assurance justify. One toggle freezes everything.
ideas.moat: Tying an autonomy level to a posted bond and an attested-runtime tier, enforced in the kernel, is a defensible 'agents earn the right to spend unattended' model. The phone becomes the operator console for risk posture, not just an approve button.

ideas.title: Deny-and-revoke: one decline that signs a denial AND poisons the capability
ideas.one_liner: When the user declines a spend on their phone, the same gesture both records a signed Denied token and revokes the underlying capability via the revocation oracle, so the agent cannot simply retry.
ideas.description: Today a Denied GovernedApprovalToken stops one call but the agent's capability token may still be live for the next attempt. Wire the mobile Deny action to do two cryptographic things atomically: (1) sign a GovernedApprovalDecision::Denied token (resume_with_decision records it, with replay protection), and (2) submit the offending capability_id (carried on every ApprovalRequest) to chio-revocation-oracle's passport_bridge, publishing a new epoch-signed sparse-Merkle root whose non-inclusion proof now fails for that capability. The kernel's next capability check fails closed with a provable revocation. Offer a graduated Deny menu: 'Deny once', 'Deny and revoke this tool', 'Deny and freeze this agent' (the latter flips kill_switch from idea 4).
ideas.chio_capability: chio-kernel resume_with_decision (Denied path) + chio-revocation-oracle passport_bridge (epoch-signed roots, non-inclusion proofs) + ApprovalRequest.capability_id
ideas.orca_surface: Deny action menu on the mobile approval sheet (mobile/app/approvals/[id].tsx); a 'Revoked' badge that propagates to the desktop worktree's capability/wallet chip in src/renderer
ideas.user_value: Declining a suspicious purchase actually stops the agent, not just this one call. The human gets a hard, provable kill of the capability, with a graduated escalation from 'no this time' to 'freeze this agent'.
ideas.moat: Coupling human denial to a cryptographic, epoch-anchored revocation with non-inclusion proofs is exactly the 'enforcement lives outside agent code' gap the market admits no payment rail fills. A denied agent cannot quietly retry, and the revocation is auditable.

ideas.title: Signed approval receipts wallet on the phone, exportable for audit
ideas.one_liner: A mobile 'Approvals' history tab where every decision the user made is a stored, verifiable receipt linking the approval token to the resulting ChioReceipt and settlement, replayable offline by an auditor.
ideas.description: Every resolved approval already yields a ResolvedApproval (approver_hex, token_id, outcome, resolved_at) and the downstream tool call produces a ChioReceipt with FinancialReceiptMetadata (cost_charged, currency, SettlementStatus, root_budget_holder). Build a phone-side history that, for each entry, shows the human-signed GovernedApprovalToken, the parameter_hash it bound, and the matched signed receipt, with a Verify button that re-checks the signatures locally. An Export action emits a chio-attest-buyer BuyerAttestationPacket / ReceiptLineageBundle so the user can hand a regulator or counterparty a self-contained, replayable proof that 'a human approved this exact spend at this time and it settled.' This makes the AP2 'consent ambiguity' dispute driver concrete and reviewable.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-kernel ResolvedApproval + chio-core ChioReceipt/FinancialReceiptMetadata + chio-attest-buyer BuyerAttestationPacket / ReceiptLineageBundle (offline replay)
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Approvals' history tab in the mobile companion next to review (mobile/app/review/[worktreeId].tsx); Export sheet that writes a signed proof bundle; mirrors into the desktop 'Attested Receipts' review pane
ideas.user_value: The human carries a verifiable, exportable record of every spend they personally authorized, with cost and settlement attached, ready for a dispute, a chargeback, or a compliance review.
ideas.moat: A tamper-evident, offline-replayable record binding the human consent moment to the settled receipt is the audit-trail standard the market says does not exist. It directly serves the EU AI Act / PCI-DSS / ISO 42001 mappings Chio already ships, from a phone.

ideas.bold_bet: Make the phone the only place an agent's spend can be authorized, by holding the GovernedApprovalToken approver key exclusively in the device Secure Enclave / Keystore and gating its use behind biometrics. This collapses 'mobile approval UI' and 'cryptographic authority to spend' into a single hardware-backed act: the kernel's trusted_approvers set contains only keys that live in human-held secure elements, so no Orca server, desktop, or compromised CI can forge an approval, and every approval is a Face ID-gated Ed25519/P-256 signature bound by parameter_hash to the exact charge. It is the sharpest expression of 'enforcement outside agent code' and turns the Orca mobile companion from a notifier into the root of spend authority for the whole fleet.

ideas.title: Settlement take-rate as a signed facilitator deduction (the core money line)
ideas.one_liner: Chio earns basis points on every agent settlement it attests, charged as an explicit, receipt-bound facilitator deduction - not a hidden spread.
ideas.description: chio-settle/payments.rs already models an x402 facilitator_url and treats ERC-4337 paymaster reimbursement and Circle nanopayments as explicit settlement-side deductions. We add a ChioFacilitatorFee struct (e.g. 30-50 bps on stablecoin settlement value) that is computed at settlement time, written into the Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact, and minted as its own IouEnvelope via chio-credit/hook.rs so the fee itself is auditable. Because Chio stays non-custodial (the operator-treasury+custodian signed capital instruction moves the money), the take-rate is a service fee on attestation+facilitation, not money transmission. Unit economics: at the cited x402 ~$50M cumulative volume, 40 bps is ~$200k of fee surface today and scales linearly with agent-to-agent volume; gross margin is near-100% software since settlement compute is negligible. This is the first dollar and the one that compounds with usage.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle/src/payments.rs (x402 facilitator + paymaster/Circle explicit deductions), chio-web3/src/settlement.rs (receipt artifact), chio-credit/src/hook.rs (IouEnvelope for the fee)
ideas.orca_surface: New `orca commerce settle` CLI verb and the commerce:* IPC namespace; the fee line renders inside the per-purchase mandate->payment->receipt chain in the annotate-AI-diffs review pane, so the reviewer sees exactly what Chio charged.
ideas.user_value: Transparent, attested per-transaction pricing instead of an opaque card spread; the buyer can replay the exact fee that was charged.
ideas.moat: Competitors (x402 Bazaar, AgentCore Payments) move money but do not bind the fee into a tamper-evident receipt; Chio's fee is itself an auditable artifact, which is what regulated buyers need.
ideas.risk: Take-rate must stay clearly a facilitation/attestation fee to avoid money-transmitter classification; pricing pressure from near-zero-fee stablecoin rails caps the bps you can charge.

ideas.title: Metered cockpit billing: usage-based SaaS off BillingExport + CostQuery
ideas.one_liner: Charge per attested tool call (a small per-receipt mediation fee) and bill it straight out of the metering crate that already produces billing records.
ideas.description: chio-metering/src/export.rs already has BillingRecord, BillingExport and create_billing_export(records, exported_at), and query.rs has CostQuery/GroupBy/CostSummary that roll cost up by agent/session/tool. We monetize the cockpit itself with a metered mediation fee (e.g. a fraction of a cent per signed receipt, or a flat per-1000-mediated-calls price) derived directly from these records, with WarehouseQuery/ApiCost dimensions (chio-metering/src/cost.rs) distinguishing cheap vs expensive calls. This is monetizable first because it needs no settlement rail and no custody: the moment an Orca agent runs through the kernel, receipts exist and BillingExport can invoice them. Unit economics: COGS per mediated call is a signing + log-append op (sub-millisecond), so even $0.0005/call is high-margin; a fleet running 10M tool calls/month yields ~$5k/month from one team purely on mediation, layered on top of any flat seat price.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-metering/src/export.rs (BillingRecord/BillingExport/create_billing_export), chio-metering/src/query.rs (CostQuery/GroupBy/CostSummary), chio-metering/src/cost.rs (CostDimension incl. WarehouseQuery/ApiCost)
ideas.orca_surface: Extends Orca's existing rate-limit/usage UI (src/main/rate-limits, mobile AccountUsage.tsx) into a real spend+invoice panel; `orca commerce usage --group-by tool|agent` prints the CostQueryResult and an exportable invoice.
ideas.user_value: Pay for exactly the mediated calls you make, with a per-agent/per-tool breakdown the existing usage panel already wants to show.
ideas.moat: The billing line is derived from signed receipts, so the invoice is itself provable - no other agent cockpit can produce an auditable, replayable usage bill.
ideas.risk: Per-call mediation fees can feel like a tax on every action; must be tiny and bundled, or teams will route around the kernel for hot-path calls.

ideas.title: Marketplace fee schedule + seller bonds (take-rate on the agent tool market)
ideas.one_liner: Run the agent-to-agent tool marketplace and skim a publication + participation fee per listing while requiring sellers to post slashable bonds.
ideas.description: chio-open-market/src/fee_schedule.rs already defines a signed OpenMarketFeeScheduleArtifact carrying publication_fee, dispute_fee, market_participation_fee and OpenMarketBondRequirement/OpenMarketBondClass. We operate the registry: sellers pay to publish a Listing, pay a participation fee to stay discoverable, and post a bond (chio-open-market penalty.rs slashes it on bad service via signed evidence). Buyers' bids mint cost-capped CapabilityTokens (bidding.rs) and Chio clips the configured fee on each accepted ask. This is strictly better than x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray: economic accountability is built in. Unit economics: marketplace revenue = listing fees (recurring) + a slice of bonded GMV; the bond float is held by the custodian rail, not Chio, so we monetize the fee schedule and dispute fees without custody. Margins are high because the matching/verification is deterministic compute.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-open-market/src/fee_schedule.rs (OpenMarketFeeScheduleArtifact, bond requirements), chio-open-market/src/bidding.rs (bid->SignedAskResponse minting CapabilityToken), chio-open-market/src/penalty.rs (slashing)
ideas.orca_surface: A new marketplace tab fed into Orca's native browsing/account-switcher UI; `orca commerce list`/`orca commerce buy <tool>` and a 'wallet' chip per worktree showing the scoped token purchased.
ideas.user_value: Agents discover priced tools they can trust because sellers are bonded and bad behavior is slashed and re-priced from receipts.
ideas.moat: Bonds + receipt-derived reputation slashing (chio-reputation/chio-pheromone) make this an accountable marketplace; the fee schedule is a signed artifact, so fees are non-repudiable.
ideas.risk: Marketplace liquidity is a cold-start problem; without enough listings the participation fee has nothing to attach to.

ideas.title: Compliance-grade audit export as the enterprise license SKU
ideas.one_liner: Charge a flat enterprise license for the only feature regulated buyers actually pay for: exportable, replayable, signed proof of everything agents bought and did.
ideas.description: chio-enterprise-export (EnterpriseExportBundle, verify_enterprise_export) plus chio-transaction-passport's evidence graph and the SIEM/lineage exporters already assemble a tamper-evident bundle binding the AP2/ACP mandate hashes (chio-commerce-order/mandate.rs), settlement proof (chio-web3/settlement_proof.rs), guard evidence, signed tool manifest (chio-manifest), and unrevoked-capability proof. We gate this entire export+verify path behind an enterprise tier and price it per-seat or per-org annually, anchored to the existing EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF / ISO 42001 / PCI-DSS v4 mappings. This is the highest-margin, lowest-COGS line: the artifacts are produced anyway by the kernel, so the SKU is packaging + the verifier + support. Unit economics: enterprise ARR with ~95% gross margin; the export is the deliverable a CISO signs off on, decoupling price from transaction volume (so it survives even if take-rates compress).
ideas.chio_capability: chio-enterprise-export/src/lib.rs (EnterpriseExportBundle, verify_enterprise_export), chio-transaction-passport (evidence_graph), chio-siem + chio-lineage exporters, chio-commerce-order/src/mandate.rs (mandate binding)
ideas.orca_surface: An 'Attested Receipts' / 'Audit' tab beside Orca's AI-diff review; `orca commerce export --siem` emits the EnterpriseExportBundle, and the phone companion can approve/forward it.
ideas.user_value: A regulator-ready, replayable record of every autonomous purchase and decision - the thing that lets a buyer move agents from PoC to production.
ideas.moat: No MIT agent runner has a tamper-evident, cross-protocol audit story; the compliance mappings already exist, so this is a wedge competitors cannot quickly copy.
ideas.risk: Enterprise sales cycles are long; value depends on the legal/regulatory weight of code-based audit trails, which the market admits is still untested in court.

ideas.title: Autonomy tiers as the upsell ladder (Shadow -> Advisory -> Active) with bonded unlock
ideas.one_liner: Sell higher agent autonomy as paid tiers, where unattended spend (Active mode) requires a posted bond and a premium subscription.
ideas.description: chio-autonomy/src/model.rs gates pricing/capital decisions behind AutonomousAutomationMode (Shadow/Advisory/Active) and review states (AutoApproved/HumanReviewRequired/ShadowOnly/Blocked); chio-credit's CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy adds a kill switch, max-autonomy-tier, and require-locked-reserve. We turn that into product packaging: a free/cheap Shadow tier where Chio only simulates and advises, a mid Advisory tier, and a premium Active tier that lets agents transact unattended only if the org posts a bond and runs a higher RuntimeAssuranceTier. Premium pricing for the unlock is computed by chio-underwriting price_premium/risk_multiplier (premium.rs) from the agent's reputation and assurance tier, so riskier agents pay more to go autonomous. Unit economics: this is classic feature-gated SaaS expansion - the same fleet pays more as it trusts agents with more money, and the bond requirement de-risks Chio's exposure while the premium is pure margin.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-autonomy/src/model.rs (AutonomousAutomationMode, review states), chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (kill switch, bonded tiers), chio-underwriting/src/premium.rs (price_premium/risk_multiplier)
ideas.orca_surface: A per-agent 'autonomy dial' in the worktree/agent view; the phone companion's pairing+approval flow (mobile/app/pair*.tsx) is the human circuit-breaker that authorizes a tier bump, and `orca commerce autonomy set <tier>` enforces it.
ideas.user_value: Buy exactly as much agent independence as you are comfortable with, with a hard kill switch and a bond backstopping the riskiest tier.
ideas.moat: The tiers are enforced in the kernel (fail-closed), not in the prompt; the premium is priced off signed reputation, which competitors with no receipt log cannot compute.
ideas.risk: Tier boundaries must map to genuinely different risk or buyers see them as artificial paywalls; pricing the premium wrong over- or under-charges for autonomy.

ideas.bold_bet: Make settlement take-rate the company's core revenue engine: every agent-to-agent transaction Chio attests pays Chio 30-50 bps as an explicit, receipt-bound facilitator fee (chio-settle facilitator/paymaster deduction -> chio-web3 settlement receipt -> chio-credit IouEnvelope), while Chio never takes custody. The flat cockpit subscription and enterprise audit license exist mainly to seed adoption; the real, compounding, near-100%-margin business is being the neutral, attested clearing layer that skims a transparent toll on the entire ACP/AP2/x402 agent economy. Whoever owns the attested settlement receipt owns the take-rate, and Chio is the only stack that binds the fee into a tamper-evident, replayable artifact.

ideas.lens: Go-to-market, ICP & wedge: who buys first, the smallest valuable thing we sell, and the positioning line

ideas.title: Wedge: the spend kill-switch for parallel agent fleets (the anti-$47k-runaway)
ideas.one_liner: Ship Chio-on-Orca first as the only agent cockpit where a runaway agent physically cannot overspend, because the limit lives in the kernel, not the prompt.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-metering BudgetEnforcer/BudgetPolicy (flat per-session/agent/tool caps with saturating arithmetic) + chio-metering BudgetTree (org->dept->team->agent) + chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier, deny_if_outstanding_delinquency)
ideas.orca_surface: A hard per-worktree spend mandate set in the existing rate-limits/usage panel (src/main/rate-limits, mobile AccountUsage.tsx) and a `commerce:*` IPC handler that the agent-hooks bus (src/main/agent-hooks) calls before each tool call; overspend fails closed and pauses the worktree.
ideas.user_value: The most-cited fear in agentic ops (dashboards but no control, the $47k LangChain runaway) is eliminated on day one. A team running 10 parallel Claude Code worktrees gets a literal ceiling per worktree and an org-wide cap, enforced outside agent code.
ideas.moat: Enforcement is in the TCB and fail-closed by design (CLAUDE.md house rule), with saturating arithmetic and a kill switch. Competing agent runners only read provider quota (Orca's rate-limits read Claude/Codex tokens); none can refuse the next paid call. This is the white space the market admits no standard owns.
ideas.risk: Requires the agent-hooks contract to become a blocking allow/deny call (a wire-protocol bump, ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION), which upstream reserves for real changes. Mitigate by shipping budgets as a soft read-only HUD first, then flipping the gate on for opted-in worktrees.

ideas.title: First customer = AI-native dev shops and agencies running fleets on client money
ideas.one_liner: Sell to the 5-50 person agency or AI startup that already runs many CLI agents in parallel and bills compute/API spend back to clients, because they feel both the overspend risk and the prove-what-we-spent pain.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit/hook.rs CreditEvaluatorHook minting a signed IouEnvelope (chio.credit.iou-envelope.v1) per finalized receipt binding amount_units/currency to receipt_id + content/policy hashes; chio-metering CostMetadata/CostDimension as the per-run cost record
ideas.orca_surface: An 'Attested Receipts' tab beside Orca's annotate-AI-diffs review and the mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx screen, rendering each agent run's signed cost line; `orca commerce ledger export` CLI verb wrapping the existing `chio` binary over its `--budget-db` SQLite store.
ideas.user_value: An agency can hand a client a cryptographically signed, per-run spend ledger (agent X cost $4.12 on this PR, here is the receipt) instead of a screenshot of a usage dashboard. That is a billable trust artifact, not just an internal log.
ideas.moat: Every run already terminates in a signed IOU + receipt chain; reproducing this needs a kernel and an append-only Merkle log a TS agent runner does not have. The ICP is narrow enough to dominate by word of mouth and broad enough to expand into.
ideas.risk: IouEnvelope and CostMetadata are typed containers the kernel must populate; deriving true per-run cost (tokens, GPU-seconds, vendor invoice) for an arbitrary CLI agent needs a collector. Start with the provider token usage Orca already fetches (src/main/claude-usage, codex-usage) as the cost source.

ideas.title: Smallest valuable unit to sell: the per-prompt budget pool for fan-out
ideas.one_liner: The first paid feature is a single field when you fan one prompt across N agents: set one pool, every worktree draws a capped, currency-coherent slice, over-allocation rejected before any agent runs.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-workflow-preflight WorkflowBudgetPool + WorkflowPreflightPlan (parent_task -> child_tasks, budget_minor per child) with the workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded validation that parent and every child stay within the pool and currency is coherent
ideas.orca_surface: Wired into Orca's fan-one-prompt-across-N-agents orchestration flow (src/cli/handlers/orchestration, the parallel-worktrees UI); a 'budget pool' field in the run-N-agents dialog and a per-worktree remaining-slice chip in the sidebar.
ideas.user_value: Today fanning across N agents multiplies spend with no shared ceiling. This makes 'try 5 approaches, spend at most $20 total, merge the winner' a one-line guarantee, validated client-side before a single token is burned.
ideas.moat: This maps one-to-one onto Orca's signature UX (its actual differentiator) and onto a Chio primitive that already exists and is tested. It is the cleanest fusion point and is hard to copy without the preflight plan + pool math.
ideas.risk: Budget state is in-memory/caller-supplied today; concurrent worktrees drafting against one pool atomically needs a durable shared ledger (the SQLite snapshot store is out of scope of chio-metering). Mitigate by serializing draws through the single commerce sidecar process.

ideas.title: Land-and-expand: bonded autonomy dial as the upsell from free budgets to paid trust
ideas.one_liner: Free tier gives budgets and signed receipts; the paid tier unlocks higher autonomy tiers that let an agent transact unattended, but only once a bond is posted and a runtime-assurance tier is met.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (require_locked_reserve, maximum_autonomy_tier, kill_switch) + GovernedAutonomyTier, gated against chio-attest-verify runtime attestation and chio-credentials TrustTier (Unverified/Attested/Verified/Premier)
ideas.orca_surface: A per-agent 'autonomy dial' control in the worktree/agent settings; raising the dial above attended requires posting a bond and surfaces a TrustTier badge, gated through a `commerce:setAutonomy` IPC handler and confirmed via the mobile pairing QR flow (mobile/app/pair*.tsx).
ideas.user_value: Buyers can graduate an agent from human-in-the-loop to unattended spend deliberately, with a posted reserve as skin in the game and a hardware/TEE assurance floor. It turns 'should I trust this agent with money' into a dial with cryptographic preconditions.
ideas.moat: Bond-gated, attestation-gated autonomy tiers are a defensible pricing surface no MIT agent runner has. It also creates a natural revenue ladder (free budgets -> paid unattended autonomy -> enterprise compliance export).
ideas.risk: Posting a real bond implies custody, the money-transmitter bright line. Keep it custody-neutral: the bond is a signed locked-reserve attestation or crypto escrow via chio-settle (feature=web3), never Chio holding user fiat.

ideas.title: Positioning line and beachhead demo: the audit-and-enforcement plane for agent spend
ideas.one_liner: Position as the neutral audit-and-enforcement plane across ACP/AP2/x402 (it is the kernel, not another wallet), and prove it with a one-command on-chain buy-pay-settle-receipt demo that needs no fiat rail.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-commerce-order verify path producing a CommerceOrderPassportReport (state machine intent->...->completed + AP2 checkout/payment mandate hashes + ACP delegated-payment-token hash + payment lifecycle); chio-settle (feature=web3) USDC escrow lock/release + EIP-3009/x402 for the live loop
ideas.orca_surface: The passport report renders inline in the annotate-AI-diffs review pane so a human approves a cryptographically attested transaction, not a log line; the demo is an `orca commerce buy <x402-endpoint>` verb (new src/cli/specs + src/cli/handlers) wrapping the `chio` binary end to end.
ideas.user_value: A prospect sees an agent discover, pay (USDC over x402), settle on-chain, and produce a signed, replayable mandate->payment->receipt passport in one command, with the human approval bound to a verifiable artifact. That is the whole pitch in 30 seconds.
ideas.moat: Chio is the only stack that already binds AP2 mandate hashes and the ACP delegated-payment-token hash into one signed ledger (chio-commerce-order/mandate.rs), making it the neutral verifier across all three standards rather than a competing wallet. The compliance mappings (EU AI Act, PCI-DSS v4, ISO 42001) are the enterprise close.
ideas.risk: chio-commerce-order verifies an already-assembled bundle; nothing in-repo orchestrates a live order forward or calls a real PSP. The crypto rail works end to end, so lead with the x402/USDC demo and treat fiat/PSP order assembly as a later, partner-backed phase.

ideas.bold_bet: Lead with a single visceral wedge for AI-native dev agencies running parallel CLI-agent fleets on client money: 'the runaway-agent kill switch you can audit.' The smallest sellable unit is the per-prompt budget pool on Orca's fan-out (chio-workflow-preflight WorkflowBudgetPool, rejecting over-allocation before any agent runs) plus a hard per-worktree spend mandate enforced in the kernel (chio-metering BudgetEnforcer + chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy kill switch). Position against the cited $47k LangChain runaway: every other cockpit shows you spend, Chio-on-Orca refuses it, and hands you a signed per-run receipt (chio-credit IouEnvelope) for the client. Free budgets plus receipts as the beachhead, paid bonded-autonomy tiers and compliance-grade attested audit export as the expansion. Win the agencies first because they feel both pains at once (overspend risk and prove-what-we-billed), then climb into regulated enterprises on the receipt and audit story.

ideas.title: Rail-Neutral Receipt: the one verifier across ACP, AP2, and x402
ideas.one_liner: A single signed passport that ingests an ACP token, an AP2 mandate chain, and an x402 settlement proof and replays them as one verified mandate-to-payment-to-receipt chain in the Orca review pane.
ideas.description: Stripe Agent Toolkit, Coinbase x402, and Google AP2 each define exactly one layer of the stack (checkout, micropayment, mandate) and structurally cannot attest the others without becoming a competitor to them. Chio already projects all three into one evidence graph: chio-transaction-passport (verifier_policy.rs with required_claims / omitted_claims) plus chio-agent-web-interop artifacts x402.rs, ap2.rs, acp_commerce.rs each validate SHA-256-pinned digests (resource, payment_requirements, payment_proof, settlement) and bind them to one transaction_passport_ref. Surface this as a per-worktree Commerce tab where every agent purchase renders as a verified cross-rail chain a human can replay offline. Because Chio is the neutral verifier and not a wallet, it is the only party that can sit above Visa, Stripe, and Coinbase at once.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-transaction-passport (verifier_policy.rs, evidence_graph.rs), chio-agent-web-interop artifacts/{x402,ap2,acp_commerce}.rs, chio-commerce-order/mandate.rs
ideas.orca_surface: New commerce:* IPC namespace (src/main/ipc/commerce.ts) feeding a per-worktree 'Commerce' tab beside the annotate-AI-diffs review surface; mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx mirror
ideas.user_value: A developer or auditor sees one replayable receipt chain regardless of whether the agent paid via Stripe checkout, an x402 USDC call, or an AP2 card mandate, instead of three disconnected vendor dashboards.
ideas.moat: Single-rail vendors cannot verify rivals' artifacts without conceding neutrality; Chio's value grows with each rail it does NOT own, which is the opposite of every incumbent's incentive.
ideas.risk: Each rail evolves its wire format (x402 source_version pinning already shows this); the projection manifests need version-tolerant upkeep as ACP/AP2/x402 churn.

ideas.title: Bonded Seller Market: slashable tool listings vs x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray
ideas.one_liner: An agent-to-agent tool marketplace where sellers post a bond, bad service is penalized with signed evidence, and reputation is re-priced from receipts, exposed as a ranked provider picker in Orca's account-switcher.
ideas.description: x402 Bazaar and Skyfire give discovery plus pay-per-call but have zero seller accountability: a bad endpoint keeps its money and its listing. Chio-open-market already has the missing economics: penalty.rs defines OpenMarketAbuseClass (FraudulentListing, UnverifiableListingBehavior) and OpenMarketPenaltyAction::SlashBond/HoldBond with a Proposed->Enforced->Reversed lifecycle, fee_schedule.rs ties bond classes to chio-credit CreditBond collateral, and bidding.rs mints a scoped cost-capped CapabilityToken only against a signature-verified funds reservation. Feed chio-reputation tiers and chio-pheromone concentration into Orca's native marketplace/account-switcher UI so the cockpit ranks providers by signed reputation, revocation rate, posted bond, and price, then auto-bids; a slashing event visibly drops a seller's rank. This is a market with real downside for sellers, which no pay-per-call rail offers.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-open-market (penalty.rs SlashBond, fee_schedule.rs bonds, bidding.rs), chio-credit CreditBond, chio-reputation tiers
ideas.orca_surface: Provider-picker / marketplace panel reusing the account-switcher UI; `orca commerce buy <tool>` CLI verb (src/cli/specs + handlers) that auto-bids
ideas.user_value: When an agent needs a paid tool the cockpit picks a bonded, well-reputed provider and the buyer has recourse (slash the bond) if service is bad, instead of losing USDC to an anonymous endpoint.
ideas.moat: Requires the full credit/bond/reputation stack (CreditBond + slashing lifecycle + receipt-derived reputation) that payment rails deliberately do not build; replicating it means becoming a clearinghouse, not a wallet.
ideas.risk: Cold-start liquidity: a bonded market needs enough sellers willing to post collateral before buyers get value; needs seeding (Chio-operated first-party listings).

ideas.title: Swarm Trust Pheromones: emergent cross-operator counterparty trust
ideas.one_liner: A live, decentralized 'is this tool server currently trusted by the swarm' signal gossiped across Chio operators, shown as a heat indicator on each agent/tool in the Orca fleet view.
ideas.description: Every incumbent trust signal is centralized and vendor-issued: Skyfire KYA, Visa/Mastercard agent tokens, AP2 mandates all flow from one authority. Chio-pheromone is a signed, Merkle-committed stigmergic substrate (PheromoneDeposit, observation-cost commitments, scarcity policy, newcomer discount horizon, RUNTIME_TRUST_FLOOR_STATE) and chio-federation/pheromone_gossip.rs ships it operator-to-operator under treaty scope with transit-chain verification, with no central issuer. This is a behavioral-consensus trust channel that no single-vendor rail can structurally produce because they have no peer operators to gossip between. Render pheromone concentration as a real-time trust-floor heat dot on each tool server in Orca's fleet/quick-open view, complementing static credentials with a 'the swarm currently distrusts this endpoint' signal that updates faster than any revocation list.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-pheromone (substrate.rs, RUNTIME_TRUST_FLOOR_STATE_SCHEMA), chio-federation/pheromone_gossip.rs (transit-chain + treaty scope)
ideas.orca_surface: Heat indicator on tool servers / agents in the fleet view and quick-open across worktrees; fed via commerce:* IPC from the sidecar
ideas.user_value: An agent about to call a tool sees a live swarm-consensus distrust signal (e.g. an endpoint that just started misbehaving across other operators) before any formal revocation lands.
ideas.moat: Decentralized emergent trust requires a federation of operators gossiping signed deposits; a single-vendor closed rail has no swarm and cannot fake one, making this genuinely uncopyable by Stripe/Visa/Coinbase.
ideas.risk: Needs a federation of operators to be meaningful (network effect); gossip-spam and collusion resistance must hold up, though scarcity policy and observation-cost commitments are designed for exactly that.

ideas.title: The Kill Switch incumbents admit they lack: kernel-enforced spend, not dashboard alerts
ideas.one_liner: A per-worktree autonomy dial backed by the kernel's capital kill-switch and maximum-autonomy-tier so a Chio-Orca agent structurally cannot make the next paid tool call once its mandate is exhausted.
ideas.description: The market's loudest admitted gap (the $47k runaway LangChain agent) is that AP2, ACP, and x402 authorize spend but do not enforce it at call time; their controls are observability. Chio puts enforcement out-of-agent in the kernel: capital_and_execution.rs carries kill_switch and maximum_autonomy_tier (GovernedAutonomyTier) on the CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy, defaulting external_execution_authoritative=false and automatic_capital_execution_supported=false, and chio-metering BudgetEnforcer/BudgetTree fail-close on overspend. The decisive move is making Orca's fire-and-forget agent-hooks bus a blocking allow/deny gate (bump ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION) so every agent tool call asks the kernel for a decision before proceeding. Expose it as a per-agent autonomy dial in the renderer: higher tiers require a posted bond and a higher RuntimeAssuranceTier. Sold directly against the runaway-agent story: enforcement lives in the TCB, not the prompt.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit/capital_and_execution.rs (kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier, GovernedAutonomyTier), chio-metering BudgetEnforcer/BudgetTree, chio-kernel
ideas.orca_surface: Per-agent autonomy dial in the renderer (reusing rate-limits/usage UI); the agent-hooks subsystem (src/main/agent-hooks/) turned into a blocking capability gate
ideas.user_value: An operator sets a hard mandate and the agent literally cannot exceed it because the kernel denies the call, replacing after-the-fact alerts with a real circuit-breaker.
ideas.moat: Incumbents are SDKs and rails that run inside or beside agent code; an out-of-agent kernel mediating every tool call with signed denials is an architecture they would have to rebuild from scratch, and it is exactly Chio's existing TCB.
ideas.risk: Turning the hook bus blocking is a wire-protocol change and adds latency to every tool call; must stay merged with upstream Orca's fast-shipping hook contract.

ideas.title: Know-Your-Buyer attestation: prove the agent is a mandate-backed, sandboxed payer
ideas.one_liner: A buyer-side attestation packet an agent presents to a merchant or peer agent to prove it is a genuine, mandate-backed, sandboxed paying customer, without locking into any one network's token.
ideas.description: Skyfire KYA, Visa Trusted Agent, and Mastercard Agentic Tokens all attest the SELLER side or issue a vendor-bound credential; nobody lets the BUYER prove its own runtime integrity in a rail-neutral way. Chio-attest-buyer already produces a fail-closed BuyerAttestationPacket and ReceiptLineageBundle (api.rs verify_buyer_attestation_packet, runtime_manifest.rs) binding buyer_id, capability_id, treaty scope, BilateralInvocation, workflow receipt, budget_refs, and settlement_claimed, replayable offline, and chio-transaction-passport/runtime_security carries the sandbox/TEE evidence. An agent in an Orca worktree presents this packet to an external x402/ACP endpoint as a Chio-attested 'I am a real bonded buyer under an unrevoked mandate' proof. This is the open, multi-rail answer to KYA that no single vendor can give because their attestation is bound to their own credential.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-attest-buyer (api.rs, runtime_manifest.rs, types.rs BuyerAttestationPacket + ReceiptLineageBundle), chio-transaction-passport/runtime_security
ideas.orca_surface: `orca commerce attest` CLI verb emitting the buyer packet; a 'present buyer credential' action on the per-worktree Commerce tab
ideas.user_value: A merchant or counterparty agent can verify, offline and rail-agnostically, that the buying agent is sandboxed and operating under a live mandate before granting access or a discount.
ideas.moat: Vendor KYA credentials are issuer-bound and seller-centric by design; a portable buyer-side proof package that replays sandbox + mandate + budget lineage is orthogonal to all of them and only Chio's receipt-lineage model produces it.
ideas.risk: Adoption depends on merchants choosing to consume a Chio packet; until counterparties verify it, value is one-sided (mitigated by also exporting it for the operator's own audit).

ideas.bold_bet: Make the forked Orca the neutral attestation-and-enforcement plane that sits ABOVE every payment rail rather than competing with any. Concretely: fuse the rail-neutral Rail-Neutral Receipt (chio-transaction-passport projecting ACP + AP2 + x402 into one signed chain) with the kernel kill-switch (capital_and_execution kill_switch / maximum_autonomy_tier enforced at the agent-hooks gate). This is the one thing Stripe, Coinbase, Skyfire, Google, and Visa/Mastercard structurally cannot build, because each is a single rail or SDK that runs inside agent code, whereas Chio is an out-of-agent kernel plus a cross-rail verifier whose value increases with every rail it does NOT own. The cockpit becomes the place where any agent transaction on any rail is provably bounded, mandate-gated, and exportable for EU AI Act / PCI-DSS audit, which is the white space the entire market openly admits is unfilled.

ideas.title: Bazaar: the in-cockpit tool registry where listings are signed and ranking is reproducible
ideas.one_liner: A built-in marketplace tab in Orca where any operator publishes a signed tool/data/compute listing and every agent searches the same freshness-ranked, verifiable catalog.
ideas.description: Fork Orca's quick-open / native-browsing surface into a 'Bazaar' tab backed by chio-listing: operators publish a SignedGenericListing under an owned namespace (Origin/Mirror/Indexer roles) plus a signed ListingPricingHint carrying price-per-call, SLA, revocation rate, and recent receipt volume. Search uses the GENERIC_LISTING_SEARCH_ALGORITHM_V1 reproducible ordering so the ranking an agent sees is itself verifiable and replayable, not an opaque ad auction. Listings are visibility-only by default (GenericListingBoundary) and require explicit trust activation before an agent can transact, so discovery and trust are cleanly separated. This is the demand-side front door of the flywheel: the more operators list, the more an agent can buy without leaving the cockpit.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-listing (listing.rs SignedGenericListing + GenericRegistryPublisher Origin/Mirror/Indexer, discovery.rs ListingPricingHint, search.rs reproducible freshness ranking)
