ideas.orca_surface: New 'Bazaar' tab reusing the quick-open / native GitHub-Linear browsing pane; backed by a commerce:listingSearch IPC handler and an `orca commerce search <scope>` CLI verb
ideas.user_value: Agents discover and price real tool/data/compute supply from inside the cockpit with a ranking they can audit, instead of hand-wiring MCP servers; operators get a distribution channel.
ideas.moat: Reproducible, signed ranking over a content-addressed registry is something a plain MIT agent runner cannot offer; the catalog is verifiable rather than a trust-me list, and it is the same registry the kernel later enforces against.
ideas.risk: Cold-start: an empty catalog has no pull. Must seed with first-party Chio-wrapped tools and a handful of design-partner operators before opening publication.

ideas.title: List-in-place: wrap any worktree tool into a sellable, metered listing with one command
ideas.one_liner: An `orca commerce list` flow that turns a tool an operator already runs into a published, priced, receipt-minting Chio tool server, lowering supply-side activation energy to near zero.
ideas.description: The supply side of the flywheel dies if onboarding a seller is hard. chio-api-protect is already a zero-code reverse proxy that reads an OpenAPI spec, generates a default policy, and mints a signed HttpReceipt per request (side-effect routes gated by a capability token). Wrap it as the Orca seller onboarding path: an operator points `orca commerce list` at an OpenAPI URL or an MCP server (via chio-mcp-adapter / chio-openapi-mcp-bridge), Chio stands up the protected proxy, generates a ListingPricingHint, and publishes a SignedGenericListing under their namespace. From that moment every call is priced, metered, and attested, and the listing is live in the Bazaar. The seller never writes payment or receipt code.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-api-protect (zero-code receipt-minting proxy) + chio-mcp-adapter / chio-openapi-mcp-bridge (wrap MCP/OpenAPI as a Chio tool server) + chio-listing publication
ideas.orca_surface: `orca commerce list <openapi-url|mcp-server>` CLI verb plus a 'Sell a tool' button in the Bazaar tab; new src/cli/handlers/commerce.ts and src/main/ipc/commerce.ts
ideas.user_value: Any developer in the community turns an existing API or MCP server into a paid, audited Chio listing in minutes, with no payment integration work.
ideas.moat: The receipt-minting proxy plus signed manifest means every seller's output is attested by construction; competitors would have to rebuild the kernel, capability tokens, and receipt log to match.
ideas.risk: Sellers may not want a proxy in their hot path for latency reasons; need a thin/advisory mode (chio-api-protect already has an advisory evaluate route) so onboarding does not force a blocking gate on day one.

ideas.title: Earned-not-bought reputation: provider ranking driven by receipt-derived tiers, with slashable bonds
ideas.one_liner: Sellers post a slashable bond to list, and their Bazaar rank is a Sybil-resistant ReputationTier computed from signed receipts, so supply quality compounds instead of being gamed.
ideas.description: Network effects only hold if added supply is good supply. chio-reputation derives a LocalReputationScorecard from signed receipts through composable feeds (arena_survival, cross_provider_equality) and maps it to a ReputationTier with per-feed floors so a flood of one feed cannot reach the top tier. chio-open-market adds a signed fee schedule with OpenMarketBondRequirement (slashable Publication/Listing/Dispute bonds) and a full penalty lifecycle (HoldBond/SlashBond/ReverseSlash) keyed to abuse classes (SpamPublication, FraudulentListing, ReplayPublication). Fuse them: to list in the Bazaar a seller posts a bond; their rank is receipt-earned reputation; bad service produces signed evidence that slashes the bond and re-prices reputation. This is structurally better than x402 Bazaar's pay-and-pray discovery.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-reputation (tier.rs ReputationTier with per-feed floors, feed.rs composable feeds) + chio-open-market (fee_schedule.rs slashable OpenMarketBondRequirement, penalty.rs slash lifecycle)
ideas.orca_surface: Reputation/bond badges on every Bazaar listing card and on the counterparty trust card in the worktree/agent view; `orca commerce reputation <provider>` to pull a fresh tier
ideas.user_value: Buyers (and buying agents) can trust the ranking because top rank requires both earned receipt history and capital at risk; good sellers rise and capture more demand.
ideas.moat: Reputation that is cryptographically tied to receipts plus economically tied to slashable bonds is extremely hard to fake or fork; it is the accountability layer the whole agent-commerce market openly admits is missing.
ideas.risk: Reputation corpus is local/caller-assembled today; needs a shared or exchangeable snapshot path so a buyer can pull a counterparty's score at deal time without running the whole corpus themselves.

ideas.title: Revenue-share that settles itself: x402/USDC payouts split across the listing supply chain
ideas.one_liner: When an agent buys a listed tool, chio-settle splits the payment across seller, indexer/mirror, and the platform per the signed fee schedule, with on-chain proof, so referrers and registry mirrors get paid automatically.
ideas.description: A developer flywheel needs a credible take-rate-and-payout story for everyone who adds value, not just the end seller. The fee schedule (OpenMarketFeeScheduleArtifact) already declares publication_fee, market_participation_fee, and dispute_fee under a governing operator; the registry already distinguishes Origin/Mirror/Indexer publishers. Wire chio-settle (feature=web3: EVM escrow, EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization, x402, Circle nanopayments) so each purchase settles a multi-party split: the seller is paid, the indexer that surfaced the listing earns a participation cut, and the platform takes its fee, every leg producing a Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact bound to the governed receipt id. This turns mirrors/indexers and referrers into economically motivated growth agents rather than passive caches.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-open-market/fee_schedule.rs (participation/publication fees, governing operator) + chio-settle (x402 / EIP-3009 / Circle on-chain split) + chio-web3/settlement.rs (Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact bound to receipt id)
ideas.orca_surface: An 'Earnings' panel reusing Orca's account/usage UI showing per-listing revenue and pending payouts; the settlement watchdog (chio-settle automation.rs) wired into Orca's notify-when-done machinery for payout/escrow events
ideas.user_value: Sellers, indexers, and referrers see attested earnings and get paid on-chain without invoicing; the platform earns a transparent, auditable take rate.
ideas.moat: Multi-party signed settlement with per-leg receipts anchored to a governed receipt id is a defensible, regulator-friendly payout primitive; stays non-custodial by settling over regulated stablecoin rails rather than holding funds.
ideas.risk: Crypto-rail-first; a fiat payout closes the loop only via a licensed custody partner. Lead with USDC/x402 for the agent-to-agent leg and treat fiat as a partner integration.

ideas.title: Federated registries: independent operators publish into one trust mesh under stake-gated admission
ideas.one_liner: Any team can run its own Chio operator and have its listings appear in everyone's Bazaar via federation treaties and stake-gated open admission, instead of one centralized app store.
ideas.description: The strongest network effect is multi-sided supply you do not own. chio-federation ships a FederatedOpenAdmissionPolicyArtifact (stake_requirements with required bond class, slashable, governance-case-required) and treaty/ladder-intersection machinery plus pheromone_gossip and revocation_gossip. Use it so a new operator joins the mesh by satisfying a published admission policy (post stake, accept the governing charter and fee schedule), after which their signed listings federate into other operators' Bazaars as Mirror/Indexer entries while trust activation stays local and explicit. Revocations and pheromone trust signals gossip across the mesh so a bad actor is contained network-wide. This makes Chio-on-Orca a federation of marketplaces, not a single gatekept store, which is far harder for a competitor to displace.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-federation (open_admission.rs FederatedOpenAdmissionPolicy with stake requirements, treaty.rs, pheromone_gossip.rs, revocation_gossip.rs)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Federation' settings surface to join/operate a registry and a federated-origin badge on Bazaar listings; mobile companion notification when admission/revocation events affect a followed operator
ideas.user_value: Enterprises and communities run their own attested registries that still interoperate, getting both control and reach; buyers get a wider catalog with network-wide bad-actor containment.
ideas.moat: A stake-gated, gossip-revoked federation of signed registries is a genuine multi-operator moat; the value lives in the mesh and its trust gossip, not in any one app instance.
ideas.risk: Governance and economic-design complexity; admission policy and charter disputes need clear adjudication. Start with a single first-party registry and invite 2-3 design-partner operators before opening admission.

ideas.title: Public Proof Room: a shareable, verifiable receipts page that recruits the next seller
ideas.one_liner: Every seller and high-volume agent gets a hosted chio-proof-room page proving its real receipt history, which doubles as community/Discord-shareable social proof and the cold-start growth loop.
ideas.description: chio-proof-room is already a servable verifier bundle (chio.proof-room.bundle.v1, verifier-report, release-truth) that serves attested fixtures and verifier reports over HTTP. Turn it into a per-seller 'Proof Room': a public, link-shareable page that replays a seller's signed receipts, reputation tier, bond status, and settlement proofs so anyone (a buyer, an auditor, a Discord lurker) can independently verify the seller is real and good without an account. Sellers post their Proof Room link in the Orca Discord and on social; each link is an ad that is also a cryptographic proof, pulling in buyers and recruiting the next seller. This is the cold-start engine: verifiable bragging rights that competitors cannot fake because the receipts are kernel-signed.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-proof-room (servable verifier bundle + verifier-report) drawing on chio-reputation tiers, chio-open-market bond state, and chio-web3 settlement_proof
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Publish Proof Room' action in the Earnings/Bazaar seller view; an `orca commerce proof-room serve` CLI verb; shareable into the existing Orca Discord community
ideas.user_value: Sellers convert their attested track record into trustless marketing; buyers verify a counterparty in one click before transacting; the community surfaces who is actually delivering.
ideas.moat: A self-serve, link-shareable, cryptographically verifiable reputation page is a unique growth surface; the proofs are kernel-signed receipts no competitor can mint or replay falsely.
ideas.risk: Receipt content may leak sensitive metadata; must use selective disclosure (chio-selective-disclosure / log redaction) so a public Proof Room reveals proof-of-quality without exposing buyer or payload data.

ideas.bold_bet: Make Chio-on-Orca a FEDERATION of attested tool registries, not a single app store. Combine the chio-listing signed registry (Origin/Mirror/Indexer roles, reproducible-ranked search), chio-open-market slashable bonds and fee schedules, chio-reputation receipt-derived tiers, and chio-federation stake-gated open admission so independent operators run their own Bazaars that interoperate into one trust mesh, with revocation and pheromone trust gossiped network-wide. The cold-start engine is the per-seller public Proof Room (chio-proof-room): a link-shareable, cryptographically verifiable receipt-and-reputation page that sellers post in the Orca Discord, turning every attested track record into both an ad and a proof. Supply (sellers wrapping APIs via chio-api-protect in one command) and demand (agents searching a verifiable catalog from the cockpit) reinforce because every transaction settles over x402/USDC (chio-settle) with a multi-party revenue split that pays sellers, indexers, and referrers automatically. The defensible asset is not the forked Electron app, which is MIT and copyable, but the multi-operator mesh of signed registries plus the kernel-attested reputation that competitors cannot fork because they cannot mint Chio's receipts.

ideas.lens: Fork & rebrand mechanics + Rust/TS bridge: the concrete plan to fork Orca, rename to Chio, manage upstream merge burden, and wire the Electron/TS app (and Swift/Kotlin mobile) to the Rust protocol via the C ABI (chio-bindings-ffi / chio-cpp-kernel-ffi), the chio-api-protect axum sidecar, the chio CLI, the UniFFI mobile bindings, and the existing React/Vite receipt dashboard.

ideas.title: Ship chio-api-protect as the bundled commerce sidecar behind a commerce:* IPC namespace (reuse, do not rebuild)
ideas.one_liner: Orca already proves the sidecar pattern (token-authed Unix socket terminal daemon); chio-api-protect is a finished axum control plane, so the bridge is config plus one IPC file, not a new server.
ideas.description: The grounding digest's 'no long-running kernel server' gap is false. chio-api-protect is a #![forbid(unsafe_code)] axum reverse proxy whose embedded sidecar already exposes /chio/evaluate, /chio/verify, /chio/health, /v1/capabilities/mint and /release, /v1/receipts and /verify, and a full /approvals/* human-in-the-loop flow, with each route's authorization semantics documented in lib.rs. Bundle it as the Chio commerce backend rather than writing a daemon. Electron main spawns it on a localhost port with a chmod-restricted Bearer token file, exactly mirroring src/main/daemon/daemon-server.ts.
ideas.chio_capability: crates/products/chio-api-protect (ProtectProxy/ProtectConfig public API; routes in proxy/router.rs; listen_addr accept loop in proxy/state.rs; documented production-vs-advisory boundary where /v1/evaluate/advisory sets chio-trust-level: advisory and authorization:false)
ideas.orca_surface: New src/main/ipc/commerce.ts registered via a one-line registerCommerceHandlers() addition in src/main/ipc/register-core-handlers.ts (mirrors existing agent-trust.ts / ai-vault.ts security channels). Renderer calls commerce:mintCapability / commerce:submitReceipt / commerce:listPendingApprovals.
ideas.user_value: A working autonomous-commerce backend on day one of the fork: every paid or metered tool call routes through a fail-closed Rust control plane that mints scoped capability tokens and emits signed receipts, with no bespoke server to write or audit.
ideas.moat: chio-api-protect pre-draws the line competitors get wrong: which routes are real allow/deny gates (/chio/evaluate, /v1/capabilities/*) versus observability-only. A plain agent-runner fork has no equivalent and would mis-wire advisory telemetry as enforcement.
ideas.risk: chio-api-protect is OpenAPI-spec-driven (it proxies an upstream API). Using it purely as a Chio control plane without a real upstream needs a degenerate proxy mode or a trimmed spec-discovery path; must confirm /chio/* and /v1/capabilities/* operate standalone.

ideas.title: Load chio-bindings-ffi as a koffi addon in Electron main for hot-path, in-process verification
ideas.one_liner: For per-tool-call checks (verify a capability, canonicalize-and-hash a receipt, verify a manifest) skip the socket and call the cbindgen C ABI directly from the trusted Electron main process.
ideas.description: chio-bindings-ffi compiles to a staticlib/cdylib with a cbindgen-generated header and a pinned ABI version, exposing JSON-in/JSON-out helpers: chio_verify_capability_json, chio_verify_receipt_json_with_trusted_signers, chio_verify_manifest_json, chio_sign_json_ed25519, chio_canonicalize_json, chio_sha256_hex_*, over a ChioFfiResult {status, error_code, ChioFfiBuffer} contract with chio_buffer_free. chio-cpp-kernel-ffi adds the full kernel decision (chio_kernel_evaluate_json, chio_kernel_verify_capability_with_context_json). Dlopen this via koffi (pure FFI, no node-gyp) so the agent-hooks gate decision is sub-millisecond.
ideas.chio_capability: crates/sdk/chio-bindings-ffi (CHIO_FFI_ABI_VERSION=1, include/chio/chio_ffi.h, ARCHITECTURE.md) and crates/sdk/chio-cpp-kernel-ffi (include/chio/chio_kernel_ffi.h)
ideas.orca_surface: New src/main/runtime/chio-ffi.ts that dlopens libchio_bindings_ffi.{dylib,so,dll} via koffi and exposes typed verifyCapability()/verifyReceipt(), consumed by the agent-hooks dispatcher (src/main/agent-hooks/server.ts). The existing tweetnacl crypto in src/main/runtime/e2ee-crypto.ts is the precedent for doing crypto in main.
ideas.user_value: Synchronous, zero-IPC capability and receipt verification on the hot path, so turning Orca's fire-and-forget agent-hooks bus into a fail-closed gate adds no socket latency to every agent action.
ideas.moat: Two transports over one Rust truth (FFI for hot verification, sidecar for stateful settlement/approvals), with the JS side asserting chio_ffi_abi_version() at startup so a binary/JS mismatch fails closed. The cbindgen header plus ARCHITECTURE.md make the contract self-documenting.
ideas.risk: Introduces the first non-TS native artifact into Orca's electron-builder packaging, code-signing, and notarization (the fork has zero Rust today). koffi sidesteps the N-API ABI-per-Electron-version problem but still needs per-OS prebuilt libs notarized, and the ChioFfiBuffer free contract must be wrapped to avoid leaks.

ideas.title: Mount the existing chio-cli React dashboard as Orca's Attested Receipts and Budget tabs (shared stack, near-zero porting)
ideas.one_liner: The Chio receipt dashboard is already React 18 + Vite + TypeScript with ReceiptTable, BudgetSparkline, DelegationChain, PortableReputationPanel, ProofRoomView - the same stack as Orca's renderer (React 19 + Vite).
ideas.description: chio-cli ships dashboard/ as a React/Vite/TS app using @tanstack/react-table and a lightweight SVG sparkline, with a documented runtime contract: Bearer token from ?token=, GET /v1/receipts/query, /v1/receipts/analytics, /v1/lineage/:capabilityId and /chain. chio-cli depends on axum 0.8 + tower-http and the dashboard proxies /v1/* to localhost:8080, so the backend exists. Port the components into Orca's renderer and feed them through the commerce:* IPC channel instead of exposing :8080.
ideas.chio_capability: crates/products/chio-cli/dashboard (api.ts typed fetch wrappers; components/ReceiptTable.tsx, BudgetSparkline.tsx, DelegationChain.tsx, PortableReputationPanel.tsx, ProofRoomView.tsx, each with a co-located .test.tsx) backed by chio-cli's axum + tower-http server
ideas.orca_surface: Port dashboard/src/components/* into src/renderer/src as a new Attested Receipts tab beside the annotate-AI-diffs review surface, and feed BudgetSparkline + OperatorSummary into the existing usage/rate-limit panel (src/main/rate-limits, mobile AccountUsage.tsx). The renderer proxies /v1/receipts/query and /v1/lineage through commerce:* IPC, so api.ts ports almost verbatim.
ideas.user_value: Users review not just code diffs but the signed economic and capability decisions each agent made (cost charged, delegation chain, settlement status), with the same component library, so the fork inherits a production-grade audit UI rather than building one.
ideas.moat: The dashboard README encodes hard-won correctness rules (totals come from /analytics not client-side reconstruction of paged subsets; highest-severity firing alert selects the primary route; a missing trend renders 'none' and must not hide a firing alert). A from-scratch fork reinvents and gets these wrong; Chio ships them tested.
ideas.risk: React 18 (dashboard) vs React 19 (Orca) minor drift, and Tailwind v4 / Radix theming must reconcile with the dashboard's plain index.css. The dashboard assumes a Bearer-token HTTP backend; inside Electron the cleaner path proxies those reads through commerce:* IPC rather than exposing :8080 to the renderer.

ideas.title: Bind agent identity through chio-kernel-mobile UniFFI on the phone companion; QR pairing becomes the mandate-signing moment
ideas.one_liner: Orca's mobile companion is Swift (iOS) + Kotlin (Android); chio-kernel-mobile emits Swift + Kotlin bindings from one UniFFI .udl, so the phone verifies capabilities and signs receipts natively, in-process, no IPC.
ideas.description: chio-kernel-mobile uses UniFFI 0.28 (staticlib for iOS, cdylib for the Android NDK, JSON-in/JSON-out) and exposes evaluate(), sign_receipt(), verify_capability_with_context(), verify_passport(), verify_mobile_receipt(), plus attest_app_attest()/verify_app_attest_evidence() (iOS App Attest) and attest_play_integrity()/verify_play_integrity_evidence() (Android Play Integrity). The QR pairing flow becomes the human-approval step that calls sign_receipt() to mint a time-bounded spend mandate, with device-integrity evidence bound into the approval.
ideas.chio_capability: crates/kernel/chio-kernel-mobile (UniFFI .udl driving Swift + Kotlin from one compiled artifact; entry points in src/lib.rs)
ideas.orca_surface: mobile/app/pair.tsx / pair-scan.tsx / pair-confirm.tsx over the existing tweetnacl e2ee device channel. A high-value purchase pushes a notification ('Agent X wants to spend $Y on compute'); the user taps approve, verify_app_attest_evidence binds the device-integrity proof into the signed approval, and verify_mobile_receipt gates settlement.
ideas.user_value: Autonomous commerce with a hardware-attested human circuit-breaker that runs on the phone itself: the approving device proves it is a genuine, unrooted iOS/Android device and the approval is a replayable cryptographic artifact, not a fire-and-forget push.
ideas.moat: App Attest / Play Integrity binding on the approval device is something no agent-runner fork has, and it directly answers AP2's consent-and-intent-ambiguity dispute driver. UniFFI generating both Swift and Kotlin from one .udl keeps the iOS and Android companions in lockstep with kernel changes for free.
ideas.risk: Orca mobile is Expo/React-Native (TS) with a native audio module; adding a UniFFI lib means new Swift Package + Android NDK build steps and Expo config-plugin/prebuild wiring. App Attest and Play Integrity need real Apple/Google enrollment and server-side nonce issuance to be meaningful, which is operational weight beyond the fork.

ideas.title: Create a chio-orca product crate (mirroring chio-mercury / chio-wall) so the cockpit is a versioned Chio entrypoint and the TS fork stays rebrand-only
ideas.one_liner: Chio already ships products as a thin binary plus a typed *-core contract crate; add chio-orca + chio-orca-core so all Orca-specific Rust lives in-tree, versioned with the protocol, and the Electron fork carries only brand strings plus IPC glue.
ideas.description: The repo has an established product-layering convention: chio-mercury (binary 'mercury') over chio-mercury-core ('typed MERCURY evidence contracts layered on Chio receipt truth'); chio-wall over chio-wall-core ('typed Chio-Wall control-path contracts layered on Chio guard and receipt truth'). Both declare public_entrypoint=true and are gated by the rust_public_entrypoints allowlist in the root Cargo.toml, with xtask plus crates/tooling (chio-spec-validate, chio-conformance) enforcing the boundary. Follow it: chio-orca-core holds the cockpit's wire contracts as schema-tagged serde types; chio-orca is the binary Electron main spawns.
ideas.chio_capability: crates/products/chio-mercury(+ -core) and chio-wall(+ -core) as the template; root Cargo.toml rust_public_entrypoints allowlist; crates/tooling/chio-spec-validate and chio-conformance
ideas.orca_surface: chio-orca-core defines the commerce:* IPC request/response types, the worktree-to-WorkflowBudgetPool mapping, and the agent-hooks gate-decision schema. chio-orca (a thin superset of chio-api-protect) is what Electron main spawns. The forked Orca repo then contains only: rebranded brand strings (appId com.stablyai.orca plus the ~56 brand paths and bin shims), the new src/main/ipc/commerce.ts, and the ported dashboard components. The Lovecast Inc. MIT notice is retained in every kept file; only net-new Chio files carry fresh copyright.
ideas.user_value: The fork's maintenance burden collapses: protocol and commerce logic live in the Rust monorepo (one cargo build --workspace, conformance-tested, fail-closed by house rule), and the daily-shipping Orca upstream is tracked as a rebrand-plus-thin-glue layer that is far cheaper to rebase than a deep TS rewrite.
ideas.moat: Putting Orca-specific contracts in a versioned *-core crate behind the same public_entrypoint allowlist and conformance harness that govern chio-mercury/chio-wall holds the cockpit's commerce surface to the same fail-closed, schema-pinned bar as the protocol. A fork that scatters this logic across TypeScript inherits none of those guarantees and drifts on every upstream rebase.
ideas.risk: Keeping a daily-shipping ~5,120-file upstream mergeable while injecting a commerce:* namespace is a continuous rebase tax even with glue minimized; the ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION bump needed to make the hook a blocking allow/deny gate is a wire change that may collide with upstream's own reserved next-version work. A hard fork trades that tax for losing Orca's daily features.

ideas.bold_bet: Do NOT build a sidecar or an HTTP server from scratch - the grounding digest's 'no long-running kernel server' gap is wrong. chio-api-protect is already a finished, unsafe-forbidden axum control plane (/chio/evaluate, /v1/capabilities/mint and /release, /v1/receipts and /verify, /approvals/*) with its production-vs-advisory route boundaries pre-documented, chio-cli already serves the dashboard backend on :8080, and chio-proof-room and chio-control-plane both run axum. The boldest, highest-leverage move is therefore a two-transport bridge that writes almost no new Rust: (1) spawn chio-api-protect as Orca's bundled commerce sidecar behind a single new src/main/ipc/commerce.ts (one-line registerCommerceHandlers() addition, mirroring the proven token-authed terminal-daemon socket pattern) for stateful settlement, capability minting, and human approvals; and (2) dlopen chio-bindings-ffi (cbindgen header, pinned CHIO_FFI_ABI_VERSION=1, JSON-in/JSON-out) via koffi inside Electron main for sub-millisecond, zero-IPC capability and receipt verification on the agent-hooks hot path. Both transports hit the same Rust truth, the JS side asserts the ABI version at startup so a mismatch fails closed, and the entire Orca-specific surface is confined to a thin chio-orca/chio-orca-core product crate plus brand strings - so the fork is rebrand-plus-glue, not a rewrite, and the daily-shipping upstream stays rebaseable.

ideas.lens: The killer demo / wow moment: the single 90-second sequence that makes someone say "I need this"

ideas.title: The $47K Runaway, Stopped Mid-Keystroke
ideas.one_liner: Watch an agent try to overspend live, and watch the kernel refuse the very next paid tool call before money moves.
ideas.description: Split-screen in the Orca terminal pane: an agent is buying compute/API calls in a loop, with a live spend bar in the usage panel climbing toward its cap. The operator drags the budget down (or flips kill_switch) on their phone. On the agent's NEXT paid call the bar goes red, the terminal prints a fail-closed denial, and a signed CreditBondedExecutionFinding with code kill_switch_enabled (or reserve_not_locked / outstanding_delinquency) renders inline. The punchline card: 'This is not a dashboard alert. The call never executed.' This is the literal answer to the widely-cited $47K LangChain runaway: enforcement lives in the kernel, not the prompt.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit capital_and_execution: CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier, require_locked_reserve, deny_if_outstanding_delinquency) -> CreditBondedExecutionDecision::Deny with CreditBondedExecutionFindingCode; chio-metering budget.rs BudgetEnforcer for the live spend bar
ideas.orca_surface: The account/usage/rate-limit panel (src/main/rate-limits, mobile AccountUsage.tsx) repurposed as a live spend meter, plus the agent's terminal split showing the denial; the kill flip happens on the mobile companion
ideas.user_value: The first agent cockpit where 'the agent cannot overspend' is a provable runtime fact, not a hope. Directly defuses the #1 fear blocking autonomous-agent adoption.
ideas.moat: Out-of-agent runtime enforcement is the white space every payment standard (AP2/ACP/x402) explicitly punts on. The deny is a signed, replayable artifact with a typed finding code, not a log line. No fork target has any money concept at all.
ideas.risk: Needs the agent-hooks bus turned from fire-and-forget into a blocking allow/deny gate (an ORCA_HOOK_PROTOCOL_VERSION wire change). The denial path itself is real and tested; the live interception is the build.

ideas.title: Fan-Out Wallet Race: One Budget, Five Agents, Atomic
ideas.one_liner: Fan one prompt across five worktrees, each gets a capped slice of one shared budget pool, and the sixth agent is rejected before it can spawn.
ideas.description: User hits Orca's 'fan across N agents'. Instead of five siloed processes, a WorkflowPreflightPlan materializes on screen: parent_task with a $50 pool, five child_tasks each minted a $10 cost-capped, time-bounded CapabilityToken (a 'wallet chip' on each worktree card). The user tries to add a sixth at $10 and it bounces client-side with workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded before any agent runs. Then the agents race; one wallet chip drains faster (it bought a pricey tool), and the HUD shows the pool draining in real time. Wow moment: parallel agents that share money safely, with currency coherence enforced.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-workflow-preflight WorkflowBudgetPool + WorkflowPreflightPlan (parent_task -> child_tasks, budget_minor, workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded); chio-open-market bidding.rs bid()->SignedAskResponse minting a per-worktree scoped CapabilityToken (max_invocations, max_cost_per_invocation, max_total_cost)
ideas.orca_surface: The parallel-worktrees orchestration view (fan-one-prompt-across-N), with a per-worktree 'wallet' chip in the sidebar and a shared-pool HUD above the worktree grid
ideas.user_value: Turns Orca's signature parallel-orchestration UX into a marketplace of cooperating agents that cannot collectively blow a budget. Each agent buys exactly the tool access it needs and no more.
ideas.moat: Maps a unique Orca UX (fan-out/merge-winner) onto a primitive no competitor has: a per-child capability wallet drawn from one currency-coherent pool, rejected at preflight. Siloed-process forks structurally cannot do shared-balance fan-out.
ideas.risk: Budget state is in-memory/caller-supplied today (no durable concurrency-safe ledger), so a true atomic multi-worktree draft needs a small shared ledger behind chio-store-sqlite to be race-proof in the live demo.

ideas.title: Click-To-Buy-The-API, Settled On-Chain in 30 Seconds
ideas.one_liner: Click a paid endpoint in Design Mode, and the agent pays it in USDC over x402 with a Chio-attested, on-chain-settled receipt before your eyes.
ideas.description: In Orca's embedded Chromium Design Mode the user clicks a data/API element behind an HTTP 402. Chio builds X402PaymentRequirements, the agent signs an EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization, an EVM escrow lock fires, and on the testnet the tx confirms. The Design Mode overlay flips the element from a lock icon to a green 'paid' state, and a Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact (status authorized->settled, with anchor-inclusion proof) drops into the review pane with a clickable tx hash. This is a full end-to-end autonomous-commerce loop (discover -> price -> pay -> settle -> attest) with zero fiat rail required.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-settle payments.rs (X402PaymentRequirements, EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization) + evm/prepare.rs (prepare_web3_escrow_dispatch, prepare_merkle_release); chio-web3 settlement.rs Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact; chio-agent-web-interop x402.rs verifier (status authorized|settled|refunded, bound chio_payment_receipt_ref)
ideas.orca_surface: Design Mode (embedded Chromium click-to-prompt) extended to 'click to purchase this API/data'; the resulting receipt lands in the annotate-AI-diffs review pane
ideas.user_value: Demonstrates agents transacting with the real open web (the x402 Bazaar of 10,000+ paid endpoints) from a familiar point-and-click surface, settled and receipted, not mocked.
ideas.moat: chio-settle already executes live USDC escrow lock/release and EIP-3009 today, so the loop is real on testnet without building a PSP. Reuses Design Mode (a marquee Orca feature) as the buy surface, which no headless payment SDK can match.
ideas.risk: Crypto-rail-first; a fiat version needs a licensed custody partner. Demo must run on testnet and pre-stage a funded operator treasury key to keep inside 90 seconds.

ideas.title: Approve The Spend With Your Thumb (Phone Circuit-Breaker)
ideas.one_liner: Agent wants to spend $80 on GPU time, your phone buzzes, you tap approve, and your tap becomes the cryptographic mandate the kernel enforces.
ideas.description: An agent hits a spend above its autonomy tier. Instead of proceeding or silently failing, the kernel pauses and pushes a notification to the Orca mobile companion: 'Agent worktree-3 wants to spend $80 on compute.' The user taps Approve. That tap mints a signed mandate (the same did:chio key that pays and that the kernel meters), the CapabilityToken's cost cap lifts to $80 for this one call, and the agent resumes. The phone screen and the desktop review pane both show the signed approval receipt. This binds the AP2 'consent and intent ambiguity' dispute driver to a verifiable, replayable artifact.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-governance CapabilityLeaseArtifact (issuer->subject scoped grant, validity window) + chio-credit autonomy-tier gating; chio-did/chio-credentials bind the human tap to the agent's signing key; reuses Orca e2ee-keypair pairing as the human-approval channel
ideas.orca_surface: The mobile companion's existing 'notify when an agent needs you' + steer-from-phone loop (mobile/app pairing flow) becomes a one-tap spend-approval that gates the kernel
ideas.user_value: Autonomous commerce with a human circuit-breaker that is demo-friendly and emotionally legible: a single thumb-tap is the difference between the agent proceeding or being denied.
ideas.moat: The approval is cryptographically the same key that authorizes, pays, and is metered, so the consent is non-repudiable and court-replayable. Competitors' 'approve' buttons write a flag; this mints a signed mandate the runtime enforces.
ideas.risk: Requires the blocking hook gate (shared with idea 1) plus wiring the mobile pairing channel to mandate minting. The mandate->capability bridge helper is described as a gap, so it must be built.

ideas.title: Two Kernels, One Truth: The Cross-Org Co-Signed Receipt
ideas.one_liner: An agent at company A buys a service from company B, and both kernels sign the SAME receipt bytes, so neither party can later deny the transaction.
ideas.description: In the review pane after a cross-org purchase, the operator clicks a receipt and a 'Dual-Signed' badge expands: org A's kernel signature AND org B's kernel signature, both over identical CoSigningBody bytes, both verified against pinned peer keys. The operator clicks 'verify offline' and chio-attest-buyer replays the whole lineage bundle (buyer_id, capability, settlement_claimed) green, with no network call. The closing frame: 'Both sides signed. This holds up in a dispute.' This is the tamper-evident, cross-party audit trail the entire market admits does not exist.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-federation bilateral.rs DualSignedReceipt over CoSigningBody (strict: both signatures must validate against pinned peers); chio-attest-buyer offline verify_buyer_attestation with receipt-lineage replay; ChioReceipt FinancialReceiptMetadata (cost_charged, SettlementStatus, root_budget_holder)
ideas.orca_surface: The annotate-AI-diffs review pane gains an 'Attested Receipts' tab where each paid cross-org call shows a co-signature badge and an offline-replay 'verify' button
ideas.user_value: Gives regulated buyers a provable, exportable, two-party audit record of what an autonomous agent bought, the single biggest blocker to moving agents from PoC to production.
ideas.moat: Bilateral kernel co-signing plus offline buyer-side proof replay is deep, already-tested machinery (strict pinned-peer verification) that is years ahead of any agent runner and maps directly to EU AI Act / PCI-DSS export.
ideas.risk: Quietest of the demos visually (it is verification, not action), so it needs strong framing to land as a wow rather than a feature tour. Mitigate by pairing it as the proof-coda after a louder idea.

ideas.title: Flip It Live: Shadow -> Active Autonomous Pricing
ideas.one_liner: An agent-run pricing engine watches in Shadow mode, you flip one toggle to Active, and the next provider purchase is auto-priced and auto-bid with no human in the loop.
ideas.description: A side panel shows AutonomousPricingDecision recommendations (Reprice / BindWithinEnvelope) streaming in AutonomousAutomationMode::Shadow, each tagged ShadowOnly and tied to prior signed artifacts. The operator flips the dial to Active. The very next time an agent needs a tool, the cockpit ranks providers by signed reputation, auto-bids, and binds within envelope, all AutoApproved, with the decision lineage shown. The watchdog (chio-settle automation) silently reconciles settlement and only pages the human on ManualOverrideRequired. Wow moment: the cockpit just made and executed an economic decision by itself, under a visible governance gate you control.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-autonomy model.rs AutonomousAutomationMode (Shadow/Advisory/Active) + AutonomousPricingDecision + review states (AutoApproved/HumanReviewRequired/ShadowOnly/Blocked); chio-settle automation.rs SettlementWatchdogJob (EscrowTimeout/FinalityObservation/BondExpiry -> ManualOverrideRequired); chio-reputation tiers for the provider ranking
ideas.orca_surface: The account-switcher / native marketplace UI becomes a provider-picker ranked by signed reputation; an 'autonomy dial' (Shadow/Advisory/Active) sits above it, watchdog alerts route to existing notifications
ideas.user_value: Shows the graduated-trust story: you can run the economic brain in observe-only, gain confidence from the shadow log, then promote it to act, with a kill switch always one click away.
ideas.moat: A staged Shadow->Advisory->Active autonomy mode with evidence-referential decisions and a watchdog that pages only on override is a governance posture no payment rail or agent runner offers. It is the safe on-ramp enterprises require.
ideas.risk: The most ambitious to make legible in 90 seconds (autonomous decisioning is abstract). Risk of looking like magic/hand-waving; needs the decision lineage visibly tied to prior receipts to feel trustworthy rather than a black box.

ideas.bold_bet: Idea 3, "Click-To-Buy-The-API, Settled On-Chain in 30 Seconds." It is the boldest because it is the only demo that closes the entire autonomous-commerce loop on screen with a real money rail (not a mock): a human clicks a paid endpoint inside Orca's signature Design Mode, an untrusted agent signs an EIP-3009 transfer-with-authorization, chio-settle fires a live USDC escrow lock/release on an EVM testnet, and a verifiable Web3SettlementExecutionReceiptArtifact with a clickable tx hash lands in the review pane, all inside 30 seconds. Nothing in the fork target has any concept of money, and no competing payment SDK can offer point-and-click-to-purchase from an embedded browser. It is high-wattage, end-to-end, and provably real because chio-settle already executes the on-chain escrow and EIP-3009 flows today, so the demo rests on shipped code rather than a promise. The honest caveat (crypto-rail-first, testnet-staged) is exactly the strategically correct first loop: it needs no fiat custody license to be true.

Sell the NO, not the YES. The entire market is building rails that let agents spend faster (ACP checkout, x402 micropayments, AgentCore wallets). The defensible product is the opposite: a cockpit whose headline artifact is a cryptographic proof that an autonomous agent was structurally PREVENTED from overspending, over-disclosing, or over-reaching, and was provably more conservative than a human operator would have been. Concretely: fork Orca, keep chio-credit's simulation_first_only / external_execution_authoritative=false posture as a hard product stance (Chio never touches money), and make the flagship deliverable a one-click 'Restraint Receipt' bundle per worktree that fuses chio-autonomy's AutonomousComparisonReport (proving the agent priced/spent NarrowerThanManual), chio-disclosure-lineage's DisclosureLeakageLedger (proving what the agent could NOT infer), and the Merkle receipt log (proving the kernel refused the call that breached the mandate). This is the artifact regulators, insurers, and enterprise risk committees will actually pay for, it is the answer to the '$47k runaway agent' story that no payment rail can produce, and it is defensible precisely because it requires the out-of-agent kernel + receipt substrate competitors chose not to build. Everyone else is selling the gas pedal; Chio sells the signed, court-admissible brake.

ideas.title: Restraint Receipts: prove the agent was more conservative than a human
ideas.one_liner: A signed 'we did LESS than you authorized' artifact, the inverse of every checkout receipt on the market.
ideas.description: chio-autonomy already emits an AutonomousComparisonReport whose disposition can be NarrowerThanManual / WiderThanManual against a manual baseline, plus AutonomousDriftReport with a rollback_plan and fail_safe_engaged flag. Wire the agent-hooks bus so that when a worktree finishes a spend session, Orca assembles a Restraint Receipt: the comparison disposition, every drift signal that fired, and the kernel decisions where a paid tool call was refused because the mandate was exhausted. The contrarian move is that the product's hero number is not 'spent $X' but 'stayed $Y under the human-equivalent envelope, provably.' Insurers and enterprise risk teams underwrite on demonstrated restraint, not on dashboards.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-autonomy (AutonomousComparisonReport NarrowerThanManual, AutonomousDriftReport, AutonomousSafeState), kernel Merkle receipt log
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Restraint' tab beside the annotate-AI-diffs review pane in src/renderer; assembled by a commerce:* IPC handler fed from the agent-hooks subsystem (src/main/agent-hooks)
ideas.user_value: An enterprise can hand its auditor/insurer a cryptographic proof that its autonomous agents acted more conservatively than a human would have, turning 'agent risk' from a blocker into a discount.
ideas.moat: Requires the out-of-agent comparison baseline + signed receipt substrate. A payment rail (ACP/x402/AgentCore) can prove a payment happened; none can prove a payment was deliberately NOT made or was narrower than authorized, because they have no kernel mediating and recording refusals.
ideas.risk: Generating a credible 'manual baseline' to compare against is non-trivial; if the baseline is hand-wavy the proof is weak. Mitigate by deriving the baseline from the operator's own historical signed receipts (chio-reputation corpus) rather than a synthetic policy.

ideas.title: Proof-of-Ignorance: a privacy receipt for what the agent could NOT learn
ideas.one_liner: Sell the absence of data exposure as a signed artifact, not just access control as a setting.
ideas.description: chio-disclosure-lineage carries a DisclosureLeakageLedger of per-field entries (field, leakage_kind, allowed_by_profile, residual_inference_note) over a transaction_passport_ref, plus a signed lineage subgraph with redactions. The contrarian insight: in agent-to-agent commerce the scary part is not payment, it is that an autonomous buyer agent silently exfiltrates the principal's context to a seller agent. Most players bolt on redaction as config; nobody ships a verifiable certificate of non-disclosure. Surface a 'Privacy Ledger' per transaction showing exactly which fields crossed the boundary, which were redacted, and the residual_inference_note for what a clever counterparty could still deduce. This is the BBS+/selective-disclosure story made into a buyer-facing product.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-disclosure-lineage (DisclosureLeakageLedger, SignedLineageSubgraph, DisclosureLineageVerifierReport), chio-selective-disclosure (BBS+)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Privacy Ledger' collapsible inside the per-purchase commerce card in the worktree view; verifier runs in the Chio sidecar, rendered via commerce:* IPC, also pushed to mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx for phone approval
ideas.user_value: A buyer can prove to its own compliance team (and a counterparty can be held to) exactly what was and was not disclosed in an agent transaction, including honest disclosure of residual inference risk.
ideas.moat: The residual_inference_note + signed lineage redaction graph is a genuinely novel artifact; competitors treat privacy as an input policy, not a signed output certificate that survives offline audit.
ideas.risk: Computing honest residual_inference_note entries is hard and easy to get wrong; over-claiming privacy is a liability. Start with conservative, manually-curated leakage_kind taxonomies per tool adapter.

ideas.title: Seller slashing in the cockpit: an accountable anti-Bazaar marketplace
ideas.one_liner: x402 Bazaar is pay-and-pray; make sellers post bonds that get slashed from signed receipts, visible in Orca.
ideas.description: chio-open-market already ships OpenMarketFeeScheduleArtifact with OpenMarketBondRequirement, OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact with OpenMarketPenaltyAction (HoldBond / SlashBond / ReverseSlash) and OpenMarketAbuseClass (FraudulentListing, ReplayPublication, UnverifiableListingBehavior), driven by OpenMarketPenaltyEvaluation. The contrarian bet against the entire discovery-marketplace trend (x402 Bazaar, 10k+ endpoints): discovery is commoditizing to zero, but accountability is not. Make Orca the cockpit where a buyer agent only transacts with sellers who have posted a slashable bond, and where bad service auto-emits a signed penalty that slashes the bond and re-prices reputation. Losing the bond is tied to the same Merkle receipt that proves the bad delivery.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-open-market (OpenMarketBondRequirement, OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact, SlashBond, OpenMarketAbuseClass, OpenMarketPenaltyEvaluation), chio-reputation, chio-settle for bond custody on-chain
ideas.orca_surface: Seller 'bond + slash history' chips in the native marketplace/account-switcher UI; an `orca commerce penalize` CLI verb and a commerce:* handler that emits the signed OpenMarketPenaltyArtifact when a buyer flags bad delivery
ideas.user_value: Buyers get recourse, not just refunds-on-trust; sellers with skin in the game rank higher and command premium pricing, creating a quality flight away from Bazaar-style markets.
ideas.moat: Slashing tied cryptographically to a signed delivery receipt (not a star rating) is unforgeable and portable. Bazaar and card-rail markets have no bond-slashing-from-receipt loop.
ideas.risk: Requires real bond custody (on-chain via chio-settle) to have teeth, and a fair dispute path before SlashBond, or it becomes a griefing vector. Gate SlashBond behind the OpenMarketPenaltyState Proposed -> Enforced flow with ReverseSlash as the appeal.

ideas.title: The custody-refusal moat: ship 'Chio never holds your money' as the feature
ideas.one_liner: While everyone races to issue agent wallets, win by structurally refusing custody and proving it.
ideas.description: chio-credit's CapitalExecutionInstructionSupportBoundary defaults automatic_capital_execution_supported=false and the control policy is simulation_first_only=true / external_execution_authoritative=false: Chio emits signed capital-execution INSTRUCTIONS and lets a licensed rail or custodian move funds. The regulatory grounding is blunt: custody triggers money-transmitter licensing (18 U.S.C. 1960, ~250k-350k of MTLs). The contrarian product stance: turn the gap (no fiat custody) into the headline. AgentCore Payments, Skyfire, Nekuda all take custody and inherit that liability; Chio-on-Orca is the only cockpit that is provably non-custodial, where every spend is a signed instruction the user's OWN licensed rail executes. Make the boundary visible: a 'custody-neutral' badge on every transaction with the signed instruction artifact and the external execution receipt side by side.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit/capital_and_execution (CapitalExecutionInstructionArtifact, simulation_first_only, custody_neutral_instruction_supported, multi-party OperatorTreasury+Custodian authority chain)
ideas.orca_surface: A 'Custody-Neutral' verification strip on each transaction in the commerce panel; the mobile pairing QR flow (mobile/app/pair*.tsx) becomes the human co-sign that authorizes the instruction without Chio ever touching funds
ideas.user_value: A startup can ship autonomous commerce without becoming a money transmitter, because Chio only signs instructions and the user's existing bank/CASP/stablecoin rail executes; the non-custodial design is provable, not just asserted.
ideas.moat: Architectural and legal, not merely technical: the simulation-first authority chain is already built and tested. Competitors who took custody to win UX cannot un-take it without dismantling their product.
ideas.risk: Non-custodial UX is clunkier (an external execution step) and a custodied competitor will feel smoother in a demo. Counter by making the co-sign a single phone tap and showing the liability trade-off explicitly.

ideas.title: Newcomer trust-decay pricing: agents pay a premium to be new
ideas.one_liner: Invert subscription pricing; brand-new agents transact at a deliberate handicap that decays with proven behavior.
ideas.description: chio-pheromone implements newcomer_discount_for_deposit (age/horizon ratio) and a signed scarcity policy with runtime_trust_floor_state, gossiped across operators via chio-federation. The contrarian economic bet: the market assumes agent identity is binary (KYA verified or not) and then static. Real defense against Sybil swarms and runaway new agents is a continuous trust-decay curve where a freshly-keyed agent gets throttled spend limits and pays a scarcity premium that mechanically relaxes as its signed behavioral history accrues. Surface this as the agent's 'trust age' that visibly matures in the cockpit, turning the cold-start problem into a priced, observable ramp rather than a yes/no gate.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-pheromone (newcomer_discount_for_deposit, PheromoneScarcityPolicy, PheromoneRuntimeTrustFloorState), chio-federation pheromone_gossip, chio-reputation tiers
ideas.orca_surface: A 'trust age' maturation meter on each worktree agent's wallet chip in the sidebar; the per-worktree budget ceiling fed by chio-metering is scaled by the live pheromone trust-floor state
ideas.user_value: Operators can safely let brand-new autonomous agents start transacting immediately at a throttled, priced handicap instead of blocking them, with the handicap provably decaying as the agent earns signed history.
ideas.moat: A decentralized, gossiped, signed trust-decay substrate is unique to chio-pheromone; it is an emergent-consensus channel competitors (static KYA credentials) structurally lack.
ideas.risk: Pheromone gossip needs a cross-operator network to be meaningful; with one operator it degrades to a local heuristic. Ship single-operator first (still useful as a per-worktree throttle), federate later.

ideas.title: Replayable forensics as a product: the time-machine for an agent's spend
ideas.one_liner: Sell deterministic replay of exactly why an agent bought something, not a log you read after the fact.
ideas.description: chio-replay-corpus writes deterministic replay fixtures (ReplayScenario, write_fixture over signed frames) with a TEE-attested bless audit (TeeBlessAuditBody, signed BlessFixture). chio-attest-buyer already replays a receipt-lineage bundle offline. The contrarian insight against the 'observability dashboard' crowd: dashboards show what happened; courts, disputes, and incident reviews need to re-execute the decision and get the same answer byte-for-byte. Package every contested agent purchase as a downloadable, TEE-blessed replay capsule that a third party (auditor, opposing counsel, insurer) loads and steps through deterministically. This is the audit-trail-standard vacuum the market openly admits exists, filled with a replayable artifact rather than a JSON dump.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-replay-corpus (ReplayScenario, write_fixture, TeeBlessAuditBody/BlessFixture), chio-attest-buyer (offline lineage replay), chio-tee
ideas.orca_surface: An 'Export Replay Capsule' action on any transaction in the review pane; a `orca commerce replay <receipt-id>` CLI verb that re-executes the decision deterministically and diffs against the recorded outcome
ideas.user_value: When an agent purchase is disputed or investigated, the operator hands over a self-contained capsule that any party can deterministically replay to see exactly why the kernel allowed the spend, making the trail defensible where untested code-based logs are not.
ideas.moat: Deterministic, TEE-blessed replay of a signed frame corpus is far beyond PostHog-style telemetry; it requires the whole signed-frame + attestation stack and is exactly the standardless gap the market concedes.
ideas.risk: Deterministic replay demands frame capture discipline at runtime; non-determinism (wall-clock, external API state) breaks byte-equality. Scope replay to the kernel's decision inputs (capability, policy, budget snapshot) rather than full external world state.

ideas.bold_bet: Rename the product around one provable promise: "No receipt, no spend." Every paid agent action in the forked Orca cockpit terminates in a signed, Merkle-committed ChioReceipt (chio.receipt.v1) carrying FinancialReceiptMetadata (cost_charged, root_budget_holder, SettlementStatus), and the brand makes that receipt the hero object, not the payment. The receipt mark is the logo, "the cockpit where agents transact" is the one-liner, and the wordmark replaces Orca's brand string across the ~56 paths plus appId (com.stablyai.orca -> com.chio.cockpit). This reframes the fork from "another agent runner" into the neutral, attested audit-and-enforcement plane that the commerce landscape openly admits nobody owns, and it is defensible because the receipt is cryptographic, replayable, and exportable for EU AI Act / PCI-DSS, which no MIT agent runner can claim.

ideas.title: Name the product after the receipt, not the payment
ideas.one_liner: Chio = the signed receipt every agent transaction leaves behind; tagline 'No receipt, no spend.'
ideas.chio_capability: chio-core-types ChioReceipt (chio.receipt.v1) + FinancialReceiptMetadata (cost_charged, root_budget_holder, SettlementStatus) in crates/core/chio-core-types/src/receipt/economics.rs; chio-transaction-passport (chio.transaction-passport.v1)
ideas.orca_surface: New 'Attested Receipts' tab beside Orca's annotate-AI-diffs review (src/renderer review surfaces; mobile review/[worktreeId].tsx); the receipt glyph becomes the app icon, replacing the Orca mark in the ~56 brand paths and appId com.stablyai.orca -> com.chio.cockpit
ideas.user_value: A developer reviews not just code diffs but the signed economic decisions an agent made; a CFO gets a tamper-evident audit trail instead of a dashboard. The brand promise is literally enforced by the kernel.
ideas.moat: The receipt is cryptographic, content-addressed, replayable offline (chio-attest-buyer), and SIEM/enterprise-exportable. A brand built on 'provable spend' cannot be cloned by a competitor that only logs to PostHog.
ideas.risk: Receipt-centric naming reads as compliance-heavy and could feel dry to the 100x-builder audience Orca courts; mitigate with the developer-facing 'Run the fleet. Sign the spend.' lockup.
ideas.description: Make the signed receipt the brand's hero object. 'Chio' is positioned as the thing that proves what an agent bought, not the wallet that paid. The headline narrative is 'every dollar an agent moves leaves a signed receipt,' and the logo is a receipt mark. This is the single cleanest reframe of the Orca fork because the receipt already exists in chio-core-types and already carries cost, budget, and settlement metadata.

ideas.title: Two audiences, one word: the Chio dual-meaning glossary
ideas.one_liner: To a developer Chio means 'capability-gated agent cockpit'; to a CFO it means 'every agent spend is mandated and attested' - same product, two landing pages.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier) and capital_and_execution 'simulation-first / custody-neutral' defaults (automatic_capital_execution_supported=false) in crates/economy/chio-credit/src/credit/capital_and_execution.rs; chio-metering BudgetEnforcer
ideas.orca_surface: Two onboarding flows behind one binary: the developer flow lands on the worktree fleet view; the operator/CFO flow lands on a per-worktree 'Spend mandate' panel grafted onto Orca's existing rate-limits/usage UI (src/main/rate-limits, mobile AccountUsage.tsx)
ideas.user_value: Developers hear 'run any CLI agent, capability-gated' and CFOs hear 'agents physically cannot overspend their mandate.' One product name carries both promises without a rebrand per buyer.
ideas.moat: The dual meaning is true, not marketing: the same key that the kernel meters is the key that pays, and the kill switch is a real CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy field. The CFO promise is enforced in Rust, not asserted in a deck.
ideas.risk: A word that means two things can end up meaning nothing; requires disciplined messaging architecture so the two narratives reinforce rather than dilute.
ideas.description: Define 'Chio' deliberately for both buyers and ship the glossary as brand canon. The developer reads autonomy and orchestration; the CFO reads control and accountability. Because chio-credit ships a kill switch, autonomy-tier ceiling, and custody-neutral-by-default capital layer, the CFO half of the meaning is provable. This lets one fork sell into both the builder and the finance/risk org from day one.

ideas.title: Name the autonomy dial after the real Shadow/Advisory/Active modes
ideas.one_liner: The Chio 'Autonomy dial' is brand-named directly from chio-autonomy's Shadow -> Advisory -> Active modes, turning a Rust enum into the product's signature interaction.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-autonomy AutonomousAutomationMode (Shadow/Advisory/Active) in crates/economy/chio-autonomy/src/model.rs; GovernedAutonomyTier (Direct/Delegated/Autonomous) in crates/core/chio-core-types/src/capability/governance.rs (requires_delegation_bond)
ideas.orca_surface: A per-agent 'Autonomy dial' control in the Orca worktree sidebar/agent card; higher settings (Active / Autonomous) visibly require a posted bond and a higher TrustTier before the agent may transact unattended, gated via a new commerce:* IPC namespace (src/main/ipc/commerce.ts)
ideas.user_value: Users get an intuitive, named slider for how much economic freedom each parallel agent has, with the safety property that the top notch demands a bond. The vocabulary (Shadow/Advisory/Active) becomes part of how people talk about the product.
ideas.moat: The modes are not UI sugar; they are evidence-referential states in chio-autonomy with review gates (AutoApproved/HumanReviewRequired/ShadowOnly). Competitors can draw a slider but cannot back it with signed advisory-vs-active decision artifacts.
ideas.risk: Three-mode naming may feel jargon-y to newcomers; needs a plain-language tooltip ('watch only / suggest / act') so the brand term and the human meaning land together.
ideas.description: Adopt chio-autonomy's existing Shadow/Advisory/Active vocabulary as a branded, user-facing interaction model rather than inventing new words. The dial maps one-to-one onto AutonomousAutomationMode, and the bond requirement maps onto GovernedAutonomyTier.requires_delegation_bond. This gives the fork a memorable signature gesture ('turn the agent up to Active') that is simultaneously the actual enforcement state in the protocol.

ideas.title: Brand the trust ladder: Unverified -> Attested -> Verified -> Premier
ideas.one_liner: Counterparties and worktrees wear a Chio tier badge drawn straight from chio-credentials::TrustTier, making 'Premier' a status agents earn and users recognize.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-credentials TrustTier (Unverified/Attested/Verified/Premier, thresholds 300/700/900 + behavioral-anomaly gate) in crates/trust/chio-credentials/src/trust_tier.rs; chio-reputation ReputationTier; chio-revocation-oracle freshness
ideas.orca_surface: A trust badge on every worktree/agent card and on the counterparty 'trust card' shown before one agent transacts with another tool server or agent (new commerce panel + mobile sessions view); tier gates discovery visibility and unattended spend
ideas.user_value: At a glance a user (or another agent) knows whether a counterparty is cleared to transact. 'Premier' becomes an aspirational, legible status that maps to real privileges (e.g. unattended autonomy).
ideas.moat: The tiers are deterministic, monotone in compliance score, and fail-pessimistic (a live anomaly blocks Premier). The ladder is computed from signed receipts and credentials, so a badge cannot be faked the way a star rating can.
ideas.risk: Tier names overlap with generic SaaS pricing tiers ('Premier'); brand guidance must make clear these denote earned trust, not a purchase, to avoid confusion with subscription plans.
ideas.description: Turn the existing four-rung TrustTier into a named, visible brand element. It already exists, is conservative by design, and gates real behavior. Surfacing it as a recognizable badge gives the product a shared trust language and lets the narrative say 'agents you can trust to transact' with a concrete artifact behind every word. It also seeds the counterparty-trust-card surface the trust layer is missing.

ideas.title: Name the swarm trust-channel 'Pheromone' and make it the differentiated story
ideas.one_liner: Chio's emergent, decentralized 'is this counterparty trusted by the swarm right now' signal is branded Pheromone, a story no competitor can tell.
ideas.chio_capability: chio-pheromone signed stigmergic substrate (PheromoneDeposit, runtime trust-floor state chio.runtime.trust-floor-state.v1, scarcity policy, newcomer-discount horizon) in crates/trust/chio-pheromone/src/lib.rs; gossiped via chio-federation pheromone_gossip
ideas.orca_surface: A live 'Pheromone' overlay in Orca's fleet view (the parallel-worktrees board) showing real-time swarm trust concentration on each tool server/agent, complementing the static TrustTier badge; surfaced through the commerce:* IPC namespace
ideas.user_value: Users see behavioral consensus form in real time across operators, not just a static credential. It explains, in one evocative word, why Chio's trust signal is alive rather than a stale score.
ideas.moat: Pheromone is a genuinely novel, Merkle-committed, gossiped trust substrate with scarcity and newcomer-discount economics; it is the most defensible single concept in the trust layer and gives the brand a memorable, ownable metaphor competitors lack entirely.
ideas.risk: The biology metaphor can read as gimmicky if shown without substance; it must be backed by a real, legible visualization or it undercuts the otherwise serious compliance narrative.
ideas.description: Lean into chio-pheromone as a named brand pillar rather than burying it as an implementation detail. It is the one trust channel that is decentralized, real-time, and emergent, and the metaphor (agents leaving trust trails) is instantly graspable. Branding it gives the product a distinctive narrative hook ('trust that the swarm computes') that differentiates Chio from every credential-and-score competitor.

ideas.title: Rename the CLI verbs so agents speak commerce: 'chio settle', 'chio mandate', 'chio buy'
ideas.one_liner: The forked Orca CLI gains a first-class 'chio commerce' verb family, fusing Orca's agent-driving CLI with the real chio-cli command tree so agents transact in the brand's own vocabulary.
ideas.chio_capability: crates/products/chio-cli (binary 'chio') already depends on chio-commerce-order, chio-credit, chio-settle with settle/market/capital/credit/liability verbs and a --budget-db flag; chio-open-market bidding.rs (bid/ask/accept); chio-metering budget
ideas.orca_surface: New 'orca commerce ...' / 'chio ...' verbs added in the same spec+handler pattern as Orca's existing CLI (src/cli/specs/*, src/cli/handlers/*), documented in a SKILL.md so coding agents treat commerce as first-class operations; signed JSON receipts surface back in the diff pane
ideas.user_value: Agents and operators set budgets, buy capabilities, and check settlement in plain, branded commands ('chio mandate grant', 'chio settle status'). The CLI is the product's verb-level brand voice and the lowest-friction integration path.
ideas.moat: The verbs map to already-wired crates that emit signed JSON, so every command produces an attested artifact. A competitor's 'buy' command returns a log line; Chio's returns a verifiable receipt the kernel will later enforce.
ideas.risk: Verb sprawl and naming collisions with Orca's existing CLI namespace; needs a tight, curated verb set so the commerce vocabulary stays memorable rather than becoming a sprawling subcommand jungle.
ideas.description: Treat the CLI as a primary brand surface and give it commerce verbs that match the narrative. Because chio-cli already ships settle/market/capital/credit/liability commands and Orca already treats agents as first-class CLI operators, fusing the two is additive. The verb set becomes how agents and humans speak the Chio brand, and every verb terminates in a signed artifact, reinforcing 'no receipt, no spend' at the command line.

critiques.dimension: Technical feasibility: fusing a 122-crate Rust protocol into a forked 40MB-TS Electron app, maintained by a small team
critiques.verdict: Buildable, but only if scoped hard. The bridge is the strongest part of the plan and is largely real today: chio-api-protect is a finished axum control plane pulling just 5 production crates (core-types, http-core, kernel, openapi, store-sqlite), and chio-bindings-ffi is a pinned-ABI (v1), JSON-in/JSON-out C surface that depends only on chio-core + chio-manifest. So you do NOT compile all 122 crates / 1190 lockfile packages into Electron; you ship two slim binaries. The fatal risk is not the bridge, it is the treadmill plus over-scope: the workspace builds with lto=fat + codegen-units=1 (cold release builds are many minutes, 13GB target), Orca ships daily, and the brainstorm casually fans 60+ features across FFI, sidecar, dashboard port, UniFFI mobile, and live on-chain settlement. Most of those features are reachable only on the slow sidecar path, several cited module paths are already stale, and the marquee on-chain demo is instruction-emitting only. A 2-4 person team can ship the budget/receipt/sidecar wedge; it cannot ship the full lens catalog without drowning in rebase and cross-language maintenance.
fatal_flaws: Hot-path FFI cannot enforce spend. The entire 'kernel refuses the next paid call' / anti-$47k-runaway pitch rests on BudgetEnforcer, which lives in chio-metering and is NOT in the FFI dependency closure (chio-core + chio-manifest only). The 14 extern-C functions are stateless verifiers (canonicalize, sha256, ed25519 sign/verify, verify capability/receipt/manifest JSON) with zero mint/budget/settle/escrow/approval/disburse. So budget enforcement on the agent-hooks bus MUST be an async localhost round-trip to the sidecar, not the advertised 'sub-millisecond zero-IPC' in-process call. The bridge brainstorm conflates 'verify a token locally' (FFI can) with 'check spend against a running budget' (sidecar only). This is recoverable but invalidates the headline latency story.

The 'live USDC on-chain in 30 seconds, rests on shipped code' demo is not shippable from this repo as-is. chio-settle is #![cfg(feature=\"web3\")] and its functions are prepare_transfer_with_authorization / prepare_* (artifact emitters). chio-credit/capital_and_execution is hardcoded simulation_first_only=true, external_execution_authoritative=false, automatic_capital_execution_supported=false. Nothing in-tree broadcasts a signed tx to a chain. A real testnet loop needs a separate signer + RPC broadcaster + key custody the team must build and operate, plus the full alloy EVM dependency stack. Several lenses present this loop as turnkey; it is not.

Fork-maintenance math is unbudgeted and underestimated. Orca ships daily and the plan rebrands ~56 brand paths + appId + bin shims while threading commerce:* IPC, a koffi FFI loader, ported dashboard, and (per some lenses) Swift/Kotlin UniFFI into a fast-moving upstream. Rebranded strings collide with upstream churn on nearly every rebase; the mobile-companion UniFFI path doubles the surface across three languages. With no stated rebase cadence or a thin chio-orca product-crate boundary actually built yet, a small team spends its capacity on merge conflicts, not features.
must_haves: Build a real chio-orca + chio-orca-core product crate FIRST (mirroring the existing chio-mercury/-core and chio-wall/-core template) so 100% of Orca-specific Rust and the commerce:* request/response schemas live in this repo, versioned with the protocol and behind the public_entrypoint allowlist. The forked Electron app must carry ONLY brand strings + one src/main/ipc/commerce.ts + ported dashboard components, or every upstream rebase corrupts. Without this boundary the fork is unmaintainable.

Pick a hard rebase contract before forking: pin to an Orca tag, rebase on a fixed cadence (e.g. weekly), and isolate all rename churn into a scripted, re-runnable brand-patch (sed/codemod) rather than hand edits, so a rebase is 're-apply patch' not 'resolve 200 conflicts'. Assert CHIO_FFI_ABI_VERSION and a sidecar /version handshake at Electron startup so any binary/JS drift fails closed.

Ship the sidecar-only wedge and stop. chio-api-protect as the bundled commerce sidecar behind commerce:* IPC (proven by Orca's existing token-authed terminal-daemon socket), the dashboard port (React 18+Vite -> Orca React 19+Vite is a minor skew, 14 components), and the budget/receipt path. Use FFI only for what it can actually do offline: local signature/expiry/canonicalization checks. Treat web3 settlement as feature-flagged, off by default, advisory until a broadcaster exists.

Re-pin every brainstorm reference to the live crate layout before estimating. commerce_order/agent_web have already moved out of chio-control-plane into standalone crates (chio-commerce-order, chio-transaction-passport, chio-agent-web-interop) in the current working tree; building against the cited src/commerce_order/* paths will not compile.

Bound the binary-distribution problem: the slim sidecar + FFI .dylib/.so/.dll must be built and code-signed/notarized per-platform (macOS/Windows/Linux) and bundled in the Electron packager. This is real release engineering on top of a 13GB-target, lto=fat workspace; CI build time and artifact signing must be planned, not assumed.

top_risks.risk: Upstream daily-ship cadence vs. rebrand surface: ~56 brand paths + appId collide with fast-moving Orca commits on nearly every rebase, and any new IPC/agent-hooks surface compounds it.
top_risks.mitigation: Scripted re-runnable brand codemod + pinned-tag weekly rebase + confine all custom logic to chio-orca-core and one commerce.ts file; never hand-edit upstream files except via the patch script.

top_risks.risk: Hot-path latency myth: agent-hooks gate advertised as sub-ms FFI is actually an async sidecar round-trip for any spend/budget/mandate decision (BudgetEnforcer is in chio-metering, outside the FFI closure).
top_risks.mitigation: Run the sidecar over a localhost Unix socket (reuse Orca's terminal-daemon pattern), keep it warm, batch checks; reserve FFI for offline signature/canonicalize/verify only and market it as such.

top_risks.risk: On-chain demo overpromise: 'live USDC settlement on shipped code' has no broadcaster/custody in-repo; capital execution is hardcoded simulation-first, non-authoritative.
top_risks.mitigation: Reframe the wedge as the audit + enforcement + custody-REFUSAL plane (which the code genuinely supports) and stage any chain loop as an explicitly separate, feature-flagged testnet add-on with its own signer service.

top_risks.risk: Scope explosion: 60+ ideas across FFI, sidecar, dashboard, UniFFI mobile, federation, pheromone gossip imply far more than a 2-4 person team can build or maintain.
top_risks.mitigation: Ship one vertical (budget pool on fan-out + per-worktree spend mandate + signed receipt tab) end to end; defer mobile/UniFFI, federation, pheromone, and marketplace bonds to post-PMF.

top_risks.risk: Cold-build and binary-bundling cost: lto=fat + codegen-units=1, 1190 packages, 13GB target, full alloy EVM stack pulled by chio-cli/settle; per-platform signing/notarization of the bundled binaries.
top_risks.mitigation: Build the slim sidecar/FFI from a feature-trimmed crate set (drop web3 from the default cockpit profile), use the docker-release thin-LTO profile for CI, and cache aggressively; only the 5-crate sidecar + 2-crate FFI need shipping, not the whole workspace.

top_risks.risk: Stale references in the plan (cited module paths already moved) cause estimation and wiring errors on day one.
top_risks.mitigation: Do a one-pass crate-map reconciliation against the current working tree before sprint planning; treat the brainstorm's paths as indicative, not authoritative.

top_risks.risk: UniFFI Swift+Kotlin mobile path triples the language surface and binds App Attest/Play Integrity work onto every kernel change.
top_risks.mitigation: Exclude mobile from v1 entirely; the desktop sidecar wedge stands alone, and chio-kernel-mobile (.udl + generated bindings) can be adopted later when the desktop contract is stable.

strongest_ideas: Ship chio-api-protect as the bundled commerce sidecar behind a commerce:* IPC namespace (Fork & rebrand lens): the single most feasible move; it is a finished axum control plane needing only config + one IPC file, pulls just 5 production crates, and reuses Orca's proven token-authed socket pattern. This is the backbone everything else hangs off.

Mount the existing chio-cli React dashboard as Attested Receipts / Budget tabs (Fork & rebrand lens): genuinely low-risk. React 18 + Vite + TS vs Orca's React 19 + Vite is a minor skew across 14 components, and the dashboard already encodes the hard correctness rules (totals from /analytics, not client reconstruction). Highest value-to-effort ratio.

Hard per-worktree spend mandate that fails the next paid call closed (x402 'Stripe for tools' lens) and the per-prompt fan-out budget pool (GTM lens): both map onto a real, tested primitive (BudgetEnforcer / WorkflowBudgetPool) and onto Orca's signature fan-out UX, and both are honestly deliverable via the sidecar gate. These are the credible wedge.

Signed IOU + receipt per call rendered in the review pane (x402 lens) and the Session Compliance Certificate on merge (Compliance lens): both are 'low' difficulty, lean on shipped crates (chio-credit hook, chio-cli cert.rs), and produce the differentiated artifact (a verifiable receipt) with no on-chain dependency. They survive the feasibility lens cleanly because they need no broadcaster, no mobile, no federation.

Local-only FFI verification on the agent-hooks bus, scoped to what chio-bindings-ffi can actually do (verify capability signature/expiry, canonicalize+hash a receipt, verify a manifest): feasible and fast precisely because it is stateless and offline; just do not market it as the spend gate.

critiques.dimension: Legal, payments & licensing (money-transmission/MSB, KYC/AML, custody, stablecoin/card-network rules, fork license/trademark/attribution)
critiques.verdict: Navigable, but only if the product ships in its non-custodial, instruction-and-attestation posture and treats the on-chain "execute" path as a regulated-operator add-on, not the default. The architecture is unusually well-positioned: chio-credit defaults to external_execution_authoritative=false, custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true, automatic_capital_execution_supported=false (verified in capital_and_execution.rs:255-266 and CapitalBookSupportBoundary:64-72), which is a genuine, code-enforced "Chio signs instructions, a licensed rail moves money" boundary that most agent-commerce rails lack. The fatal risk is that the headline demos ("Click-To-Buy-The-API, Settled On-Chain," escrow-on-delivery) deliberately cross that boundary: under the web3 feature chio-settle holds operator_private_key_hex (evm/sign.rs:163-182), signs ECDSA, and broadcasts via eth_sendTransaction (evm/prepare.rs:594-612, mod.rs:857), requiring automatic_dispatch_supported=true. Whoever runs that key and controls release is doing money transmission / custody, and the take-rate business model (skim 30-50bps on every settlement) is the single most license-triggering decision in the entire brainstorm. Custody and the facilitator fee, not stablecoins per se, are what turn this from a software vendor into a regulated MTL/MSB.
fatal_flaws: Settlement take-rate as the core revenue engine is near-fatal as designed. The business-model lens proposes Chio skim 30-50bps as a 'facilitator deduction' on every agent-to-agent settlement (chio-settle facilitator/paymaster deduction). Receiving compensation for the transmission of value, while controlling or directing the movement of funds, is the textbook definition of money transmission under FinCEN (31 CFR 1010.100(ff)) and most state MTL statutes. The 'we never take custody' defense collapses the moment Chio is in the flow of funds taking a cut: FinCEN's 2019 CVC guidance treats fee-taking facilitators that exercise control as MSBs even without holding a wallet. This is not navigable as a default product; it is navigable only as (a) a pure software license fee unrelated to transaction value, or (b) a fee collected BY a licensed partner who remits a referral share to Chio.

Operator-held private key + automatic on-chain escrow release IS custody, regardless of the 'non-custodial' branding. The web3 feature path (operator_private_key_hex in evm/types.rs:118, sign_digest in evm/sign.rs, submit_call->eth_sendTransaction) means an operator unilaterally signs and broadcasts USDC escrow lock/release. 'Total independent control over value' is the FinCEN custody test; holding the release key meets it.
