Marketing this as 'custody-neutral' (the contrarian lens's 'custody-refusal moat') while shipping a key-signing dispatcher is the kind of mismatch the SEC/CFTC/FinCEN and plaintiffs' bar treat as a material misrepresentation. The defensible artifacts (external_execution_authoritative=false) live in chio-credit; the demos route around them through chio-settle. The brand claim and the operative code path must be reconciled or it is fatal on both regulatory and consumer-protection grounds.

Agent-to-agent escrow with deadline-based automatic refund/release is the highest-risk single feature for unlicensed money transmission AND for acting as an unregistered clearing/settlement system. 'Escrow-on-delivery' (chio-settle prepare_dual_sign_release / prepare_escrow_refund) holds a third party's funds pending a condition and releases them. Holding funds belonging to two transacting parties pending performance is the classic money-transmitter/escrow-agent activity that is licensed state-by-state (and escrow-agent-licensed in CA, WA, etc.). Doing it on-chain does not exempt it; it adds Travel Rule (FinCEN/FATF) obligations for transmittals >= $3,000 once a VASP is involved. As shipped (operator broadcasts release), this is fatal without an MTL or a licensed escrow/custody partner.

KYA legal-entity binding mints an unlicensed identity/credential product into a regulated KYC chain without owning the KYC. The trust lens's KYA ReputationCredential 'issued by a licensed KYC provider' is fine ONLY if Chio is strictly the relying party and the credential issuer carries the KYC/AML obligation, the BSA recordkeeping, and the liability for a bad verification. If Chio is read as performing or warranting CIP/KYC, it inherits BSA program obligations (written AML program, CDD, SAR filing, recordkeeping) it is not set up to discharge. The Travel Rule overlay (Skyfire-style KYA) means counterparty PII must be transmitted and retained; mishandling it is both a BSA violation and a GDPR/CCPA exposure. The honest framing 'issuer is pinned, Chio only verifies' must be enforced in contract and code, or this becomes an unlicensed KYC/AML undertaking.
must_haves: Ship default-non-custodial and make the custody/broadcast path a gated, off-by-default, regulated-operator-only mode. The product default must be the chio-credit instruction posture (external_execution_authoritative=false, automatic_capital_execution_supported=false, custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true). The web3 auto-dispatch path (automatic_dispatch_supported=true, operator_private_key_hex, submit_call/eth_sendTransaction) must be a clearly separated SKU that only a customer-operated or licensed-partner-operated key can enable, with the key never bundled in the Orca distribution. 'Bring-your-own-licensed-rail' is the legal spine of the whole product.

Take a software fee, not a transaction-value take-rate, unless a licensed partner collects it. Replace 'Chio skims 30-50bps on settlement' as the core engine with (a) flat/seat/usage SaaS priced on attested tool-call mediation (chio-metering BillingExport, which is value-neutral), and (b) compliance/audit-export enterprise license. If a percentage-of-value fee is commercially essential, it must be charged and remitted by a licensed money transmitter / PSP partner who pays Chio a referral or technology fee, with Chio contractually never in control of, and never compensated as a function of, the movement of funds.

Route all fund movement, escrow, and stablecoin settlement through a licensed third party (PSP, MTL holder, qualified custodian, or a regulated stablecoin issuer's rail) under a written agreement that places custody, BSA/AML program, Travel Rule, sanctions screening, and consumer-protection obligations on that party. Card-network rails additionally require PCI-DSS scope minimization (do not touch PANs; the brainstorm correctly leans stablecoin-first, which avoids most card-network rules but NOT money transmission). The settlement watchdog, kill switch, and SettlementEmergencyControls are good, but they are controls on someone else's licensed activity, not a substitute for the license.

Implement sanctions (OFAC/SDN) and jurisdiction screening as a fail-closed precondition to any settlement or capability mint, and surface it as a first-class denial. Autonomous agents transacting peer-to-peer across borders (the chio-link cross-currency FX feature, OracleConversionEvidence) is a sanctions-evasion vector regulators will scrutinize. Screening cannot be the partner's problem alone if Chio is selecting counterparties; the Counterparty Trust Card and PassportVerifierPolicy should hard-block sanctioned/embargoed DIDs and jurisdictions before any token mints.

Reconcile the brand with the operative code path: do not market 'Chio never holds your money' / 'custody-refusal moat' while shipping a key-holding broadcaster. Either (a) gate and disclaim the custody path so the default truthfully matches the claim, or (b) drop the absolute custody-neutral marketing. Misalignment here is a deceptive-practices (FTC/UDAP) and securities-style misrepresentation risk, and it is the exact claim a regulator or plaintiff will test against evm/sign.rs and evm/prepare.rs.

MIT fork hygiene: retain the upstream MIT copyright/permission notice in every retained Orca file (the brainstorm's instinct to keep the Lovecast Inc. notice is correct), add Chio copyright only to net-new files, and ship a NOTICE/THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES manifest. This is straightforward and non-fatal. The real IP risk is trademark, not copyright.

Trademark and brand separation: do not retain 'Orca' or 'Stably' marks, the appId com.stablyai.orca, icons, or trade dress in the shipped Chio product; MIT licenses copyright, not trademarks. Confirm the 'Chio' wordmark/app name is clear of existing marks (do a clearance search) before the rebrand and public launch. Removing ~56 brand paths and the appId, as the brainstorm notes, is necessary not just cosmetic.

AML/MSB posture must be documented even in the pure-software case: a written policy stating Chio is a technology provider that does not transmit, hold, or control funds, plus contractual flow-downs to operators who DO move funds, plus a 'regulated activity is the operator's responsibility' clause in the EULA. The EU AI Act / PCI / ISO mappings already in-tree help the enterprise sale but do not address money-transmission; that gap must be closed explicitly.
strongest_ideas: The compliance/audit lens as a whole (Session Compliance Certificate, OCSF SIEM streaming, one-click EU AI Act/PCI evidence export, tamper-evidence monitor). These are value-neutral attestation and audit features that touch no money, trigger no MTL/MSB/custody analysis, and are exactly what the regulated buyer pays for. This is the safest revenue surface and should arguably lead the go-to-market.

The kill-switch / budget-enforcement cluster (chio-metering BudgetEnforcer, chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy kill_switch, WorkflowBudgetPool fan-out preflight, the '$47k runaway stopped mid-keystroke' demo). Refusing spend is the opposite of transmitting value; preventing a transaction has no custody or money-transmission footprint. It is the cleanest wedge and the contrarian 'sell the NO' framing is also the legally safest framing.

Restraint Receipts / Proof-of-Ignorance / replayable forensics (the contrarian lens). Proving an agent did LESS, or could not learn X, or replaying why it acted, are pure cryptographic attestation artifacts with zero payments-law surface. Strong differentiation, near-zero legal risk.

The custody-neutral instruction layer itself (chio-credit capital_and_execution: SignedCapitalExecutionInstruction with simulation_first_only=true, external_execution_authoritative=false, custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true, multi-party OperatorTreasury+Custodian authority chain). Verified in code. This is the single most defensible legal primitive in the repo: Chio emits a signed instruction and a licensed custodian executes. Every money feature should be built on THIS rather than on chio-settle's broadcasting path.

Rail-Neutral Receipt / cross-rail verifier (chio-transaction-passport projecting ACP+AP2+x402 into one signed chain) and Know-Your-Buyer attestation (chio-attest-buyer). Being a neutral verifier ABOVE the rails, rather than a rail, is both the competitive moat and the legal shelter: a verifier of someone else's regulated settlement is not itself a money transmitter.

Mobile phone-tap consent that mints a signed ApprovalCase/mandate (Secure-Enclave approver key). As a human-consent and authorization-evidence artifact it is low-risk and directly mitigates AP2's consent-ambiguity dispute driver; just ensure the tap authorizes a licensed rail's action rather than directly triggering a Chio-held-key broadcast.

top_risks.risk: Settlement take-rate (30-50bps facilitator deduction) makes Chio a fee-compensated participant in the flow of funds, the core trigger for money-transmitter / MSB licensing in 49+ US states and FinCEN registration; the 'non-custodial' defense does not survive being paid as a function of value moved while directing release.
top_risks.mitigation: Do not make value-based take-rate the core engine. Monetize via value-neutral SaaS (chio-metering BillingExport) and compliance/audit licenses. If a percentage fee is essential, have a licensed PSP/MTL partner collect and remit it, with Chio paid a technology/referral fee and contractually outside control of funds.

top_risks.risk: The web3 escrow path holds operator_private_key_hex and broadcasts USDC lock/release via eth_sendTransaction (evm/sign.rs, evm/prepare.rs:594, mod.rs:857), which is custody/control of value; shipping it as a default and branding it 'custody-neutral' is simultaneously an unlicensed-MT risk and a deceptive-marketing risk.
top_risks.mitigation: Gate the broadcasting path behind a separate regulated-operator SKU, never bundle the key, default to the chio-credit instruction-only posture, and align marketing so the absolute 'never holds money' claim only describes the default mode.

top_risks.risk: Agent-to-agent on-chain escrow (hold two parties' funds pending a co-signed deliverable, auto-refund on deadline) is licensed escrow-agent / money-transmission activity and pulls in FATF/FinCEN Travel Rule duties (>= $3,000 transmittals) once a VASP is in the loop.
top_risks.mitigation: Implement escrow only via a licensed custodian/escrow partner or a smart-contract escrow where neither Chio nor an operator holds the release key (release governed solely by the co-signed receipt verified on-chain), and add Travel Rule data handling at the partner boundary.

top_risks.risk: KYA / legal-entity binding and cross-border FX settlement create BSA/AML (CIP, CDD, SAR, recordkeeping), Travel Rule, and sanctions (OFAC) obligations, plus GDPR/CCPA exposure for transmitted counterparty PII; agents transacting across currencies and borders is a sanctions-evasion vector regulators will probe.
top_risks.mitigation: Keep Chio strictly a relying party on a licensed KYC issuer; push AML program, SAR, and Travel Rule duties contractually to that issuer and to the settlement partner; implement fail-closed OFAC/jurisdiction screening before any mint or settlement; minimize and encrypt PII (BBS+ selective disclosure helps).

top_risks.risk: Stablecoin-specific regime risk: US GENIUS Act / EU MiCA and issuer terms constrain who may handle and for what purpose; routing 'every paid action' through USDC at scale without a compliant issuer relationship invites issuer-terms termination and emerging-reg exposure.
top_risks.mitigation: Use a compliant issuer's sanctioned rail (e.g., Circle programmatic access under its terms), stay non-issuing and non-custodial, and keep settlement rail-agnostic so a single issuer/jurisdiction change is not existential.

top_risks.risk: Trademark/brand-dress carryover from the MIT fork: MIT licenses copyright, not the 'Orca'/'Stably' marks, icons, appId, or trade dress; retaining them, or launching 'Chio' without clearance, is infringement risk independent of the (easy) copyright-notice obligation.
top_risks.mitigation: Strip all upstream marks/appId/icons, retain MIT notices in kept files, ship a THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES NOTICE, and run a trademark clearance search on 'Chio' before public launch.

top_risks.risk: Securities/CFTC characterization of slashable seller bonds and on-chain penalty/slash mechanics (chio-open-market SlashBond, bond custody on-chain) if bonds are pooled, yield-bearing, or custodied by Chio.
top_risks.mitigation: Keep bonds operator/partner-custodied or smart-contract-escrowed, non-pooled, non-yield-bearing; document them as performance collateral with deterministic, receipt-evidenced slashing, not an investment product, and keep Chio out of bond custody.

critiques.dimension: Security & abuse surface (unauthorized spend, fraudulent billing, mandate bypass, key theft, money laundering)
critiques.verdict: The cryptographic spine is real and unusually strong: the kernel's ApprovalToken::verify_against actually binds governed_intent_hash to parameter_hash and enforces a non-empty trusted_approvers set (approval.rs:178-193); execution_nonce.rs binds (subject, capability, server, tool, parameter_hash) so a stolen approval cannot be replayed against a different call; chio-custody-hw ships genuine Apple App Attest CBOR verification with a pinned root and counter enforcement, Play Integrity, WebAuthn passkeys, and FIPS P-256/384 backends with a replay nonce store and rate limiter; and open-market bidding is demonstrably fail-closed on revoked/stale/expired listings and scope widening. So the phone-as-signer, the kill switch, the bonded-autonomy gate, the slashable-bond market, and the co-signed receipt are buildable on shipped code, not vapor. But two gaps are disqualifying for an autonomous-commerce product as pitched. First, there is zero AML / sanctions / Travel-Rule / legal-entity-KYC code anywhere in the repo (a case-insensitive grep across all crate sources returns nothing); the "KYA credential" is just a ReputationCredential with an issuer_allowlist, which is a trust tier, not identity. An agent marketplace that moves USDC with no sanctions screening and no transaction monitoring is a money-laundering conduit and is not legally deployable for the regulated-buyer ICP the brainstorm targets. Second, the headline enforcement claim ("a runaway agent physically cannot overspend") rests on BudgetEnforcer, which is an in-memory, single-process, non-atomic u64 counter with no shared store; across Orca's signature N-parallel-worktree fan-out there is no demonstrated cross-process spend ledger, so the fan-out double-spend is a real hole hiding behind a marketed feature.
fatal_flaws: No AML / sanctions / Travel-Rule / KYC primitive exists in the codebase (grep across all crate src returns zero hits for AML, OFAC, sanctions, launder, travel-rule, KYC). The brainstorm's 'KYA credential' is chio-credentials::ReputationCredential gated by an issuer_allowlist (artifact.rs:283, policy.rs:48) - a reputation tier, NOT a verified legal-entity binding and NOT sanctions screening. An agent-to-agent USDC marketplace with bonds, payouts, and revenue-splits to 'referrers' and 'mirrors' (Ecosystem lens) and cross-currency oracle settlement is a textbook layering/structuring venue. Shipping it without sanctions screening at mint/settle time and without transaction monitoring is the single fatal flaw: it is not deployable to any regulated buyer and exposes the operator to MTL/BSA liability the moment real value moves.

Budget enforcement is not concurrency-safe and not shared across worktrees. chio-metering BudgetEnforcer is an in-memory struct (total_spent: u64, &mut self, no Arc/Mutex/atomic/persistence - budget.rs:79-96, 168). Saturating arithmetic prevents overflow but not double-spend: Orca's defining feature is fanning one prompt across N parallel agent processes, and the brainstorm sells 'Fan-Out Wallet Race: One Budget, Five Agents, Atomic' - but nothing in the inspected enforcer provides the atomic shared-balance reservation that claim requires. Two worktrees checking the same pool concurrently both pass. Unless a single authoritative reservation service (the chio-api-protect sidecar mint/release endpoints) is the ONLY path to spend and per-process enforcers are advisory, the 'physically cannot overspend' promise is false in exactly the topology the product runs in.

Approval is opt-in at the type level, not structurally mandatory. chio-kernel runtime.rs carries approval_token: Option<GovernedApprovalToken> (runtime.rs:68). A None on a governed/paid intent is a mandate-bypass unless the dispatch path rejects it fail-closed. With an untrusted LLM authoring tool-call requests and a prompt-injection adversary, any code path that treats missing-approval as proceed-without-approval defeats the entire gate. This must be inverted: governed intents with no valid approval token deny by construction.

Two-transport bridge (Fork-mechanics lens) splits the trust boundary in a way that invites enforcement-bypass. Hot-path verification via koffi/FFI in Electron main PLUS stateful settlement via the axum sidecar means there are two code paths to 'allow'. If the FFI path is used for the agent-hooks allow/deny gate but the sidecar holds the authoritative budget/approval state, a stale or spoofable FFI verdict can authorize a call the sidecar would have denied. The brainstorm even flags that chio-api-protect has advisory routes (/v1/evaluate/advisory sets authorization:false); mis-wiring an advisory verdict as enforcement is a documented foot-gun and silently turns the kill switch into telemetry.
must_haves: Single authoritative spend ledger with atomic reserve-then-charge. There must be exactly ONE process (the chio-api-protect sidecar capability mint/release) that holds funds-reserved state, and every paid tool call MUST obtain a scoped CapabilityToken via an atomic reservation before execution. Per-worktree/per-process BudgetEnforcer instances are advisory caches only. Without this, fan-out double-spend defeats every budget claim. The WorkflowBudgetPool preflight (chio-workflow-preflight) validates allocation but is not a runtime reservation - it must be backed by atomic mint at call time.

Fail-closed-by-construction approval: governed/over-threshold intents with no valid ApprovalToken DENY, never proceed. The Option<GovernedApprovalToken> in runtime.rs must resolve to a hard reject for any intent above the autonomy/amount threshold. Pair with execution_nonce binding (already shipped) so an approval for call A cannot authorize call B.

Sanctions/Travel-Rule screening as a kernel guard at mint AND settle, fail-closed. Before any CapabilityToken that authorizes payment is minted and before chio-settle emits a settlement instruction, the counterparty did:chio (and its KYA-bound legal entity, once that actually exists) must clear a sanctions/denied-party check. This crate does not exist today and is non-negotiable before any real-value rail ships. Fail-closed: unscreened or unreachable-screening-oracle denies.

Hardware-bound, non-exportable approver keys with a server that cannot forge approvals. The chio-custody-hw App Attest / passkey path (verify_app_attest, pinned APPLE_APP_ATTEST_ROOT_SHA256, counter enforcement) must be the ONLY source of the trusted_approvers key material for high-value tiers, and the Orca server/desktop/CI must never hold approver signing material. This is the strongest control already shipped - it must be mandatory, not optional, above a spend threshold.

Compromised-seller billing fraud containment: cost claims must be bounded by the signed manifest price and the buyer's max_cost_per_invocation cap, charged only against a co-signed/attested delivery, with metered cost dimensions independently checkable. A malicious tool server must not be able to bill arbitrary amounts; the capability token's max_cost_per_invocation / max_total_cost (open-market bidding) must be the hard ceiling the kernel enforces regardless of what the seller's receipt claims, and overcharge attempts must slash the seller's bond via a receipt-bound OpenMarketEvidenceReference (penalty.rs:79).

Revocation freshness must gate spend fail-closed. chio-revocation-oracle ships verify_fresh_epoch_root with max_staleness_ms (freshness.rs:38) and non-inclusion proofs (sparse_merkle.rs:77). A paid call whose capability/counterparty revocation status is staler than the configured ceiling MUST deny, and a phone denial must atomically poison the capability (Deny-and-revoke idea) so a prompt-injected agent cannot retry.

Defense against injected purchase intents: the human-ratified parameter_hash must be over the FULL economic envelope (amount, counterparty, currency, resource), so an agent cannot get approval for a benign-looking call and substitute a malicious payee. The mandate-gated checkout passport (commerce-order) is the right shape; the approval digest must cover payee + amount + currency, not just a tool name.
strongest_ideas: Secure-Enclave approver key (Mobile lens) and Approve-The-Spend-With-Your-Thumb (Demo lens): survives best. chio-custody-hw genuinely ships App Attest / Play Integrity / passkey verification with pinned roots and counter enforcement, and the kernel's trusted_approvers + parameter_hash binding makes 'the server literally cannot forge an approval' a true statement, not marketing. This is the most defensible security feature in the entire brainstorm.

Deny-and-revoke: one decline signs a denial AND poisons the capability (Mobile lens). Couples the human NO to chio-revocation-oracle epoch-anchored non-inclusion proofs (verify_non_inclusion shipped). Directly closes the prompt-injection retry loop, which is the core abuse vector for spend authority. High security value.

The $47K Runaway, Stopped Mid-Keystroke (Demo lens) - but ONLY if re-scoped to the single authoritative reservation service. The CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy (kill_switch, deny_if_outstanding_delinquency default true - capital_and_execution.rs:688-709) and the fail-closed deny are real. As a single-agent demo it is honest; as a fleet claim it needs the shared ledger fix.

Bonded Seller Market with receipt-bound slashing (Competitive / Contrarian lenses). open-market penalty.rs binds slashing to OpenMarketEvidenceReference (evidence_refs, penalty.rs:79) and bidding is provably fail-closed on revoked/stale/scope-widening listings. This is the right containment for the compromised/fraudulent-seller threat IF cost is capped by the buyer's token, not the seller's claim.

Two Kernels One Truth: cross-org co-signed receipt (Demo lens) and Know-Your-Buyer attestation (Competitive lens). chio-federation DualSignedReceipt strict pinned-peer verification plus chio-attest-buyer offline replay give non-repudiation that survives audit - strong for the fraud-dispute and chargeback-defense surface.

Restraint Receipts / custody-refusal (Contrarian lens). The simulation_first_only / external_execution_authoritative=false / custody_neutral defaults are real in capital_and_execution.rs (594-605, 255-266). Staying non-custodial is the single best way to shrink the regulatory blast radius - but it does NOT remove the sanctions-screening obligation for the marketplace and settlement-instruction surface.

top_risks.risk: Money laundering / sanctions evasion via the agent marketplace and cross-currency settlement. No AML, sanctions, Travel-Rule, or legal-entity-KYC code exists in the repo; the 'KYA' idea is only an issuer_allowlist reputation tier. Bonds, multi-party USDC revenue-splits to mirrors/referrers, and oracle FX settlement form a layering venue with no denied-party screening.
top_risks.mitigation: Build a sanctions/Travel-Rule guard crate that screens both counterparties' did:chio (and a real KYA-bound legal entity) at capability mint AND at chio-settle instruction emission, fail-closed on unscreened/unreachable. Add a genuine legal-entity-binding credential issued by a licensed KYC provider pinned via chio-attest-verify. Cap and monitor settlement velocity. Do not ship any real-value rail (even testnet-to-mainnet promotion) until this exists.

top_risks.risk: Fan-out double-spend: parallel worktrees each hold an in-memory BudgetEnforcer with no shared atomic ledger, so concurrent checks against one pool all pass. Directly contradicts the 'atomic' fan-out wallet claim and the runaway-agent kill-switch promise in Orca's signature topology.
top_risks.mitigation: Make the chio-api-protect sidecar the sole holder of funds-reserved state; require an atomic reserve-then-mint of a scoped CapabilityToken before any paid call; treat per-process enforcers as advisory caches that cannot authorize spend. Add a concurrency/property test that spawns N workers against one pool and asserts total charged <= pool.

top_risks.risk: Mandate bypass via optional approval token: runtime.rs approval_token is Option<..>, so any dispatch path that treats None as 'proceed' lets a prompt-injected agent skip human ratification for a governed/high-value buy.
top_risks.mitigation: Invert to fail-closed: governed intents above the autonomy/amount threshold with no valid ApprovalToken deny by construction. Keep execution_nonce binding so an approval cannot be reused across calls. Add a Kani/property harness asserting no allow path exists for a governed intent lacking a verified, non-consumed, non-expired token.

top_risks.risk: Compromised tool server bills fraudulently (inflated cost dimensions, phantom WarehouseQuery bytes). Metering trusts seller-reported cost; the brainstorm's 'true-cost meter' reads dimensions the seller controls.
top_risks.mitigation: Enforce the buyer's max_cost_per_invocation / max_total_cost from the open-market CapabilityToken as the hard kernel ceiling regardless of the seller's receipt claim; charge only against an attested/co-signed delivery; auto-slash the seller's posted bond via receipt-bound OpenMarketEvidenceReference on overcharge; rank down on advertised-vs-measured SLA divergence.

top_risks.risk: Two-transport (FFI hot-path + sidecar state) enforcement skew and advisory-as-enforcement mis-wiring. A stale/spoofed FFI verdict, or accidentally treating chio-api-protect's /v1/evaluate/advisory (authorization:false) as a gate, silently disables enforcement.
top_risks.mitigation: The authoritative allow/deny for spend MUST come from the sidecar production routes (/chio/evaluate, /v1/capabilities/*), never the advisory route and never an FFI cache, for any paid call. Assert chio_ffi_abi_version() at startup (fail-closed on mismatch) and forbid the FFI path from returning a spend-authorizing allow. Add an integration test that points the hot path at the advisory route and asserts the call is refused.

top_risks.risk: Approver key theft / device loss = unbounded standing-allowance spend. BatchApproval / standing-allowance cards pre-authorize a class of spend; a stolen unlocked device or exfiltrated key drains the allowance.
top_risks.mitigation: Bind approver keys to the secure element (non-exportable, biometric-gated - already supported by chio-custody-hw passkey path), keep allowances time-boxed with low per-call and total caps and one-tap revoke (BatchApprovalStore.revoke is shipped), require fresh biometric for high tiers (no silent reuse), and tie device-integrity counter regression (App Attest counter check) to automatic allowance freeze.

top_risks.risk: Replay / nonce-substitution across unrelated tool calls. Reusing a payment authorization or approval for a different call.
top_risks.mitigation: Already mitigated in shipped code: execution_nonce.rs binds (subject, capability, server, tool, parameter_hash) and rejects substitution (line 416-418); approval token consumption is tracked (is_consumed). Keep these mandatory and add the EIP-3009 authorization nonce to the same binding so an x402 transfer-with-authorization cannot be replayed.

critiques.dimension: Market demand & timing: Is there real demand NOW for autonomous agent commerce, who pays this year for what, and is the TAM real or narrative?
critiques.verdict: The honest answer is mixed and asymmetric. Autonomous agent-to-agent commerce as a transacting economy is premature for 2026: there is almost no live volume of agents paying agents over x402/ACP/AP2, so any "take-rate on the agent economy" business model is a narrative with a near-zero base today and is the weakest part of this plan. But one slice of the demand is real and acute RIGHT NOW: the runaway-spend / prove-what-we-billed pain for teams running parallel CLI-agent fleets, where Orca already has product-market signal and Chio uniquely offers out-of-agent, fail-closed enforcement plus signed receipts. The defensible move is to sell the brake and the audit trail (control/compliance) into a market that is buying control THIS year, and treat the marketplace/settlement/take-rate layer as a 2027+ option you are positioned for but do not underwrite the company on. Crucially, the code's own custody-neutral, simulation-first posture (verified: external_execution_authoritative=false, automatic_capital_execution_supported=false) means Chio is not a payments company and should not be priced as one; its TAM is governance/observability/compliance for agent spend, which is real and growing, not the larger payments-rail TAM the bold bets imply.
fatal_flaws: 'Settlement take-rate as the core revenue engine' (Business-model lens) is timing-fatal: agent-to-agent on-chain settlement volume in 2026 is negligible, so 30-50bps of ~nothing is ~nothing. Worse, the code is structurally non-custodial and simulation-first (verified in crates/economy/chio-credit/src/credit/capital_and_execution.rs: external_execution_authoritative=false, custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true). You cannot charge a settlement take-rate on flows you deliberately never touch; a licensed rail executes and captures that economics. This revenue thesis contradicts the product's own architecture.

The 'real money rail today' claim that underpins the killer demo and several settlement ideas is overstated for paying customers. Verified: crates/economy/chio-settle/src/lib.rs is `#![cfg(feature = "web3")]` and the whole crate is gated behind that flag; it prepares EVM escrow/EIP-3009 dispatches on testnet. That is real engineering and a great demo, but 'agents settling in USDC on-chain' is not a workflow enterprises will run with production money in 2026, so it does not generate this-year revenue even though it generates this-year wow.

Demand timing for the two-sided marketplace ideas (Bazaar with bonds, list-to-sell wizard, federated registries, revenue-share, bonded contractor reputation) is wrong by 12-24 months. These require liquidity on BOTH sides (sellers wrapping tools AND agents autonomously buying them) that does not exist yet. A bonded, slashable, federated tool exchange is a 2027+ artifact; shipping it in 2026 means building supply and demand from zero simultaneously, the classic marketplace cold-start, with no evidence either side is ready to transact unattended.

The TAM framing across the bold bets conflates two very different markets: (a) the large agentic-payments TAM owned by Visa/Mastercard/Stripe/Coinbase/Google, and (b) the much smaller but real agent-governance/audit TAM. Chio can credibly win (b) now; the bets repeatedly imply (a). Pricing, fundraising, or positioning against the payments TAM is a narrative the product cannot deliver this year and invites direct collision with incumbents who own the rails.

Product-readiness gap is itself a timing flaw: verified that the Orca fork does not exist in-repo (no chio-orca crate, no src/main/ipc/commerce.ts, the 169 TS files are the existing Chio dashboard + demo harness, not a forked cockpit). Even the demand that IS real this year (kill-switch + receipts for agencies) cannot be captured until the fork+bridge ships. The window where 'audit your agent spend' is a novel wedge is finite; competitors and the incumbents' own dashboards are moving.
must_haves: Lead with control/compliance, NOT commerce. The thing a customer will pay for in 2026 is 'my parallel agents provably cannot overspend client money, and I can hand the client a signed receipt.' That is a budget-line a 5-50 person AI dev shop approves this quarter. Sell the kill-switch (chio-metering BudgetEnforcer + chio-credit CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy) and the signed per-run IOU/receipt (chio-credit IouEnvelope) as the wedge; everything else is expansion.

Price as governance/observability software (seat + usage + enterprise compliance license), explicitly NOT as a payments take-rate. The unit economics must not depend on agent-to-agent settlement volume materializing. Any revenue model that needs that volume to exist in 2026 should be cut from the near-term plan and parked as optionality.

Find and cite live evidence of the specific pain before scaling spend, beyond the much-repeated '$47k runaway agent' anecdote. One viral incident is a hook, not a market. The must-have is named design partners (2-3 agencies running fleets on client money) who will pay for the budget pool + receipt today; if they will not, the 'now' thesis is unproven regardless of how good the Rust is.

Keep the on-chain/USDC story as a demo and a 2027 option, not a 2026 revenue dependency. Be explicit (internally and to investors) that the web3 path is testnet-staged and feature-gated, and that the custody-neutral posture is a deliberate moat AND a deliberate ceiling on near-term payments revenue. Honesty here prevents a fatal mispricing of the round and the roadmap.

Sequence the marketplace AFTER the control wedge has installed base. The bonded seller market, federation, and agent-to-agent hiring only make sense once there is a population of Chio cockpits with budgeted agents that have somewhere to spend. Demand for the exchange is downstream of demand for the brake; building them in parallel splits a small team against two cold-starts.
strongest_ideas: Wedge: the spend kill-switch for parallel agent fleets (GTM lens) and 'The $47K Runaway, Stopped Mid-Keystroke' (killer-demo lens). This is the ONLY idea family whose demand is unambiguously present in 2026. Verified primitives exist and are tested (chio-metering/src/budget.rs BudgetEnforcer, budget_hierarchy.rs, chio-credit kill_switch). It maps to a budget a real buyer (AI dev agency on client money) approves now, and it is the one thing incumbents' dashboards structurally cannot do because enforcement lives outside agent code.

The per-prompt budget pool for fan-out (GTM lens, 'smallest valuable unit'). Verified real and tested (crates/platform/chio-workflow-preflight, workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded validation). It is the cleanest fusion to Orca's signature fan-out UX, low difficulty, and sells the control story with zero dependence on any payment rail or marketplace liquidity. This is the right beachhead SKU for this year.

One-click regulator evidence package / Per-worktree Session Compliance Certificate / signed audit export (Compliance lens). The CFO/CISO compliance buyer is the one enterprise segment with budget allocated NOW for AI governance (EU AI Act enforcement timelines, PCI-DSS, ISO 42001). The differentiator (offline-verifiable, Merkle-proven, per-clause control map) is real and pre-built in chio-enterprise-export and docs/compliance/*. This is the expansion revenue that does not require autonomous commerce to be real.

Restraint Receipts / 'sell the NO' (Contrarian lens). Strategically the sharpest read of timing: the market is buying control and proof, not speed. An artifact proving the agent did LESS than authorized is exactly what risk committees and insurers will pay for in a year defined by agent-safety anxiety, and it sidesteps the premature 'agents transacting' thesis entirely. It reframes the whole product around demand that exists today.

Mandate-gated checkout passport / Rail-Neutral Receipt as a VERIFIER (Buyer-agent and Competitive lenses), but scoped to human-in-the-loop procurement, not autonomous buying. Demand for 'a human ratifies an attested agent purchase in the same review pane as code' is plausibly real for early adopters this year precisely because it does NOT require trusting agents to buy unattended. As a verifier across ACP/AP2/x402 it also avoids competing with rails that have the volume.

top_risks.risk: Building the company's revenue thesis on settlement take-rate / agent-to-agent commerce volume that will not materialize in 2026, when the product is architecturally non-custodial and cannot capture that economics anyway. This is a timing-and-architecture double miss that could define the round and roadmap around a market that isn't there yet.
top_risks.mitigation: Reframe the business as agent-spend governance + compliance software priced on seats/usage/enterprise license. Treat the take-rate and marketplace as 2027+ optionality you are uniquely positioned for, and never let near-term unit economics depend on agent-to-agent settlement volume. Say this explicitly in the plan and the pitch.

top_risks.risk: Premature autonomy: the deepest ideas assume agents will be trusted to BUY, HIRE, and SETTLE unattended in 2026. Enterprises are nowhere near granting that; the actual 2026 posture is human-ratified, tightly-budgeted, mostly-blocked agent spend. Demand for 'full autonomous commerce' is a 2027-2028 curve, not a 2026 one.
top_risks.mitigation: Ship Shadow/Advisory and human-in-the-loop modes (chio-autonomy review states, phone-tap mandate) as the default and the product story; position 'Active/Autonomous' as an aspirational, bond-gated tier that almost no one turns on yet. Sell the dial as a way to keep agents conservative, which is what buyers want now.

top_risks.risk: The acute pain (runaway spend, prove-what-we-billed) is real but the addressable buyer pool that feels it strongly enough to pay THIS year may be narrow (AI dev agencies running large parallel CLI fleets on client money). If that segment is smaller or less willing-to-pay than assumed, the 'now' thesis weakens even though the tech is right.
top_risks.mitigation: Validate with 2-3 paying design partners before scaling. Make the beachhead SKU (budget pool + signed receipts) cheap and self-serve so the narrow ICP can adopt by word of mouth, and instrument whether they actually flip on enforcement and export receipts to clients.

top_risks.risk: Window risk / capture lag: the audit-and-enforcement wedge is novel now, but the fork+bridge does not exist yet (verified: no chio-orca crate, no commerce IPC). Time-to-shippable-product eats into the window where this is differentiated before incumbents' dashboards and other agent runners add spend caps.
top_risks.mitigation: Exploit the verified low-build path (chio-api-protect sidecar + existing React dashboard port + thin commerce.ts IPC) to get the control wedge shipped fast, and resist scope creep into the marketplace/settlement layers that lengthen time-to-market without serving 2026 demand.

top_risks.risk: TAM is real but smaller than the bold bets imply, and adjacent to incumbents. Agent-governance/audit is a credible, growing market; the agentic-payments TAM the bets gesture at is owned by players with the rails and the volume. Mispositioning into the larger TAM invites a fight Chio loses and undersells the fight it can win.
top_risks.mitigation: Position explicitly as the neutral verifier/enforcer ABOVE every rail (the one thing single-rail incumbents structurally will not build), price into the governance/compliance budget, and let the payments TAM be someone else's to own while Chio takes the toll-free audit layer.

critiques.dimension: Moat & competitive threat (can Stripe / Coinbase / Visa / Mastercard / Google / an agent-IDE incumbent crush this by shipping the same thing, and what is genuinely defensible vs a one-quarter bolt-on)
critiques.verdict: The Rust substrate is real and genuinely hard to build (I verified: kill_switch + custody-neutral + simulation-first posture in capital_and_execution.rs, loopback-only settlement RPC enforcing that Chio never broadcasts or custodies, three separate rail artifacts x402/ap2/acp projected into one evidence graph, real Azure-MAA JWT runtime attestation gating bonded autonomy, and a 147-test federation/gossip layer). But "hard to build" is not the same as "defensible," and the brainstorm repeatedly conflates the two. The honest moat is NOT the receipt format, the kill switch, the wallet, the marketplace, or any single artifact (every one of those is a feature an incumbent bolts on in a quarter, and several are being shipped right now). The only durable moat is the COMBINATION of (a) architectural neutrality (an out-of-agent kernel that verifies rivals' rails and whose value grows with every rail it does NOT own) plus (b) a multi-operator federation mesh of signed registries with cross-operator trust gossip that no single-rail vendor can fake because they have no swarm. Everything else is a wedge, not a wall. The fatal exposure is that this moat is a two-sided-network and standards-adoption bet, and Stripe / Visa / Google sit on exactly the distribution, merchant relationships, and standards authorship (AP2, ACP, x402 itself is Coinbase's) needed to win that bet first. Chio can be technically right and still lose the moat if the rails it wants to neutrally verify simply embed their own attested-receipt + budget-cap primitives and never give Chio a reason to sit above them.
fatal_flaws: The neutrality moat assumes the rails WANT a neutral verifier sitting above them, but they have the opposite incentive and the distribution to deny it. x402 is Coinbase's spec; AP2 is Google's; ACP is OpenAI/Stripe's. Each is racing to make its OWN rail the place attestation and receipts live. They do not need to copy Chio's cross-rail verifier; they need only ship a good-enough single-rail receipt + budget cap (Stripe already issues spend controls and signed events; Visa/MC Agentic Tokens already bind agent-to-principal) so that 90% of buyers never feel the pain Chio solves. A neutral verifier with no transaction volume to verify has no moat. The moat is contingent on the very incumbents it claims to be defensible against choosing to interoperate, which is a market-structure bet, not a technical one.

The single most-repeated demo claim across the brainstorm ('chio-settle already executes live USDC escrow lock/release and EIP-3009 today, real money rail not a mock') is materially overstated by the code: settlement RPC is hard-gated to loopback-only (config.rs rejects any non-loopback RPC URL), and every EVM entrypoint is prepare_*/build_* (prepare_web3_escrow_dispatch, prepare_dual_sign_release, prepare_escrow_refund), i.e. sign-an-instruction, never broadcast. The custody-neutral / simulation_first_only / external_execution_authoritative=false posture is real and is the right legal stance, but it means Chio is an instruction-and-proof layer that still requires a licensed rail to actually move money. The 30-second on-chain demo therefore needs a real broadcast path + funded testnet wiring that does not exist in-tree yet, and the moat narrative quietly depends on a money-movement capability the product deliberately does NOT have. An incumbent that DOES custody (Coinbase, Stripe) can ship the same escrow UX end-to-end without that gap.

chio-commerce-order, the load-bearing 'neutral verifier across all three standards' that nearly every lens leans on as the differentiator, has only ~8 test functions and the AP2/ACP binding is three hard-coded hash fields (ap2_checkout_mandate_hash, ap2_payment_mandate_hash, acp_delegated_payment_token_hash) in a fixed state machine. Binding three opaque hashes into a ledger is genuinely useful but is NOT deep IP: a competent incumbent team replicates 'we hash your AP2 mandate and ACP token into our receipt' in a quarter. The depth is in federation/credit/reputation, not in the cross-rail binding that the GTM actually sells as the wedge. The defensible part and the marketed part are different parts.

The MIT-cockpit half of the product (forked Orca) is explicitly copyable by anyone, including the incumbents, and the brainstorm admits it ('the defensible asset is not the forked Electron app'). So the moat must live ENTIRELY in the Rust protocol, yet the protocol is open-source in this repo too. If the crates are MIT/Apache, a well-funded incumbent forks the protocol AND the cockpit and ships it with their distribution and their rail pre-integrated. The only thing that is not forkable is the live federation mesh and the accumulated kernel-signed reputation history, which is precisely the cold-start asset Chio does not yet have. The moat is real but it is 100% in the future-network, 0% in present code.
must_haves: Pick the ONE thing incumbents structurally cannot do and build the whole moat narrative on it: out-of-agent enforcement + cross-rail neutrality. A rail (Stripe/Coinbase/Visa) cannot credibly verify a rival rail without conceding it is not the universal rail, and cannot put the kill switch OUTSIDE agent code because their SDK runs INSIDE agent code. This is the one genuinely architectural, incentive-incompatible-for-incumbents position. Everything in the pitch that is not downstream of this (wallets, dashboards, marketplaces, receipt branding) should be demoted to table-stakes, not sold as moat.

Make the federation mesh a Day-1 asset, not a someday feature. The ONLY uncopyable thing is a multi-operator network of signed registries with cross-operator trust gossip plus accumulated kernel-signed reputation that a fork cannot mint (you cannot fork other people's receipts). The verified chio-federation depth (147 tests, open-admission stake gating, pheromone + revocation gossip) is the real crown jewel, far more than the receipt format. If the product ships as a single-operator app, the moat is zero and an incumbent out-distributes it. The go-to-market MUST seed independent operators early or there is no wall.

License the protocol crates defensively (or at minimum the federation/reputation/attestation substrate) and keep the kernel-signing trust root proprietary. If the Rust is permissively licensed and self-hostable, an incumbent forks protocol + cockpit + their rail and the entire moat evaporates. At least the operator-identity / receipt-signing authority and the federation admission must be a service Chio runs, not a binary anyone compiles.

Be ruthlessly honest that this is a standards/neutrality play whose success depends on the rails NOT converging on their own attestation. Hedge that risk by being the FIRST and most complete cross-rail binder while the standards are still fragmented (AP2 vs ACP vs x402 genuinely do not interoperate today, which is the real and time-limited window). The defensibility is a land-grab on neutrality during a fragmentation window, and the plan must treat that window as closing.

Lead with the compliance/audit-export artifact (offline-verifiable, EU AI Act / PCI-DSS clause-mapped, no-running-node verification) as the enterprise moat, because that is the one place 'hard to build' actually equals 'hard to compete against': it is years of compliance engineering an agent-IDE incumbent will not prioritize, it is non-custodial so it sidesteps the money-transmitter bright line, and a payment rail's incentive is to NOT make its logs independently re-verifiable by a third party. This is more defensible than any money-movement feature.
strongest_ideas: Rail-Neutral Receipt / the one verifier across ACP, AP2, and x402 (Competitive-differentiation lens) - this is the single idea whose moat is incentive-incompatible for every incumbent: a single-rail vendor cannot verify rivals' artifacts without conceding neutrality. The architecture is the moat. Caveat: the in-tree binding (3 hashed fields, ~8 tests) is thin and must be deepened before it can carry the weight the GTM puts on it.

Federated registries under stake-gated admission + Public Proof Room (Ecosystem lens) - the only genuinely uncopyable asset is a live multi-operator mesh of signed registries plus kernel-signed reputation a fork cannot mint. Verified as the deepest, most mature part of the codebase (147 federation tests, open_admission stake gating, pheromone + revocation gossip). This is the actual wall; it just is not built into the product surface yet.

The custody-refusal moat / 'Chio never holds your money' as the feature (Contrarian lens) - confirmed structural in code (loopback-only RPC, prepare-only EVM dispatch, simulation_first_only, external_execution_authoritative=false, custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true). This is architectural AND legal: incumbents who took custody to win UX cannot un-take it without dismantling their product. The strongest moat that is true TODAY rather than contingent on a future network.

The kernel-enforced kill switch / out-of-agent spend refusal (multiple lenses) - verified real (kill_switch, maximum_autonomy_tier, deny_if_outstanding_delinquency, require_locked_reserve, minimum_runtime_assurance_tier gated by real Azure-MAA JWT attestation). Defensible specifically because incumbent SDKs run INSIDE agent code and cannot place the brake outside it. This is the sharpest single technical expression of the architectural moat.

One-click offline-verifiable compliance/audit export with per-clause control mapping (Compliance lens) - the one place where 'hard to build' equals 'hard to compete against,' non-custodial, and counter-incentivized for rails (a rail does not want its logs independently re-verifiable). Best enterprise wedge and least copyable by an agent-IDE incumbent who will not invest years in compliance engineering.

top_risks.risk: Incumbents neutralize the wedge without copying it: Stripe ships agent spend controls + signed events, Visa/Mastercard Agentic Tokens bind agent-to-principal, Coinbase x402 + AgentKit add receipts on their own rail. None needs Chio's cross-rail verifier because each makes ITS rail the home of attestation, and their distribution means most buyers never feel the multi-rail pain. The neutral verifier ends up with nothing to verify.
top_risks.mitigation: Win the fragmentation window NOW: be the only complete binder of AP2+ACP+x402 while they genuinely do not interoperate, and anchor in the enterprise/regulated buyer who specifically needs a NEUTRAL third party (not the seller's rail) to attest. Make 'the rail cannot be its own auditor' the explicit positioning. Treat the window as 12-24 months, not permanent.

top_risks.risk: The protocol is permissively licensed and self-hostable, so a well-funded incumbent forks protocol + MIT cockpit + their own rail and out-distributes Chio with the exact same architecture. 'It is the kernel not the app' stops being a moat if the kernel is also free.
top_risks.mitigation: Keep the operator-identity / receipt-signing trust root and federation admission as a Chio-run service, not a freely compilable binary. Accumulate the one thing a fork cannot copy: live cross-operator reputation history and the mesh itself. Without this the moat is purely first-mover.

top_risks.risk: The 'real on-chain settlement today' demo claim is not backed by the code (loopback-only RPC, prepare/sign-only, no broadcast path), so the marquee 'Click-to-Buy settled on-chain in 30 seconds' wow-moment is currently a promise, not shipped. A Coinbase/Stripe demo that actually moves money end-to-end beats it head-to-head and undercuts the 'rests on shipped code' credibility claim.
top_risks.mitigation: Either build the testnet broadcast wiring and fund a relayer so the demo is genuinely real, or reframe the demo honestly around what IS shipped and uniquely defensible: the signed instruction + offline-verifiable receipt + kernel refusal, with money movement explicitly delegated to a licensed rail. Do not claim live custody you do not have.

top_risks.risk: The cross-rail binding that the GTM sells as the core wedge (chio-commerce-order) is shallow in-tree (~8 tests, 3 hard-coded hash fields in a fixed state machine) and is the most copyable part of the stack, while the genuinely deep IP (federation, credit, reputation, attestation) is not what the pitch leads with. Buyers and incumbents will reverse-engineer the marketed wedge in a quarter.
top_risks.mitigation: Lead the moat story with federation + custody-refusal + compliance export (the deep, incentive-incompatible parts) and treat the rail-binding as a feature that gets continuously deepened, not as the wall. Add real conformance tests across all three rail artifact types.

top_risks.risk: An agent-IDE incumbent (Cursor, GitHub/Copilot, the actual Orca upstream, or an OpenAI/Anthropic first-party cockpit) bundles 'good-enough' budget caps + spend dashboards natively and captures the dev-agency ICP on distribution before the commerce/attestation depth matters to that buyer. The agency feels the overspend pain but may accept a non-cryptographic cap.
top_risks.mitigation: Make the cryptographic-receipt + offline-replayable-audit the reason the agency keeps Chio when its clients demand prove-what-we-billed, which a dashboard cap cannot produce. Convert the cheap kill-switch wedge into stickiness via the audit artifact, fast, before incumbents add caps.

critiques.verdict: There is a real, defensible product here, but it is buried under roughly 10x more surface than can be built or sold at once. The disciplined minimum is a single wedge: kernel-enforced spend limits on Orca's fan-out, proven by a signed receipt. I verified the wedge primitives genuinely exist and are tested (WorkflowBudgetPool with workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded validation, BudgetEnforcer, CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy with kill_switch, IouEnvelope via CreditEvaluatorHook), and the bridge to ship it exists (chio-api-protect axum sidecar with the claimed routes, chio-bindings-ffi with pinned ABI v1, a React+Vite dashboard of ~1741 TS files that matches Orca's renderer stack). But the brief systematically overclaims maturity in ways that distort scoping: chio-cli exposes zero commerce verbs today (the crates are linked but unsurfaced), the web3 settlement path is prepare-only and never broadcasts (external_execution_authoritative=false, simulation_first_only=true), and commerce-order is a verifier of an assembled evidence bundle, not a live order engine. The fork itself is unstarted (no chio-orca crate) and the commerce substrate is mid-refactor (commerce_order, transaction_passport, agent_web being extracted out of chio-control-plane in uncommitted changes). Ship the brake, not the marketplace; everything two-sided is a year-two bet that the wedge has not yet earned.
fatal_flaws: Two-sided marketplace ideas (Bazaar, list-to-sell, federated registries, bonded sellers, revenue-share, Proof Room cold-start) are a cold-start trap with no demand and no supply on day one. They are the single largest source of scope creep across the 18 lenses and none survive a focus test: a buyer cockpit has no sellers until it has buyers, and bonds/slashing only matter at transaction volume the product will not have for a year. Cut all of them from v1.

The flagship killer-demo ('Click-To-Buy-The-API, settled on-chain in 30 seconds, provably real because chio-settle already executes the on-chain escrow') is factually wrong against the code. chio-settle is prepare-only: prepare_web3_escrow_dispatch builds a signed instruction and the credit defaults are external_execution_authoritative=false, simulation_first_only=true, custody_neutral_instruction_supported=true. Nothing broadcasts. A live on-chain demo requires writing and operating a broadcast/relayer path plus testnet ops that no lens budgets for. Leading with this demo invites a credibility-destroying 'it does not actually settle' discovery.

The 'live order engine' framing (commerce-order as a state ladder that drives the agent, gating fund release at bind_mandate, live job ladders on desktop and mobile) does not match the code. verify_commerce_order replays an already-assembled CommerceOrderVerificationBundle; is_allowed_transition validates a transcript of events. There is no component that emits events, reserves budget, calls settle, and advances the order in real time. Building that orchestration layer is a large hidden project disguised as 'fuse existing primitives.'

FFI hot-path ideas that put the kill switch or budget refusal in-process via koffi are mis-architected against the actual binary. chio-bindings-ffi exports only verify/sign/hash (chio_verify_capability_json, chio_verify_receipt_json, chio_canonicalize_json, ed25519). It does NOT export budget enforcement, capability minting, or the bonded-execution kill switch. Those are stateful and live only behind the sidecar. Any plan that gates spend on the FFI path will either fail closed on every call or quietly degrade to advisory.
must_haves: One wedge, ruthlessly: the kernel-enforced per-worktree spend cap plus per-prompt fan-out budget pool, with a signed IOU/receipt per run as the proof artifact. This is the only thing that is (a) genuinely differentiated (no MIT agent runner can refuse the next paid call), (b) backed by primitives I verified exist and are tested, and (c) one-to-one with Orca's signature fan-out UX. Everything else must justify itself as a strict expansion of this.

Two-transport bridge discipline, wired correctly: chio-api-protect spawned as the bundled sidecar for all stateful enforcement (budget refusal, minting, approvals) behind one commerce:* IPC namespace; chio-bindings-ffi via koffi used ONLY for stateless verify/hash on the read path, with the JS asserting chio_ffi_abi_version()==1 at startup so a mismatch fails closed. Do not route any spend decision through FFI.

Honesty about custody: adopt the contrarian lens stance as the actual product posture, not a footnote. Chio prepares and proves; it never broadcasts or custodies. The hero artifact is the signed Restraint/Receipt bundle ('the agent was structurally prevented from overspending'), which is true against simulation_first_only=true and needs no money-transmitter exposure. This converts the prepare-only limitation from a weakness into the positioning.

Stabilize the substrate before forking. The commerce crates are mid-extraction out of chio-control-plane (uncommitted deletes of commerce_order, transaction_passport, agent_web, enterprise_export, trust_market). Land that refactor and pin a chio-orca-core contract crate first, or the Electron fork will be wiring against types that move on every rebase.

Surface the commerce verbs in chio-cli before wiring Orca. The CLI today has no settle/market/buy/mandate/capital/credit verb despite linking the crates. Orca's commerce:* IPC and any 'orca commerce' verb shells to chio; if chio has no such command, the fork has nothing to call. Build the minimum chio commerce CLI (budget set, run-with-cap, receipt export) as the contract the cockpit consumes.
strongest_ideas: GTM wedge: 'the runaway-agent kill switch you can audit' for AI-native dev shops billing client money (GTM lens). It names a narrow ICP that feels both pains (overspend + prove-what-we-billed), and every primitive it cites (BudgetEnforcer, BudgetTree, CreditBondedExecutionControlPolicy kill_switch, IouEnvelope) I confirmed exists and is tested. This is the single wedge that earns the right to build the rest.

Smallest valuable unit: the per-prompt budget pool field on fan-out (GTM lens / Fan-Out Wallet Race demo). WorkflowBudgetPool and workflow_preflight_budget_pool_exceeded are real and tested; it maps one-to-one onto Orca's actual differentiator (fan-one-prompt-across-N) and rejects over-allocation before any agent runs. Lowest difficulty, highest strategic fit, fully demoable without any money rail.

Mount the existing chio-cli React dashboard as Orca's Attested Receipts/Budget tabs (Fork mechanics lens). Verified: ~1741 TS files, React+Vite, co-located tests, same stack as Orca's renderer. This is the lowest-risk, highest-leverage build in the entire set because it is a port, not a rewrite, and it gives the wedge its proof surface (the receipt) for almost free.

Ship chio-api-protect as the bundled sidecar behind one commerce:* IPC file (Fork mechanics lens). The sidecar, its routes (/chio/evaluate, /v1/capabilities/*, /approvals/*), and its production-vs-advisory boundary all exist. Reusing it instead of building a server is the correct 'write almost no new Rust' move and is the backbone the wedge rides on.

Restraint Receipts / custody-refusal as positioning (Contrarian lens). This is the only framing fully consistent with the code's prepare-only, simulation_first_only reality, and it turns the biggest factual limitation (Chio does not actually move money) into the defensible story (Chio is the signed brake, not another wallet). It should replace the on-chain-settlement demo as the headline.

top_risks.risk: Boiling the ocean: 18 lenses x ~6 ideas = ~100 features, most requiring different crates, UI surfaces, and a two-sided network. Attempting more than the budget-cap wedge in v1 guarantees a shallow, undifferentiated fork that ships nothing convincingly. The fan-out budget pool + kernel kill switch + receipt dashboard is the disciplined minimum; everything two-sided (marketplace, federation, agent-to-agent escrow, reputation/bonds/slashing) is post-PMF.
top_risks.mitigation: Hard-gate v1 to the single wedge plus its proof surface (budget pool, per-worktree cap, kill switch, ported receipt/budget dashboard). Explicitly defer every marketplace, federation, agent-to-agent, settlement-rail, and identity/KYA idea to a written 'year-two if the wedge lands' list. Treat any feature that needs a counterparty, a live chain broadcast, or a second operator as out of scope by default.

top_risks.risk: Demoing capabilities the code does not have. The web3 'settles on-chain in 30s' demo and the 'live commerce-order engine' are both contradicted by the source (prepare-only settlement; commerce-order is a verifier of an assembled bundle). Leading with either invites a fatal 'it does not actually do that' moment in front of a buyer or investor.
top_risks.mitigation: Lead with the enforcement-and-restraint demo, which is real today: an agent tries to overspend, the kernel refuses the next paid call (CreditBondedExecutionDecision::Deny is a signed artifact), and a Restraint Receipt drops into the ported dashboard. Keep web3 strictly in a clearly-labeled 'prepare instruction + verify proof' mode; never claim live settlement until a broadcast/relayer path is actually built and operated.

top_risks.risk: Forking before the substrate settles. The commerce crates are being extracted out of chio-control-plane in uncommitted changes (commerce_order, transaction_passport, agent_web, enterprise_export, trust_market all show as deleted-and-moved). A fork wired against the old layout will break on the next rebase, and the daily-shipping Orca upstream compounds the merge burden.
top_risks.mitigation: Land and stabilize the crate-extraction refactor first, then freeze a chio-orca-core contract crate that the Electron fork imports. Pin schema IDs and ABI versions. Do not begin the rebrand/glue work until the chio commerce CLI surface and the *-core types are committed and conformance-checked.

top_risks.risk: Mis-wiring advisory telemetry as enforcement. The sidecar deliberately separates real allow/deny gates from advisory/observability routes (/v1/evaluate/advisory sets chio-trust-level: advisory, authorization:false), and the FFI surface is verify-only. A naive integration that reads an advisory response or an FFI verify as 'spend approved' would silently defeat the entire kill-switch value proposition.
top_risks.mitigation: Route every spend decision through the sidecar's production boundary (/chio/evaluate, /v1/capabilities/*) on the agent-hooks bus as a synchronous allow/deny; treat advisory routes and all FFI calls as read-only and never as authorization. Add an integration test that asserts an over-budget call is refused by the sidecar before money moves, and that an advisory response cannot release a paid call.

top_risks.risk: Mobile Secure-Enclave and KYA/legal-entity ideas are deep multi-quarter efforts (App Attest / Play Integrity binding, UniFFI Swift+Kotlin, a licensed KYC issuer pinned via chio-attest-verify) that several lenses casually slot into v1. They are real moats but enormous scope, and the KYA issuer does not exist in-repo (it is named as the one missing piece).
top_risks.mitigation: Defer all hardware-backed mobile signing and KYA legal-entity binding to a later phase. For v1, the mobile companion does at most a notify-and-approve over the existing pairing channel feeding the sidecar's /approvals; do not promise Secure-Enclave-rooted authority or KYC-bound identity until there is a buyer pulling for it.
